Born in Petrograd to the family of Jaan Kaljo, a metal factory worker, and Minna Kaljo (née Lahman). In 1917–1918 the family moved to Estonia, to Tartu. R. Kaljo studied at the primary school of Tartu Teachers' Seminary, and in 1928–1933 at H. Treffner's private boys' gymnasium, where his drawing teachers were Eduard Ole and Agu Peerna. In 1933–1935 he did his military service in the navy of the Republic of Estonia as a second-class sailor in the Peipsi fleet division. In 1935 he worked as an apprentice typesetter at the Tartu publishing cooperative Loodus. In 1935–1936 he studied at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of the University of Tartu, and in 1936–1940 at the Higher Art School Pallas. He initially experimented with sculpture and painting studies in the studios of Anton Starkopf and Aleksander Vardi, but his final choice became graphic art in Arkadio Laigo's studio; Roman Vaher was also one of his teachers. He took part in exhibitions of Pallas students' works, and submitted, among other things, the woodcut "Tänavasillutajad" ("Street Pavers") (1940) to the exhibition of graduation works. In 1937 his first woodcut "Puu" ("Tree") was made; the woodcut subsequently became Kaljo's main technique, in which he created figure compositions, portraits, cityscapes and nudes. Already in his early works an interest in colourful human types and expressive scenes was evident; in the expressive, at times grotesque, manner of depicting the human figure the influence of Arkadio Laigo's and Eduard Wiiralt's work could be seen.

In 1938 Kaljo's first drypoint, "Akordionimängija" ("Accordion Player"), was exhibited in Tallinn, marking the beginning of his participation in professional artists' exhibitions. R. Kaljo took part in exhibitions organised by the Board of the Fine Art Foundation, and, during the Soviet period, in selective exhibitions of Estonian graphic art and all-union group exhibitions. According to Paul Ambur's periodisation, 1939–1948 was the first period of his ex-libris work: the first ex-libris was made for Leo Martin.

At the first competition of design sketches organised by the Board of the Fine Art Foundation in 1940, Kaljo shared three first prizes with Eduard Järv and Paul Liivak, and at the second competition he won the first prize with the design for the woodcut "Poliitiliste vangide vabastamine 1940. aasta 22. juunil" ("The Liberation of Political Prisoners on 22 June 1940").

In 1940–1941 he was a freelance graphic artist in Tartu. The works of this period reflected, both directly and indirectly, the contemporary events of the artist's time — the June coup of 1940, the Second World War. The expressive manner was gradually replaced by an austere, objectivity-seeking approach. In 1941 he began working as a book illustrator, creating cover images for publications of the publishing house Ilukirjandus ja Kunst.

During the Second World War, Richard Kaljo's home at Roosi tn 4, together with his studio, burned down; along with other property, his book and ex-libris

The sculptor Georgi Markelov (19.05.1929 – 15.01.2014) was born in Narva as the son of a construction entrepreneur and studied at Narva Primary School No. 6 from 1937 to 1943. Georgi Markelov's paternal home was also destroyed in wartime air raids. His father was deported to Siberia at the beginning of the Soviet occupation.

After post-war studies at Väike-Maarja Secondary School, he entered the Estonian State Art Institute in 1950, graduating in 1956 in the field of sculpture. From that same year Markelov worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn; in 1959 he was accepted as a member of the Artists' Union, and in 1979 he was awarded the honorary title of Meritorious Artist by the government of the time.

Georgi Markelov cultivated portrait sculpture in a realistic style, but he also created a series of 14 wood sculptures titled "Ei iialgi enam sõda" ("Never Again War"), several examples of which are held in the sculpture collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. In the 1970s–1980s he carved over-life-size portraits of V. I. Lenin from oak, most of which were acquired by state institutions. In turbulent times, some of these portrait examples also ended up in museum storage. The older generation of artists and art enthusiasts probably remember precisely these masterfully carved heads from the exhibitions of the Tallinn Art Hall's survey shows of the time. In 1975 the artist received the Kristjan Raud Prize for one such portrait. As a masterful carver, he also loved to create more lyrical small sculptures, flowers and birds, and wooden masks. In the summer of 2010 Markelov surprised both colleagues and the art audience with a solo exhibition at the gallery of the Monumental Art House on Raja Street. He presented an installation filling the entire gallery space, "Lilled emale" ("Flowers for Mother"), where the floor was covered with more than 6000 virtuosically carved flower blossoms of various kinds, made of mahogany, oak, ash, linden, etc. It was, as it were, a unique summation of the activity and standpoint of a sculptor — and of a person who had lived through various eras — regarding his place in today's world.
2e313e823b05f4322b3453d1b0732f90febc7a11:
Maie Raitar was employed at the Tartu State Art Museum from 1966, already as a student, finishing in 1988 as scientific director. She became an indispensable worker as an editor and proofreader of the museum's publications, but she also began writing about art.

In 1988 Maie Raitar was one of the most active and knowledgeable people involved in the restoration of the Pallas art society and the establishment of its painting studio. Her contribution was effective in the realisation of the first large exhibition of Aleksander Vardi's abstractions (1991) and the survey exhibition of Valve Janov's work (1992).

Over the years Maie Raitar became the foremost connoisseur of the life and work of Konrad Mägi, the main awakener of our contemporary painting. In 1998 she compiled an extensive survey exhibition of Mägi's work at the Tartu Art Museum. In cooperation with Andres Sööt, the remarkable documentary film "Konrad Mägi" (2001) was made. Together with Andres Sööt, an album on Konrad Mägi's life and work was also produced, whose publication one would still hope for this year. A number of Mägi's works, previously thought lost, as well as important archival data, came to light. A new monograph on Konrad Mägi was in the works. Maie Raitar's like-minded collaboration with Andres Sööt had, however, already begun with the film "Tartu kunstnikud" ("Tartu Artists"), completed in 1989, which is full of footage that is now already very rare.

In 2002 began Maie Raitar's intensive and fruitful cooperation, as an editor of broad outlook and stylistic sensitivity, with the publishing house Varrak. This resulted in about ten voluminous and complex history books, as well as Juri Lotman's "Filmisemiootika ja filmiesteetika probleemid" ("Problems of Film Semiotics and Film Aesthetics") (translated by Elen Lotman, 2004), which she herself had proposed. The final proofreading of two edited books, Frederick Forsyth's "The Afghan" and Niall Ferguson's "The War of the World: Twentieth-Century Conflict and the Descent of the West", remained unread. Maie Raitar translated for Varrak Ian Dunlop's "Louis XIV" (together with Erki Sinijärv, 2003) and Tamara Miljutina's memoirs "Inimesed minu elus" ("People in My Life") (2007).
b28de6b2ebe1336a08d5160e2701785a0b958cce: Eduard Wiiralt was born on 20 March 1898 in Saint Petersburg Governorate, the son of Sophie-Elisabeth Asur, a maid at the Robidets manor, and Anton Wiralt, a manor employee. In 1909 the family moved to live near Varangu manor in Järvamaa. E. Wiiralt studied at the Koeru Education Society school and at the Koeru German private school. In the autumn of 1915 he entered the Tallinn City School of Applied Art. In 1918 E. Wiiralt took part in the Estonian War of Independence. In 1919 he appeared for the first time in Tallinn with four graphic works at a survey exhibition of Estonian art held at the premises of the Girls' Commercial School. In the autumn of 1919 Wiiralt entered the newly opened Pallas art school in Tartu, from where, in the spring of 1922, he went to the Dresden Academy of Fine Arts for further training. In the autumn of 1923 the artist returned to his homeland and, in the spring of the following year, graduated from the Pallas school. In the autumn of 1924 Wiiralt began working as head of the Pallas graphic art studio, while also being active as a book graphic artist. In the spring of 1925 Wiiralt received a scholarship from the Board of the Fine Arts Foundation for a trip to Paris, where he arrived in the autumn of that year and stayed to live. In the autumn of 1936, while the artist was abroad, his first solo exhibition in Estonia took place at the Tallinn Art Hall, organised by Alfred Rõude, with more than 300 works exhibited. In the summer of 1938 Wiiralt travelled from France to Morocco. In the autumn of 1939, before World War II, the artist returned to Estonia via Paris, where he stayed until 1944. Having briefly stayed in Vienna and Stockholm and travelled in Lapland, Wiiralt spent the last decade of his life again working in Paris, where he died on 8 January 1954 and was buried in the Père-Lachaise Cemetery in Paris.
f272bf0dc80c2a3eb632cf05dad4202c76b0febe: Osvald Timmas was born 17.09.1913 in Saaremaa, Kärla parish, Pai village, died 27.10.2005 in Toronto, Canada. He studied in the humanities branch of Saaremaa Joint Gymnasium and at the Tondi Military School in Tallinn, which he graduated from in 1934. He then studied at the school of the Estonian Consumer Cooperatives' Central Union (ETK) Cooperative Union and in 1937–1944 at the Faculty of Economics of the University of Tartu. He was a member of the fraternity Rotalia. In art, he took private lessons in 1939–1942 from Nikolai Kummits and in 1942–1944 from Günther Reindorff. In 1944 he fled together with his wife Erika to Sweden, where he worked in the life insurance field. In 1947–1949 he studied on illustration courses in Stockholm. In 1951 he moved to Toronto, Canada, where he also worked in life insurance. In 1956 he received Canadian citizenship. In the 1960s Timmas attracted attention with watercolours depicting geological layers of the earth's surface and the underwater world, as well as views seen through a microscope. In 1972 he devoted himself entirely to art. In 1961–1968 Timmas was president of the Colour and Form Society and in 1971–1975 vice-president of the Ontario Society of Artists. Timmas was also a founding member of the Estonian Arts Centre in Ontario in 1974. In 1973 O. Timmas was elected a member of the Royal Canadian Academy of Arts. In 1977 he received a decoration from the British Queen. In 2005 O. Timmas was awarded the Order of the White Star, 5th Class, of the Republic of Estonia. In his will he established the Erika and Osvald Timmas Memorial Fund, with the aim of preserving and developing Estonian culture and art. This fund has, for example, supported the building of Kumu, the activities of the Tartu Art Museum, the exhibition of Estonian émigré art in 2010–2011 in Tallinn, Tartu and elsewhere. Solo exhibitions in Estonia took place: in 1990 at the Adamson-Eric Museum, in 2003 at the National Library and at the Saaremaa Museum.
d8479c2fb86ff59de95e416c67116635717cc0ea: He became a renewer of Estonian modernist sculpture in the 1970s. Alongside formal searches based on the interaction of plastic volumes and space, an exceptional pursuit of elegance appeared in his work. Soans has managed to poeticise bronze as a sculptural material of value, and his bronze sculptures are created with a pure silhouette effect. He broadened the thematics and communicativeness of Estonian sculpture, bringing into his works existential reflections on the possibilities of man and the humanities in a technology-based, alienating world. Soans can be viewed as an intellectual and a teacher, followed both by his students and his colleagues. The public knows him predominantly as a monumentalist. He has created more than 30 monuments and public sculptures and immortalised great national figures: for example the monuments to A. H. Tammsaare (1978), Voldemar Panso (1980) and Michel Sittow (1982) in Tallinn, the monuments to Kristjan Jaak Peterson (1983) and Jakob Hurt (1994) in Tartu, the monument to August Gailit in Valga (2009). He has also created abstract large-scale forms in Estonia, Finland, the Netherlands and Argentina. Soans's work of recent years carries a cheerful intellectual play with the field of meaning of figures. Bronze of past decades has been replaced by steel, wood and other less durable materials, as well as ready-made objects. In his spatial installations one encounters recognisable recurring motifs, reflections on the nature of sculpture and its relations with time and space. Jaak Soans is professor emeritus of the Estonian Academy of Arts. He has been awarded the honorary title of Meritorious Artist of the ESSR (1980) and People's Artist of the ESSR (1986), the Kristjan Raud Art Prize (1974 and 1986), the grand prize of the Riga Sculpture Quadrennial.
c5f27ad72595d27f097dd0bdea4e408b584b3bea: Edgar Viies (1931–2006) is one of the most important Estonian sculptors of the 20th century. His innovative formal searches and modern choice of materials (aluminium, clinker, welded iron, sheet metal and concrete) marked the beginning of the modern era in Estonian sculpture in the 1960s. With his work, a stylistically pure abstract formal culture appeared in Estonian sculpture for the first time in the post-war years. He already appeared with modernly generalised portrait work in exhibition halls in the late 1950s, attracting attention with his unusually pure silhouette effect and having an inspiring influence. Quite a few of his works from the 1960s–1980s have become classics of Estonian art. Besides the aesthetic problematics, which were important to Viies especially in the first half of his oeuvre, the experiential quality of his works and their connection to universal human spiritual and emotional life should also be valued. In the early 1960s he brought creative experiment into a relatively conservative and rather dull sculpture scene, directing sculptors' attention to the relations of space, form and material. It can be said that it was precisely Edgar Viies who gave impetus to decorative sculpture, which at the time existed in a state of suspended animation. His numerous free works belong to the golden fund of Estonian modernism. Viies's public sculptures in Tallinn, Tartu and Viljandi remain captivating to this day. The best known of these are the monuments to Johann Köler (1976), Jaan Koort (1983) and Friedebert Tuglas (1986), the "Mermaid" (1981) adorning Viru Square, and the soaring "Pegasus" (1963) at the café on Harju Street in Tallinn, which was familiar to several generations as the first modernist interior sculpture in Estonia. Edgar Viies studied in 1951–1952 at the State Art Institute of the ESSR
15f1590c30bcdcaf938173ddfedef6cc2b35220c: painter, printmaker and pedagogue. At the beginning of his creative path he drew pictures with political content, including caricatures (under the pseudonym Vaikne), for Estonian satirical publications. The figure "The Torch-Bearer" on the cover of the first "Noor-Eesti" album was the first to attract attention. He made illustrations and design based on Art Nouveau-stylised ornament and symbolic imagery for G. Suits's poetry collection "Tulemaa" (1913) and for the fifth "Noor-Eesti" album (1915). While staying in Norway he focused on landscape painting ("Decorative Norwegian Landscape", 1908). His early painterly work shows the influence of symbolism, especially in compositions with national-romantic legendary subjects and depicting heroic battle scenes. Triik was one of the most esteemed portraitists, emphasising spirituality, inner dignity and dramatism (K. Mägi 1908, Juhan Liiv 1909, M. Levin, I. Menning and Viktoria Martna 1910). Later his manner of expression became more expressive compared to the earlier one (portrait of A. Laikmaa, 1913). The free graphic drawings "Martyr" (1913) and "Catastrophe" (1917) express the split personality and tragedy characteristic of expressionism. The drawings "The Birth of Freedom" (1919) and "Howling Dog" (1921) reflect the events following World War I. From the second half of the 1920s comes a number of drawn, distinctive portraits (F. Tuglas 1928, H. Raudsepp 1932, G. Suits 1933); in the 1930s he again cultivated landscape painting more, the most outstanding being landscapes made near Paldiski at Leetse-Lepiku and winter views of Tartu. He also created applied graphics (the publisher's mark of "Siuru", 1917) and the design of the Cross of Liberty (1920)
f420bf4dfbeae5427e5bed16a1fe58e3e0083e7d: Ellen Kolk (1942) belongs to the circle of women artists who changed the overall picture of Estonian art exhibitions at the beginning of the 1970s. As with several of her contemporary young women sculptors in the early 1970s, Ellen Kolk's arrival at art exhibitions can also be linked to the revaluation of aestheticism in sculpture. It was she who brought bronze back into exhibition halls as a sculptural material, considerably before the beginning of the regular bronze casting of ARS Monumentaal. The "Venus" completed in 1970 is one of the first full figures in the new aestheticist manner. Kolk has been interested both in motifs derived from ancient mythology and in classicistically ennobled imagery and allegorical choice of themes. Elements of nature appear as attributes in several figural compositions. Sensitively modelled sculptures with masterly surface treatment connected with the aesthetics of the new generation of the early 1970s. The works are figural, distinguished by precise modelling, clear classical formal language and masterly surface treatment. Most of the works are executed in bronze, but she has also created works in marble and dolomite. Chamber-like figures and portraits have over the years found their way into public space (e.g. the green area with a pool in front of the North Estonia Medical Centre in Mustamäe, Kuressaare Hospital, Maardu Manor, Palmse Manor, the Commandant's Garden on Toompea in Tallinn, SEB Bank in Tallinn, the Russian Embassy in Luxembourg). Kolk graduated from Tartu Art School in 1962 and from the State Art Institute of the ESSR in the speciality of sculpture in 1967. She has been awarded the Kristjan Raud Prize (1981).
996d5586d6d3f1eb47e4dd5ce60d17c35942572c:
Alver Linnamägi’s Letters from the Army was made during his service in the Estonian Defence Forces. At the same time Anneli Porri cureted an exhibition in EKKM titled Making of Contemporary Art. During the exhibition the museum received a letter each week for four consecutive weeks, for which there was a mailbox installed on a fence in front of the museum. There was none before and no mail had until then arrived to the museums address. Letters from the Army was from its beginning closely related to the EKKM and therefore it seemed logical to add the work to the collection. For its compensation, Anders Härm, a member of the museum’s board, replied to Alver Linnamägi’s letters while the originals were exhibited in EKKM in 2011 during the exhibition of the collection entitled Museum Files I: Collected Principles. The four replies also arrived to the museum’s address.

Alver Linnamägi: ‘The four letters that were delivered from the Defence Forces to the EKKM were one of the few chances I, as a student and as a recruit, had to maintain a connection with the art world and the people in it. The work consists of texts written during night watch, descriptions of certain situations, which purpose was to share what was happening around me with people, to most of whom this environment seemed as alien as to myself. is a work consisting of a 24-hour sound composition, which repeats continuously throughout the exhibition period. The sound is played through megaphones mounted on a wooden pole, connected to a transmission network. The composition is based on sound recordings collected over a two-week period in the immediate surroundings of the installation. In order to avoid overwhelming the site acoustically, the performance frequency of the recorded sound fragments corresponds to the natural soundscape of the location. The installation reflects the site’s characteristic sound environment while simultaneously extending and subtly shifting it. Additional keywords include public and private space, noise pollution, and the low-cost functionalist aesthetics of transmission networks.

Raul Keller: “The creation of the original work happened to coincide with the April 2007 riots in Tallinn, commonly referred to as the ‘Bronze Night’. As a result, the installation’s sound programme included recordings of the events, which were then played back regularly for approximately two weeks. After the exhibition at Tallinn Art Hall ended, the pole with the megaphones (without the sound component) was never removed, gradually becoming an almost invisible artwork. It remained in place for years and was only dismantled later, when the communication infrastructure in front of Tallinn Art Hall was upgraded.”
905518b7485b20fd09fb12b7bec00bc4b770d609:
The series of paintings named Tip of the Day was first exhibited in the Tallinn Art Hall exhibition Violence & Propaganda in 2006. The series consists of nine paintings, the texts of which were based on what was being said in the media.  Its core lies in the Guantanamo (Gitmo) prison camp, which was not subject to the Geneva Convention (III) concerning the rights and general human rights of ‘prisoners of war’ before July 2006. Focusing on three key elements – a gun, Casio watches and olive green – which should serve as the terrorists’ ‘field-marks’. The author raises questions concerning the background and reasons of placing people in prison camps. The series of paintings has been acquired in return for everlasting free entrance to EKKM exhibitions, even though Elin Kard is a member of the board of EKKM  and all exhibitions at EKKM are free.

Elin Kard: ‘At that time I read a lot of different materials from the foreign press about the Guantanamo (Gitmo) prison camp which at that time still operated. In my recollection various people who ended up in Gitmo were asked when, where, and on what grounds they were arrested. The staff was asked what the so called ‘external features’ are, which help to recognize terrorists. The required elements or elements that could be misleading were: possession of a gun, the Casio F-91W wristwatch and the use of olive green in clothing’.
e0f5c8dddb11a8562895f5041fef69c16cbc2e1e: Estonian actor, studied 1918–24 at the Tallinn Municipal Boys' Secondary School and 1924–25 at the State School of Arts and Crafts (in Günther Reindorff’s graphic art class). Studied singing under Armanda degli Abbati and Helmi Einer. Was admitted in 1925 to the Estonia study group, worked 1925–41 (also performed in operetta) and 1947–49 at Estonia, in 1947 at Rakvere Theatre, 1949–65 at the Drama Theatre and 1966–83 at the Youth Theatre; from 1941–46 was deported to Solikamsk. Performed in radio plays (Tolstoy’s The Living Corpse, 1956; Cronin’s The Citadel, 1956; Büchner’s Danton’s Death, 1963), television productions (Hauser’s White Blood, 1959; Gruszecki’s Big Bobby, 1962; Dürrenmatt’s The Meteor, 1969; Bunin’s On the Night Sea, 1977) and in more than 30 films (Children of the Sun, 1932, Theodor Luts’s studio; Pöördel, 1957, The New Devil of Hell's Bottom, 1964, Indrek, 1975, The Master of Kõrboja, 1979, all Tallinnfilm; Traces in the Snow, 1955, The Quiet Season, 1968, both Lenfilm; Ambassador of the Soviet Union, 1969, Mosfilm; Between Three Plagues, 1970, Eesti Telefilm). Was also known as a painter and, before World War II, as a mood singer. Memoir book Näitleja on ajastu lühikroonika (1986). Films have been made about him: Ants Eskola (1968, Eesti Telefilm) and Ants Eskola: olla või mitte olla (2008, director Kristjan Paul Virve). His prison letters have been published in the book Härra Ants. Ants Eskola kirjad Hugo Laurile Solikamski vangilaagrist (2005, compiled by Irja Vaher).
00b5c63801379b7f388324d4140f1f82f92193a3: Evald OKAS was an extremely versatile artist who participated in Estonian art life for more than sixty years. His early work consists mainly of nudes and portraits, but after World War II his large figural compositions and industrial views became notable, with which he represented the Tallinn school of Soviet contemporary art, or severe style, in the 1950s (Nikolai Kormašov, Enn Põldroos, Olev Subbi and others are also considered to belong to this school). In the 1970s Okas brought a sensual-erotic treatment to Estonian painting, creating numerous vividly colored theatrical compositions and nudes. As a creator of vital and colorful nude paintings and compositions, Okas worked until his death. Okas first obtained his art education as a student of Voldemar Mellik and August Jansen at the State School of Arts and Crafts, later under the guidance of Johannes Greenberg at the State Higher Art School, where he gained in-depth knowledge in the field of painting. From 1944 Okas worked as dean of the Estonian State Institute of Applied Art, from 1954 as professor at the Estonian State Art Institute, and in 1993 became professor emeritus of the Estonian Academy of Arts (Tallinn Art University). From 1975 Okas was an academician of the USSR Academy of Arts, which enabled him to undertake numerous horizon-broadening trips abroad (including to Japan, the United States, India, etc.).
9c142f320c2d556d20191160fa64f372daf189e2: He was born in Tuhalaane Parish, Viljandimaa, and after finishing secondary school moved to St Petersburg, where he entered the Stieglitz School of Art, which he graduated from in 1902, becoming the first Estonian to complete studies in decorative and glass painting. He was elected by the school's council as head of the glass painting department, after which he went to further his professional knowledge in Paris and at the Royal Institute of Glass Painting in Munich. Later he went to Darmstadt for the same purpose, and painted, on commission from the Russian imperial court's chancery, a large glass painting for the mausoleum of the Peter and Paul Fortress. He also painted a glass-painting altarpiece for Vladimir Cathedral. In 1905 he was head of the interior decorative painting of the Russian church built in Darmstadt by Emperor Nicholas II. He travelled repeatedly to art schools and museums in Germany, France and Italy, as well as to Turkey, Greece, Egypt, Palestine and Syria. He was a drawing teacher for 13 years at the Peterhof gymnasium and at St Catherine's School in St Petersburg. In 1917 he graduated with a diploma from the Imperial Archaeological Institute. From 1918 to 1929 he was a teacher at Leningrad's 1st Realschule and was appointed professor at the Estonian Workers' University. In 1920 he returned to Estonia and began working at the State School of Applied Art, the Tallinn Technical School and the Conservatory. From 1925 to 1928 he was director of the Estonian Art Museum, from 1926 chairman of the Estonian Artists' Union, and from 1935 chairman of the Estonian Academic Association of Professional Artists. He retired in 1940.
c7e64aa50233e5ded6e427cfc3c8d86ea9a170c9: A Baltic German printmaker, painter and pharmacist. He was born as the son of a pharmacist of Swiss origin who was also a town councillor of Limbaži; his mother was the daughter of a local pastor. In 1828 Gehlhaar passed the examination for pharmacist's assistant at the University of Tartu, and in 1828, as an external candidate, the examination for pharmacist. In 1834 he became the owner of his father's pharmacy in Limbaži. He presumably studied at the drawing school of the University of Tartu under C. A. Senff, but as an artist he was mainly self-taught. In 1828 he published in Tallinn the first series of view prints in aquatint technique, published by Georg Eggers. The series included three views drawn by T. Gehlhaar himself, six sheets reproduced gouache paintings by Johannes Hau, and three engravings rendered sepia drawings or paintings by Karl Ferdinand von Kügelgen. In 1832/33 there appeared, compiled/executed by T. Gehlhaar and marketed by G. Eggers but published anonymously, a series of 12 sheets in the so-called ink-manner aquatint technique. In 1833–35 Gehlhaar also made individual sheets with views of Tallinn and its surroundings, as well as, in 1835, a series of views of Riga in aquatint technique. Around 1840 Georg Friedrich Schlater lithographed in colour in Tartu T. Gehlhaar's 12-sheet ethnographic series "Characteristic Scenes from the Life of the Peasants of Estonia and Livonia". Around 1850 T. Gehlhaar executed a series of 10 lithographs of views of Tallinn (publisher F. Kluge) and other individual sheets (lithographer F. J. Tempeltey). T. Gehlhaar has also created oil and gouache paintings.
5518a3235dba165b3533016e11546ca218f5b0b4:
Priidu Aavik was born as the fifth child in the nine-child family of the schoolteacher Eduard Aavik. In 1914 the family moved to Tallinn, and in 1917 relocated to Maidla Manor in Hageri. Priidu Aavik studied at the Hageri parish school. In 1918 his mother died, and P. Aavik went to live with the Kruus family in Haiba village, Kernu Parish; at the age of 17 he moved to Tallinn.

P. Aavik studied art at Ants Laikmaa's studio school; in 1934 he entered the Pallas Higher Art School, where he studied under Nikolai Triik and Ado Vabbe until 1938. He then founded his own studio; in 1939 he made a trip to Paris but was forced to return upon the outbreak of war. In the summer of 1941 Aavik was mobilised into the Red Army. He took part in battles near Tallinn and Leningrad, later moving to Yaroslavl, where he was one of the founders of the collective of Estonian artists in Yaroslavl and of the Estonian Soviet Artists' Union.

After returning to Estonia, he worked from 1944 to 1946 as acting director of the Tartu State Art Institute, from 1945 to 1947 as chairman of the board of the Estonian Soviet Artists' Union, and from 1947 to 1948 as chairman of the Tallinn Art Fund. From 1951 to 1953 he was chief artist of the Estonian pavilion at the All-Union Agricultural Exhibition, and from 1954 to 1962 chief artist of the Estonian SSR National Economy Exhibition. From 1962 to 1965 he took part in two longer Atlantic Ocean voyages, belonging to the base of the Tallinn fishing fleet (the first in the North Atlantic, the second in the south, also visiting West Africa).
4d473176e89c9081fa0606995de41f9d9a9a77a3: The Estonian painter, pedagogue and public figure Enn PÕLDROOS (1933, Tallinn) has cultivated mainly figural composition and portraiture (he has also been called a painter of people and human relationships). He entered the art scene immediately after completing his studies and sought to express the novel views of himself and his generation's contemporaries, opposing the hitherto naively idealising or exaggeratedly grandiose depiction of reality with an artistic generalisation of the essence of phenomena. Põldroos attracted attention with his somewhat rough manner of treatment; many of his paintings display the so-called severe style [karm stiil] of the 1960s, characterised by simple form, clear sharp contour and a sparse choice of colour. Over the course of the decade the distinctive features of Põldroos's work took shape: emphasis on silhouette and detail, composition based on dissonant contrasts (e.g. mechanical–organic, geometric–painterly), and the highlighting of conflict and drama in situations. He has also created existentialist works based on poetic symbolic imagery. At the end of the 1960s the artist's creative manner changed, manifesting itself in a vigorous, expressive brush treatment and a vivid colour scheme. The search for a new approach to colour is expressed above all in portraits, in which he emphasises the rich inner life and inner energy of the person depicted; some works acquire a touch of the grotesque.
9ec5f64f5f98413a00d6581503c55ed88cb94c8c: Herman Aunapuu was born on 12 March 1915 in Kokand, Turkestan, Central Asia, where his father was a stationmaster. The family moved to Tartu in 1921. In 1933 Aunapuu entered the Pallas Higher Art School, where he received a first-class education under Jaan Vahtra, Voldemar Mellik and Villem Ormisson. His main supervisor, however, was Ado Vabbe, under whom he also continued his studies at the Tartu State Art Institute from autumn 1944. In March 1945 Aunapuu was arrested and, by decision of a special tribunal, sentenced from 8 September to eight years in a corrective labour camp for betraying the homeland. He remained in labour camps in the Komi ASSR and Arkhangelsk Oblast until 1953. Herman Aunapuu first exhibited in 1940 at an exhibition organised by the Pallas Art Society, where donations and deposits were displayed — ranging from Konrad Mägi to Elmar Kits — which were meant to become the founding stock of the Tartu Art Museum then being established. Aunapuu was at that time still a student, yet he was already being compared to Endel Kõks and Elmar Kits. After the labour camps Aunapuu rarely exhibited; in fact he was pushed aside from exhibitions. He was never admitted to the Artists' Union. From 1971 onward the artist lived in seclusion near Tartu, in Peedu. Herman Aunapuu died on 29 December 1998 in Tartu and is buried at Raadi Maarja Cemetery.

Joann Sõstra was born in 1913 by Lake Peipsi in the village of Lisje, into a family with many children. He attended four grades of village school; already at the age of 15 Joann worked at the Lauassaare peat bog, later doing forest work.

In 1932 Joann Sõstra went to Kanaküla in Pärnumaa for forest work, where he ended up as a lodger at the Leppoja farm. There Joann Sõstra found himself a new home, and in addition to three foster children, 4 more children were born together with the mistress of the house, Olga.

In connection with the nationalisation of farmlands, Joann Sõstra moved to Viljandi in 1949 to work as a logger at the Forestry Combine. In 1967 he went to work at the Kilingi-Nõmme Demonstration Forestry Enterprise, where he was engaged in various forestry tasks.

After a heart attack in 1977, when his health no longer allowed heavy physical labour, he devoted himself increasingly to making wood sculptures. In addition to his very diverse body of wood sculpture, Joann Sõstra has made willow-wicker furniture pieces, a garden gate, vases, walking sticks of curious shapes, wooden spoons and ladles, woven baskets and trays. It is difficult to determine the total number of works, as no record of them has been kept. Many items have been given as gifts to acquaintances and relatives.

Joann Sõstra has on several occasions been written about as a very diligent working man, but never as an amateur artist. Joann Sõstra died in 1992.
d07c1d60aeada9d277d8427c9b7c91ee04a52cde: Ülo Õun has influenced an entire generation of Estonian sculptors, even though he never worked as a teacher. With him came something essentially new to Estonian sculpture of the 1970s: a previously unencountered, friendly grotesque, which found expression both in the portraits created by the sculptor and in figurative free creation. Also surprising was a free modelling that indirectly recalled the late work of Alberto Giacometti (1901–1966). Thanks to Ülo Õun, Estonian sculpture became considerably more communicative. He was captivated by colour in sculpture, and by the fluidity and mutability of forms. Ülo Õun's working method differed significantly from the formal aspirations of contemporary Estonian sculptors. His sculptures generally lacked the nature-following modelling and the generalisation derived from it, which was generally considered important in Estonian sculpture of that period. The flowing forms of Õun's portraits and figures spread according to their own will. As a final material he preferred plaster, which had until then been regarded as an intermediate material, and he painted his sculptures with bright aniline colours, which unfortunately have by now mostly lost their intensity. He sought to bring into sculpture qualities usually considered to belong to theatre art and music. Ülo Õun graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1966 and, after briefly working as a taxidermist at the Estonian Museum of Natural History, was a freelance artist for the rest of his life.

Jesus (in Aramaic [ישוע] (Yeshua or Yeshu); in Greek form Ἰησοῦς (Iesus); Jesus of Nazareth; for Christians Jesus Christ; born probably before the year 4 BC, around 6 BC to 4 BC in Bethlehem, Judea; died around 30 to 33 AD in Jerusalem) was a Jewish, Judaic itinerant preacher, religious teacher and healer. From around the year 28 he appeared publicly in Galilee as well as in Judea. Two or three years later, soldiers of the Ancient Roman Empire crucified him at the order of the Roman prefect Pontius Pilate.

The New Testament, as a document of faith of early Christianity, is also the most important source for research into the historical Jesus. According to the New Testament, Jesus called disciples, proclaimed to the Jews of his time the nearness of the Kingdom of God, and thus called his people to repentance. His followers proclaimed him, after his death, as the Messiah (Christ) awaited in Judaism, and as the Son of God. From this arose the new world religion of Christianity. Jesus also became significant outside Christianity.

Jesus Christ is the central figure of Christianity, in church tradition the founder of the Christian faith. According to Christianity, Jesus was the Messiah (Christ) awaited in Judaism and the Son of God, who through his death and resurrection brought redemption to humankind and, after his return, establishes a kingdom of justice and peace.

0ffda64f07cb7ea6ea54a76251be77466661bb9f: Matti Varik (1939–2011) became one of the most prominent creators of public sculptures and monuments in Estonia during the 1960s-1970s, though his free creative work of the 1970s was equally innovative. He brought coloured figures to sculpture exhibitions, preferring bronze as a material, but also created large-format figures from dolomite. The monuments he created during the Soviet era as state commissions (for example the monument to the victims of fascism in Kuressaare, 1965, the monument to the Battle of Tehumardi, 1967, both together with Riho Kulla, the sculptural part of the Maarjamäe memorial complex, 1975) are resolved innovatively and mark a turn in Estonian monumental art towards effective laconicism. His monumental work is characterised by a forceful plastic form, compactness and balanced composition. The best works of this period, such as the monument to V. I. Lenin in Kotka (1979), the monument to Ernst Särgava in Tallinn (1985) and the public sculpture "Perekond" erected in Berlin (1984), employ a novel formal language and adapt successfully to their surroundings. His monumental work, which met the expectations of the era, brought him social recognition in the 1970s-1980s. After Estonia regained independence, he created successful monuments both at home and abroad.

d1fb308e4dc48db53f213694a245bb801510827a: Raivo Korstnik (1932-1992) was born in Maidla, Ida-Virumaa. He received his art education at ERKI (1951–1957). After graduating from ERKI, the 1960s marked the beginning of Korstnik's best-known and most highly regarded period of creative work. This period also includes Korstnik's appearance at the 1966 youth exhibition, which is considered one of the most important displays in Estonian art history focused on new art. As far as is known, only one solo exhibition took place during the artist's lifetime. Although he was a well-known and recognized artist, he preferred working as a lecturer over active exhibition activity. Until his death Korstnik worked at the Estonian SSR State Art Institute (ERKI) and at the Tallinn Pedagogical Institute, while remaining connected in parallel to the world of television and film. Whereas earlier attention was mainly drawn to Korstnik's realistic works from the 1960s, mostly sea-themed paintings, industrial landscapes representing the "harsh style", and cityscapes with cubist touches, now it is the artist's surrealist works that attract the most attention. Surrealist elements can be found in the artist's early landscape paintings, nude paintings and sketches. During his lifetime the artist also frequently painted landscapes and views of Tallinn.

Together with his uncle Karl Adolf Senff he travelled to Italy in 1831, where he lived in Rome, visited Naples and Pompeii. 1fbd72cff483eef726b8f403fbb1f5086df3f7be: Writer, literary and theatre critic; studied 1898–1903 at Hugo Treffner Gymnasium in Tartu and 1906–07 and 1907–11 at the Faculty of Law of the University of Tartu. She has been professor at the sculpture department of the Pallas University of Applied Sciences since 2014. Founder of the Paper Museum in 2010. Holder of a Guinness World Record: together with her students she created the world's largest mosaic made of used batteries, 2017. Founder of the Estonian Origami Centre SATORI, 2020.
a1deb13a4bb9145877196a355c46988de7007f22: Aime Kuulbusch-Mölder (1942) entered Estonian art life at the beginning of the 1970s. In connection with her work, one can speak of a revaluation of aestheticism in sculpture. Her figures and portraits, with their restrained form and masterful surface treatment, connected with the aesthetics of the new generation of the early 1970s. Her portraits created in the 1970s of young Estonian artists and intellectuals – among them, for example, Juhan Viiding, Malle Leis, Tiit Pääsuke and others – can be viewed as a collective portrait of the entire generation of creative intelligentsia of the time that stood in opposition to the Soviet regime. The portrait sculptures created in the 1970s–1980s, as well as memorial monuments to cultural and educational figures rendered in a portrait-like manner, follow the aesthetic canons established in the 1970s. As a material she has preferred bronze, but has also created decorative chamotte figures and used plastic and aluminium. In the 1980s she became one of the most prolific monumental artists. Aime Kuulbusch graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1969. She has been awarded the Kristjan Raud Art Prize (1983) and named Honoured Artist of the Estonian SSR (1984).
7f5e18961afa8326a80492bd2b5462c5efaf9fbe: Madlen Hirtentreu (1993) is a multidisciplinary artist whose work encompasses sculpture and site-specific installations. She has earned a bachelor's degree in visual communication from the Istituto Europeo di Design in Milan and a master's degree in sculpture and installation art from the Estonian Academy of Arts. The driving force of Hirtentreu's work is memory, history and the exploration of materiality, through which she blurs the boundaries between archaeology, speculative fiction and industrial aesthetics. These sculptures and installations can be both historical excavations and speculative visions of the future. Her works often refer to absence or a lost presence. In her works one frequently encounters ghostly, hybrid and fragmentary bodies or abandoned structures, which evoke the feeling that something once existed but no longer exists fully. Hirtentreu offers an alternative view of history, seeing it not as a fixed past but as a process in constant interpretation. She treats objects and materials as fossils of an unknown future.
f9340075aa774d8f081ca7b985f292aa35e548cd: Kertu Rannula (b. 1997) lives and works in Tallinn. Through site-specific photo and video installations, she explores the relationships, signs and symbols between the contemporary human being and cultural space. Inspired by everyday life and personal experience, Rannula adapts to the world and its phenomena through her creative work. In creating her works, she often uses her own physical presence and takes on different roles. In doing so, she finds answers to her own questions, analyses and makes sense of the environment around her. In shaping her works, she considers it important to work with space, approaching materials and media experimentally. Rannula has earned a bachelor's degree in photography from the Faculty of Fine Arts of the Estonian Academy of Arts. She has furthered her studies at the Iceland University of the Arts in the Fine Arts department and at PXL University of Applied Sciences and Arts in Belgium in the department of sculpture and installation. Rannula has participated in exhibitions in Estonia and abroad. Among the most recent are “snapchat dystopia” at Kanal Gallery (2022) and “memories -70%” at Riga Photomonth (2021). In 2020, she participated in the ISSP Residency in Riga, Latvia.
03d14f6d1b63201c3539190aab555da08bf500d9: Eduard Ole was born in 1898 in Valga County, Karula Parish, Kaagjärve Municipality, at the Saibasoo farm. He studied at pastor Wühner's four-grade church school and at Valga town school. He received his art education in 1914–1918 in Russia at the Penza private art school (a branch of the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts), from which he graduated with the qualification of drawing teacher. After returning to Estonia, he worked from 1919 as a teacher at Rakvere Secondary School and the Teachers' Seminary, from 1922 at the Tartu Girls' Gymnasium and the Commercial and Trade School, and from 1924–1936 at Hugo Treffner Gymnasium; from 1936 at the Tallinn French Lyceum. In 1923, E. Ole was a founding member of the avant-garde Estonian Artists' Group; from 1927 he belonged to the Estonian Central Society of Visual Artists, later serving as the society's vice-chairman. E. Ole visited Paris repeatedly, for the first time in 1927. In 1937 he travelled together with Juhan Raudsepp to England, Belgium, France, Italy and Central Europe. In 1943 the artist fled Estonia for Finland; from 1944 he lived in Sweden, in Vällingby, West Stockholm, and worked at the Nordic Museum. In 1946, Ole, together with Eduard Wiiralt, undertook a trip to Lapland.
7f70918f71fccaf5dcd196de1e7457b989fa9624: Born according to the old calendar on 29 November 1795 at Teenuse (Stenhusen) manor in Läänemaa, studied 1804-1810 at the Herrnhuter school in Neuwied and 1811-1812 at the Tallinn Cathedral School. Served 1812-1820 in the Russian army, worked 1820-1822 in the archive of Tartu University, studied under the guidance of C. A. Senff at the university's drawing school. In 1822 travelled in Berlin and Dresden, until 1827 furthered his education in art in Italy. In 1824 met the artist A. L. Richter and in 1825 travelled together with him, staying in Civitella. Lived 1827-1829 at Teenuse manor, in 1829 settled in Tartu, where in 1835 he founded a wood-engraving workshop. Began a series of copper engravings (+etchings) devoted to the history of Livonia, "Viiskümmend pilti..." ("Fifty Pictures..."), of which the 1st issue appeared in 1839 and the 2nd issue in 1842, along with two further sheets. Produced graphic teaching aids, painted portraits and altarpieces (1835 Saarde church, 1837 Ruhja church, 1845 Põlva church). Maydell's paintings for Tartu St John's Church have been destroyed. He was also a sculptor, and a designer of silverwork and woodwork. From 1829 he worked on the restoration of Tallinn's St Olaf's Church (completed 1840). Died according to the old calendar on 6 September 1846 in Tallinn, buried in the Kullamaa churchyard
98be4797b06dd68707458526b2b6b9f5420b15ab: Jevgenia Dudin (1986) is an artist from Pärnu, working in Tallinn. She has completed her master's studies at Tallinn University in the field of art education. She currently teaches fine art at a hobby school, helping preschool- and school-age children develop attention, taste and creative thinking. In her works she combines a decorative approach with realistic elements, using acrylic paints and saturated colours. Her paintings are devoted to everyday scenes in which one senses silence, observation and inner life. Contemplative female figures, everyday objects and interior fragments often appear in her paintings as depictions of memories or personal states. In addition to painting, she is also an illustrator: her work ranges from serious graphics for history publications to colourful pictures for children's books. She regularly takes part in exhibitions and develops her brand Padiloom, where she handmakes textile bags with illustrative motifs. This project combines her love of drawing, applied art and the desire to make everyday things a little more personal and expressive.
85af75e4c28a7eef82a39d66bafdef33bd8a96f4: Hedi Kuhi (b 1998) is a painter who lives and works both in Tallinn and in Valga. In 2019 she graduated from the Tartu Art School in the speciality of decorator, and in 2026 from the Pallas University of Applied Sciences in the speciality of painting. In 2023 Hedi was awarded the Hotell Pallas scholarship, as a result of which the solo exhibition "Jälle siin" ("Here Again") was created at the Tartu Art House. In 2025 she was awarded the Eduard Wiiralt scholarship and the Pallas field scholarship in the arts. In the autumn of the same year Hedi took part, together with Danel Ülper, in the duo exhibition "Ega sa siin Valgas Marki ei tea? Lugu piirilinnast" ("You Wouldn't Happen to Know Mark Here in Valga? A Story of a Border Town") at Hobusepea Gallery. She has also taken part in several group exhibitions and auctions. In her work Hedi focuses on the perception of the surrounding environment. She is interested in the balance between wildness and order, both in urban space and in a person's inner world. Figures, nature motifs and cityscapes are often layered together in her paintings. In creating her works she uses the technique of double exposure, as a result of which the depicted views feel as though suspended between the dreamlike and the real world. Her body of work consists mainly of oil and acrylic paintings, drawings and graphic works.
99f0ae64c1231bb27698b1c65846b099b71e02e1: Allan Roosileht is a legendary Estonian musician, DJ and music lover, one of whose hobbies is collecting sound recordings. In addition to his love of music, Allan is also a great enthusiast of art. "I think my first interest in art is connected with my mother. My mother bought and gave art to loved ones, and it was probably on her recommendation that I had my first great art experience at the Kunstihoone exhibition "Ruum ja vorm" ("Space and Form") in 1976. Since then I have been on familiar terms with art. During my time at university I had the honour of attending Kaalu Kirme's wonderful lectures on art history. Those wonderfully warm and exciting teachings helped me form a broader picture of what was happening in the art world. I have considered Leonhard Lapin my great favourite and inspiration, and through him also Kandinsky. Music, especially pop and rock music, has always been connected with art. Salvador Dalí teamed up with Alice Cooper, Andy Warhol with "The Rolling Stones". Jüri Arrak has designed the album covers of "Metsatöll", and Kalev Mark Kostabi has made forays into music. In the world there is a range of artists and designers whose work is known precisely through record covers," says Allan Roosileht.
f2b0c378238032c75c8162d5405fe87b8aab849b: Tiina Sarapu is a glass artist in whose work glass is primarily an installation and sculptural material, but on the level of ideas an intermediate stage between the visible and invisible world. Sheet glass is often the starting material for her works, from which, by means of a seemingly simple bending, a three-dimensional form has been created. The edges and surfaces in these are at once independent yet interdependent elements, and thanks to the transparency of the glass they form a complex multi-layeredness. The spatial layers of glass in Sarapu's works often carry the meaning of layers of time. Tiina Sarapu studied in the Department of Glass Art at the Estonian Academy of Arts, from which she graduated with a master's degree in 1996. Since that time she has taught in the same department, and has been a docent there since 2003. She has taken part in numerous exhibitions, symposia and workshops both at home and abroad. Her works are held in the collections of museums and private collectors. Sarapu has been awarded the honorary title "Tunnustatud klaasikunstnik 2004–2005" ("Recognised Glass Artist 2004–2005") and the Kristjan Raud Prize in 2007. She has received recognition at several international glass art competitions. (M. Bukovec)
b20eca413cb1ddeeb9f25e7bcf839219f43f4a94: The Akstra technique - this technique was invented in Viljandi. The cultivation of Akstra art began in the second half of the 1970s under the guidance of A. Gross in the so-called "Akstra" studio. The Akstra technique was A. Gross's own invention. The main components of the technique were enamel paint (of a composition made by the artist himself, which he did not reveal to others) and diluted bitumen. Light enamel paint and dark bitumen were used on the principle of silkscreen printing, but instead of a silk frame a stencil was used. The parts that did not fall under the stencil had to be covered over, sprayed over with enamel paint using an atomiser, and then the enamel paint in turn had to be covered over with the bitumen mixture. The result was a pitch-black plate. Next one had to wait for a reaction, which resembled the developing of a photograph. The places that had been covered turned dark, while the light enamel paint left under the bitumen began, in turn, to react - pressing through the bitumen, and gradually, as a result of the reaction, the desired image was formed. The result of this kind of technique was a somewhat mysterious, watercolour-like painting with vague and sharp outlines. This technique could be executed with two colours.
8d957684fa429e2f0e70e438c19d3153e001fd1c: Nele Tiidelepp (1998) is a multidisciplinary artist and writer who graduated from the Department of Installation and Sculpture at the Estonian Academy of Arts, whose artistic practice is driven by spontaneous reactions to the environment and materials. Poetic and literary elements and narratives often appear in her works. Tiidelepp operates on the border of fictional and real spaces, people and moments, whereby collectivity often appears, both in a direct and an indirect sense: from the use of random fragments of sentences by other people in her texts, to collectively created performances in which every participant is an equally important author. Her works are located on an axis at either end of which stand media of contradictory nature: sculpture and text. The first of these is static, dictated by the practical world and limited by the capabilities of the human body. The second, however, is available at any moment, quick, light, weightless and limited only by the imagination. Somewhere in between are located performative interventions manifesting themselves in different contexts, which often contain text and sound.
a04b41f2f4f36971f083c71e99d1dbfbdffd27ba: Before World War II, August Vomm's oeuvre consisted mainly of portrait busts and about a dozen labour-intensive gravestones. He depicted Ruts Bauman, Ants Lauter, Hugo Laur, Gustav Ernesaks, Romulus Tiitus, Ferdi Sannamees and others. As one of the few artists who spent the war years in his homeland, August Vomm adapted to the new demands right in the first post-war years. In 1945 he joined a brigade of sculptors, creating for the Estonia Theatre reliefs symbolising the union republics. In 1947 a monument to those fallen in the Great Patriotic War was completed in Viljandi, in 1952 a monument to Lenin, again created by the brigade method, was unveiled in Tartu, as well as, together with Lagle Israel, a memorial to Nikolai Burdenko on Toome Hill in Tartu. The monuments to the revolutionary figures Johannes Vares-Barbarus and Hans Pöögelmann in Tallinn, created by him, have since been relocated. For the Lenin jubilee exhibition in 1970, Vomm created a giant oak portrait bust of V. I. Lenin, for which, together with Elmar Kits and Avo Keerend, he was awarded the State Prize and the honorary title of Merited Artist of the Estonian SSR, as well as all-Union recognition in the press
b60a75186393abd5ab819bfd09e9ce74daba520e:
by Johannes Säre parodies the neo-Nazi stereotype by transforming the right-wing extremist, usually dressed in military or neutral tones, into a colorful macho. This change of colors diminishes all threat and credibility and shows just how much the color of someone’s clothes affects people’s first impression of them. The artwork was completed during the time when Tallinn was shook by Pronksiöö riots, which made these questions raised by

was created due to an obligation to finish a task at school, on the other hand it was the desire and need to shift already fixed notions. At the time when I was doing this picture there were riots in Tallinn and my prearranged model, who had more extreme views than the average, had vanished into thin air. Luckily these (pink) boots fitted perfectly to a friend of mine, who happened to come by the school on the day I was to take the photo and the shoot was rescued. Finally, having seen the result, I was very happy and jet again my odd sense of humor had manifested itself in one of my artworks. “
dc2dd3c645f63d58139dda5bc331cf27d7ba47c4: Valerija Oja (b. 2002) is an artist based in Tallinn, who works mainly with painting, but also with monumental painting techniques and various material-based practices. In 2026 she completed her bachelor's studies in painting at the Estonian Academy of Arts, and in 2023–2024 she studied as an exchange student at the State Academy of Fine Arts Karlsruhe in Germany. In her work, Oja explores corporeality, vulnerability and materiality, moving along the borderline between figuration and abstraction. She is interested in opposing states and their coexistence – tenderness and violence, fragility and resilience, the organic and the artificial. Human and animal forms, personal experiences and existential themes intertwine in her works. She has participated in exhibitions in Estonia and Germany, including the duo exhibition Maybe We Should Sleep on the Floor Tonight (Schaudepot am Marktplatz, Karlsruhe, 2023), the group exhibition Õnnekompost (Narva Art Residency, 2024), and the duo exhibition Ma ei taha veel üles ärgata (Täisnurga Gallery, Tallinn, 2026). In 2024–2025 she worked as a gallerist at Täisnurga Gallery.
7db12404fcb53580f0ceaffd29a8de51528bfbd7: Elmar KITS (1913, Tartu – 1972, Tartu) was one of the most outstanding representatives of the "Pallas" school of painting, who cultivated all genres of easel painting, monumental painting and book illustration. He began with impressionistic, light-filled paintings rich in nuanced colour, and painted dynamic figure compositions with a lyrical undertone as well as cityscapes with great generalization of form. Thanks to his ability to also paint in the realistic genre, Kits adapted fairly easily after World War II to the demands placed on art by the new regime. In the late 1950s, form-renewing cubist and abstractionist notes appeared in the artist's work. He was the first in Estonia to apply stylization and abstracted imagery also in monumental painting. Kits received his art education at the Pallas art school, where he graduated in the 1939 class, considered very strong, under Aleksander Vardi, Kaarel Liimand, Villem Ormisson and Ado Vabbe. From 1947 to 1949, Kits worked at the Tartu State Art Institute as head of the department of monumental painting, later working as a freelance artist in Tartu. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
bdee63e0b0f26f96731d8df7b889c99afabfa91b:
Superflex, the well-known Danish art group, participated in the KUMU opening exhibition titled Shift Scale in 2006 with its non-alcoholic vodka project. Non-alcoholic vodka tastes like vodka but does not contain alcohol. The work seems to comment on uniqueness being lost in globalization – the need to comply with the demands and requirements of international markets and a struggle for survival amongst existing products sets a certain framework, of which being outside of is not beneficial to the product. Non-alcoholic vodka is a good example of a product being outside of said framework.

Hanno Soans, the curator of contemporary art in KUMU at the time and one of the organizers of the exhibition, acquired one of the bottles at the exhibition and donated it to the EKKM collection on the condition that a member of the management board of EKKM, Marco Laimre gets a bottle of alcohol free beer at the NOKU club without paying for it. The deal is yet to be completed, as Laimre has not been able to avoid paying at the bar.
d4ddf3af4d637a34c95a2e38fd9a2faac8611080: Johannes Luik (1988) was born in Tartu. In 2019 he obtained a bachelor's degree at the Estonian Academy of Arts in the Department of Installation and Sculpture. In 2021 he obtained a master's degree in Fine Arts at the LUCA School of Arts in Belgium. As a sculptor and installation artist, Luik is interested in the materiality of (objects) and the parameters conveyed through it that describe the properties of the physical world, such as material, texture, mass, volume and dimensionality. He is interested in the relationship of (abstract) objects to three-dimensional architectural space and the functional relationship of architectural details to these objects. Luik says: "This kind of intervention points to the potential of a space to look different or to be used differently. As an installation artist, space thus becomes a material which, when activated, makes it possible to create different ways of experiencing and remembering." In 2018 and 2019 he received the Young Sculptor Award, and in 2020 he was recognized with the Adamson-Eric scholarship.
404cdf1623e51fcfdc2de1ed75b987eb10485528: Came from a family of shoemakers. Worked in a joinery workshop in Erastvere. Was accepted to study in Frankfurt an der Oder, continued studies in Berlin, and on the recommendation of Fr. R. Kreutzwald, in St. Petersburg in the studio of sculptor A. F. von Bock, and 1865-1867 at the Imperial Academy of Arts in St. Petersburg. Worked in Tartu, Berlin, Munich, and 1873-1890 in Rome. Received the award of the Paris World Exhibition for the sculpture "Hamlet". From 1890 to 1914 he lived and worked in St. Petersburg, and thereafter until his death in Tallinn. From 1916 he served as overseer of the city's art treasures. The main part of his work consists of classicist allegorical figures and portraits. Throughout his career, but especially during his St. Petersburg years, he also created portraits of emperors and empresses, and in the 1890s participated in several competitions for monuments to rulers. The marble portrait bust of Alexander II that he created became especially popular, and the sculptor made several repetitions of it. He also portrayed other emperors and empresses who ruled during his lifetime - Alexander III and Maria Feodorovna, and Nicholas II and Alexandra Feodorovna.
49f5cea82808c9c397337463c1fac9d7aa28dfa5: Kaupo Kikkas (b. 1983) is an Estonian visual artist and music portraitist. He received formal training in photography at Finland’s Visual Arts Institute, but he attributes his award-winning classical music portraits to his education in that field (clarinet, sax, and voice). He has concentrated on fine art photography for twelve years. Although based in Northern Europe, he frequently works in London, Berlin and in the US, as well annual projects in the Amazon rainforest. His personal projects include a study of graveyards, a portrait series of shale miners, and images of a lost cinema in the Egyptian desert, which received wide exposure in the international media. He has photographed a number of books and classical music album covers, and his work often appear in magazines. He was named best commercial portrait photographer at the WPPI Las Vegas 16×20 print competition in 2013, and was honoured as the best Estonian portrait photographer in 2011 (Baltic’s Photography Festival).
814f94fb0103e8658141588bcfe55f62412ac49c: Miina Barrera Pinochet (b. 1991 in Tartu) is an artist from Estonia whose creative practice is divided between Estonia and Germany. Her main medium is painting, complemented by video art and performance. Barrera Pinochet's work often addresses the connections between nature, psychology and human nature, focusing on the cycles of decay and renewal and their emotional and existential resonance in both ecological and inner landscapes. Drawing on natural morphologies, the boundaries between the organic and the symbolic, the intimate and the universal become blurred in her work. Miina Barrera Pinochet graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in painting (BA, 2016) and furthered her studies at the Berlin University of the Arts. She is currently completing her studies in fine arts at the Kassel Academy of Fine Arts. Since 2025 she has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Painters' Association, and a co-founder of the international artist collective Fluidum Ensemble. She has participated in exhibitions since 2011.
8e2944fb2c137fc44d52a3bb55039c78211d690a: Ernst Jõesaar studied sculpture and painting at the Tartu Higher Art School Pallas, graduating from the school in 1933 as a sculptor. His pre-war creative style was connected with the realistic tendencies prevalent in Europe in the 1930s. He emigrated to Sweden in 1944 already as an established sculptor. His work in the free world was inevitably influenced by the canons of European modernism of the first half of the 20th century, but on the other hand his work can be considered extraordinarily independent. Of the works created in the post-war decades, a large group consists of psychological portraits of the contemporary refugee community. Numerous figurative sculptures and reliefs deal figuratively with great, universally human themes; one can read allusions to both antique mythology and biblical legends. An expressive stylisation, containing elements of Mediterranean culture but at the same time northern in its austerity, carries a philosophical thought, the resignation of an artist who had experienced life's hardships and the loss of his homeland, and at the same time hope for the eternity of human creation.
61d06d6ab8fc73609459c3235e8b9d632a634cbf: Kristjan TEDER (1901, Kuigatsi Parish, Tartumaa – 1960, Tartu) was an Estonian painter and gardener who mainly cultivated flower painting, and to a lesser extent also landscape, portrait and genre painting. His early work is New Objectivity in style, characterised by clearly delineated forms and a dull brownish colour scheme. In the 1930s his manner of painting became impressionistically rich in nuance, the colouring bright and, in some works, vivid, with the mode of depiction occasionally showing a naivistic roughness. In the flower paintings created after World War II, Teder focused his attention on bringing out spatiality and modelling with light and shadow. Alongside baroquely lush flower paintings, he also produced landscapes and townscapes in a more restrained colour range. In the second half of the 1950s Teder mainly painted vividly coloured flower pictures and landscapes. Teder acquired his art education at the Pallas Art School, first under Konrad Mägi and then under Ado Vabbe, and in Paris at Vassili Šuhhajev's private academy. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
0ff67553a85995e2f06987de1984c026d4330a7b:
Be Drunk, Be Very, Very Drunk talks about the relationship between alcohol and philosophy. Based on Deleuze and Guattari, Anders Härm links becoming an (conceptual) idiot with alcohol, and later reaches Guy Debord considering Situationists International the first deliberately drunk revolution. The brandy consumed in the course of the lecture makes the academic presentation an ironic human experiment which tests the limits of acceptable and non-acceptable. The criticism does not fall only on the academical mannerism but also on the academy as an institution that is based on over-exploited concepts which smother creativity.

The documentation of the performance was born as an exchange with Latvian Television, who insisted a post-presentation interview from the lecturer before the performance. Härm agreed on the condition that the Latvian Television records the performance from the beginning. The recording reached the lecturer but the interview was dropped.
2d55375bc59a92ed32d507a21e46442725b8ad94: Mirjam Mölder-Mikfelt has been holding solo exhibitions since 2004, has participated in numerous joint exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad, and has taken part in various art projects. The recurring theme of her work is the sensing of oneness with oneself, nature and the universe. The artist finds inspiration in the colours of life, in mind-expanding music, in her own magical dreams, in transformative experiences brought back from travels around the world, and in everything else that makes the soul resonate. Everything that is genuine and inspired resonates with her highly sensitive nature. For the artist, painting is above all a form of therapy, a means of meditation and self-development. The aim of her work is to have a healing effect on the viewer as well, offering positive emotions, a state of peace and uplifting feelings. Experimenting with different techniques and materials results in distinctive, somewhat mystically tinged, dreamlike paintings that reflect the author's inner world.
8983b10129386960ae3deceb137a712320ab8088: Sandra Lääne (b. 1990) is an artist who works mainly in the collage technique, interweaving acrylic painting, marker drawing, photography and newspaper clippings. She has completed her bachelor's studies at the Painting Department of the University of Tartu (2013) and obtained a master's degree in art education at the Estonian Academy of Arts (2016). Collaboration and chance play an important role in her work. Her children Osvald (b. 2022) and Vilma (b. 2023) often become co-authors of the works, their drawings and brushstrokes becoming the starting point of the works or shaping their further course. Lääne's collages are born as a layered process that develops over time, in which different materials, spontaneous traces and conscious interventions intertwine into a whole. Her works often combine abstract colour surfaces and detailed black-and-white drawings, creating a visual space where childlike freedom and playfulness meet the artist's conscious sense of composition. Lääne has previously participated in exhibitions in Estonia, Finland and England.
b11146616dfa044eb654a5e6b6a103556653c92b: Greenberg was an Estonian painter whose work, following the artistic trends of the era, underwent a long stylistic development. The paintings created at the end of the 1920s are expressive, with a rough texture that adds expressiveness. In the 1930s Greenberg was influenced by art deco, in which the treatment of colour emphasises the plasticity of forms. In the middle of the same decade Greenberg's colouring lightened under the influence of impressionism, and he became fascinated by the world of theatre – the peculiar charm of actors and the charm of women quilted with poetic melancholy. During World War II, worry, grief and tragedy were added to his work, which the artist expressed using classical solutions. Greenberg received his art education at Ants Laikmaa's studio school in Tallinn, at the evening courses of the school of applied arts in Berlin, at A. Ažbe's art school in Munich, in H. Groeber's studio, and at the Munich Academy of Art. Later he worked as a lecturer at the Jaan Koort State School of Applied Art and at the Tallinn State Art Institute.
3abeb802708b8d2b9d86db2c61f72b2d8744b7aa: Silvia Sosaar (b. 1979) is an artist living and working in Tallinn. She has an MA from Contemporary Art Dept. of Estonian Academy of Arts. She uses a contemporary work of art to be a so-called (user) interface between the creator, context of creation and the audience. Her activity as an artist is based on mutual creative cooperation and adventures with people that I have chosen. Sosaar has experimented with the analysis of femininity from the neo-pop viewpoint; street-level action; performances at rock concerts; a video production on the topics of mental health based on a literary work; an anthropological study of a profession; including amateurs, etc She is the co-founder and general manager of the publishing house ';paranoia' and has participated at numerous performances of the presentations of publication. Sosaar is a founder of publishing house 'skaala publishing'. She is also a member of the artists' performative musical group 'Karamell'.
884b9e10e6b82446b1bb0ad355346abd219e3ef8: Illimar Paul (b. 1945) began his graphic art studies at the Estonian Academy of Arts (ERKI) in 1964. He continued his studies at the Leipzig Higher School of Graphic Arts and Book Design, from which he graduated with a diploma in 1971. He has taken part in more than 300 joint exhibitions both at home and abroad, and has had 68 solo exhibitions. "Illimar Paul's townscapes made in the hyperrealistic style of the 1970s in the serigraphy technique belong not only to the classics of our graphic art, but were at the time among the most innovative works of graphic art, both in terms of technique and manner of depiction. In his work Paul has used several techniques – besides silkscreen printing, other graphic techniques (linocut), but also watercolour, coloured pencil drawing, mixing them together, moving from a two-dimensional mode of presentation into space, making three-dimensional collages, etc., but his love of detail has survived to this day. Moreover, detail has always meant something very personal and emotional to him." Reet Varblane, 2015
d58589b3f9673f0804a469cda0830eed8ece50ba: Albert Eskel (1922–1975) applied a recognisably distinctive modernist formal language in the 1960s, both in portraits, figural compositions and monumental work. A large part of his bronze sculptures existing today were only cast in the precious material after the author's death. His portrait work, which was cast in bronze already during the author's lifetime, is characterised by a rich nuance of surface treatment and a good sense of the possibilities of the material. He has mostly cut the portraits very low, excluding the neck area, leaving the modelling occasionally deliberately rough. Among the figural compositions there are music-themed compositions marking the era, some of which are also executed in coarse-textured chamotte. All his work of the 1960s is characterised by a striving for forceful expressiveness, the form is laconic and remarkably monumental in overall effect. Among his monuments, the best known is the monument to Eduard Vilde in Tallinn (1965), but he has also created a series of memorial plaques and gravestones.
a09a40f6d19b0044542675031ce618dea04f90db: Enn Roos (1908–1990) is one of the most outstanding sculptors in Estonian art of the post-war decades; his most active period as a sculptor falls in the 1940s–1960s. Having received his education at Tartu Art College Pallas, the sculptor had to spend the war years in Moscow after the Soviet annexation – but upon returning home this brought him certain privileges on the post-war Estonian art scene. Enn Roos was one of the most senior sculpture instructors at the Estonian SSR State Art Institute. Almost all of the current older and middle-aged sculptors have been his students. He became one of the sculptors with a more chamber-like creative style during the post-war decades. The main part of his oeuvre consists of modernist animal sculptures, portraits and decorative sculptures. The monument to the liberators of Tallinn, opened in 1947 by Roos and architect Arnold Alas (relocated in 2007 to the Defence Forces Cemetery), has for decades been regarded as the more artistically successful work of Estonian post-war monumental art.
ae4926873dac76623168fb170bf281b69068d950: Maria Izabella Lehtsaar is an artist working in Tallinn. She graduated from the EKA graphic art department with a bachelor's degree and earned a master's degree in EKA's contemporary art speciality. Lehtsaar works primarily with underrepresented queer experience and narrative, often playing with the boundaries between reality and fantasy. Her works often tell of spaces and hidden symbols, and of coded meanings in queer and lesbian material culture. In her work she weaves together pop culture aesthetics and sensitive monochrome graphic art, combining them in practice with textile, drawing and poetry. The use of different media in her works distorts the familiar, creating multilayered meanings. Lehtsaar's first solo exhibition "Sinikalilla" took place in 2024. In addition, the artist has taken part in several group exhibitions, for example at the Lithuanian Museum of Contemporary Art (MO museum) in the exhibition "We Don't Do This. Intimacy, Norms and Fantasies in Baltic Art". The artist received the Wiiralt Prize in 2023.
f6338076d92aa876c9c7700de90c64efc7403485: Andres Adamson's reply: "Sirje is my mother, who today (28.09.2021) happens to turn 81, and Võidu 18-8 was our address in Kärdla, 1963?-1972. My mother is also currently in Kassari, I'm only going to the birthday afterwards, on Sunday, I'll show her this picture and ask whose it is. Because of the (lack of) level, I assume it's hers. My mother indeed had a proper artistic talent too, she was also supposed to go to ERKI, but by the time they married my father was already there, and they lived in such cramped conditions that two family members studying at the same time was difficult. It was postponed and in the end never happened. I doubt my father's authorship because when was Rannapaargu finished?, probably 1966, he was already 28 then, schools behind him, I wouldn't want to believe such a poor technical level, he later won medals at the Baltic Watercolour Biennials etc. Also the signature is not written in his hand (though it doesn't resemble my mother's either), and he would never under any circumstances have written his own address next to a picture. Unfortunately I can no longer ask my father."
74b3489c9a3586e4eb801ceb05447796be32f88a: He studied at the Karksi and Pöögle parish schools and worked for a while as a farmhand. He then studied wood carving from 1896 at Bandelier's furniture factory in Tartu and drawing at the Tartu German Crafts School. He worked in Riga under the wood carver Johanson, in Liepāja at the Ahi furniture factory, and in Odessa. From 1900 he worked at the Steinberg furniture factory in Rakvere until 1901–1904, when he settled permanently in Pärnu, where he worked as an independent wood carver. His works include the altar decorations of Pärnu Transfiguration of the Lord Church (1904), and writing desk sets for the Supreme Court (1935). In 1935 he organised exhibitions of his works in Pärnu and Tartu, where, among other things, "Ancient Estonian Life in 14 Pictures" was on display. Later he made a 27-picture work about Estonian life 100 years ago and in the present. The wood-cut relief displayed at the exhibition was acquired by the Estonian National Museum. He was a founder and leader of the Pärnu Animal Protection Society. For his services he received the 2nd class Green Cross of the Estonian Animal Protection League.
70048ccad6f000e488614b7efd6de9e08a456bf3:
