79dc599b8650706e8b1365da3d1059d27e4241c2: 1862-64 teacher at the Birkenruh county gymnasium (near Cesis). From 1864 senior teacher of ancient languages and German literature at the Kuressaare progymnasium (from 1865 - gymnasium). As an active public figure, the teacher took a leading part in the establishment of the town park, the founding of a savings bank, and the establishment of a fire brigade society. Holzmayer's greatest merits are as a researcher of antiquities. Under his direction archaeological excavations were carried out at the Kaarma hill fort, the Pöide Order castle, etc. Thanks to his activity, Saaremaa and Muhumaa were, in the second half of the 19th century, one of the archaeologically best-studied areas in the Baltic provinces. Founding member of the Society for the Study of Saaremaa (Verein zur Kunde Oesels), vice-president of the society and curator of the museum 1867-1890.
f03b844a907a5d537ad87c298294c6c332a4c515: Kati Kerstna (1970) works with glass as her material and sculpture as her output. In her works she looks primarily at the current era, the anthropocene, characterised by humanity's ultra-rapid development with unforeseeable effects on the living environment until the end, and in revealing her themes she uses, among other things, the contradictory character of glass – its fragility and strength. Kerstna has obtained a master's degree in the field of glass art at EKA (2001), has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad, and also works as a curator, currently in the working group organising exhibitions of Baltic glass art. In 2023 she received the audience award of the Spring Exhibition. Kerstna is a member of the Estonian Glass Artists' Association, the Estonian Sculptors' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
f83aa0d2d5dc827b6c3e25276a2cef9b3876a1cf: Andre Joosep Arming (1995) lives and works in Tallinn. He studied in the Faculty of Fine Arts of the Estonian Academy of Arts, BA in Photography (2018) and MA in Contemporary Art (2024). In his work Arming primarily uses the media of polaroid and video, as well as the diary format. Arming's works are characterised by themes such as being born and dying, experiential experimentation, timeline and cyclicality. After that he continued his master's studies in contemporary art, taking time to develop his position as an artist. In October 2022 he received a new heart. This year Arming took part in the group exhibition "Enese õrnad žestid" ["Tender Gestures of the Self"] at the EKA gallery (curator: Kaisa Maasik) and at the end of spring took part in the TASE '24 graduation exhibition at the Tallinn Art Hall.
006cfe32d5235f5ce921cb36093794ba150005c4: Bork, Ilmar, (24 June 1927 Tallinn – 11 January 2008 Tallinn), sailor and ice-yachtsman. 182 cm, 64–65 kg. Graduated from Tallinn 2nd Secondary School in 1945 and as an architect from TPI in 1952. Began sailing in 1947 at the Kalev Yacht Club. In 1947, together with Ernst Kuzmanov and Eli Kaldma, became USSR champion in the L3 class. In 1949–50 he was also USSR champion in ice-yachting together with Rein Kumari in the 12 m² free class, in 1948 in ice-yachting in the monotype XV class together with Ernst Kuzmanov, and in 1953 in sailing in the 5.5R class together with Rein Kumari and Leo Purre won bronze at the USSR championships. In 1947–53 he achieved prize-winning places at Estonian championships in sailing and ice-yachting. Worked as an architect, was 1973–80 chairman of the sports club of Vinni Sovkhoz-Technicum. Belonged to the membership of Kalev and Jõud.
da5e48aa386352565628f0a5ee22ba6b02f22836: Natalia Mirzoyan is an animation director and artist working in Estonia, originally from Yerevan, Armenia. She holds a master's degree in Animation from the Estonian Academy of Arts (EKA). Her films have received numerous awards at international animation festivals around the world. Natalia works in various techniques, from hand-drawn animation to stop-motion. In addition to animation, she works as an artist, illustrator and sketcher. She is the author of four murals located in Ülemiste City (Tallinn). Natalia has participated in several group exhibitions and has also had three solo exhibitions. She teaches a sketching course at the Estonian Academy of Arts and also runs courses independently.
7a8ab77e0ea070f1146056eadbb3f0f86c2463fc:
The main character of the story of Sodom and Gomorrah is Lot – Abraham's nephew, who accompanied Abraham on his journey from Ur to Canaan. Because he liked the fertile valley of the Jordan, he decided to settle in the city of Sodom.

God destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah because of their immoral way of life. Lot and his two daughters escaped. They settled in a cave in the mountains. The daughters believed that no men remained alive on earth. Wishing to bring forth offspring, they got their father drunk on two consecutive evenings and then lay with him. Some time later the elder daughter gave birth to a son, who later became the ancestor of the Moabites. The younger daughter also gave birth to a son, who became the ancestor of the Ammonites. Thus Lot became the forefather of two notable peoples.
2b0d3086b4089151ae015e60c61caa89a4630109: Manfred Dubov (1986) depicts in his oil paintings the states of people and places, exploring the connections between the personal and the collective, the physical and the metaphysical. Many of his motifs come from personal life; they pass through the so-called "canvas of the soul", producing notes and sketches which later all find their way to the canvas in some form. Dubov graduated from the painting department of EKA (2010) and has actively participated in exhibitions. He has written two poetry collections and his debut collection "Täna leitakse kõik üles" (2016) was nominated for the Betti Alver Prize. Dubov has worked as a lecturer at EKA and as a nurse in the field of emergency medicine and training. He is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
542a7c61efa50c315633d343eb7881a833a260e2: Tiiu Rebane (b. 1970) graduated from the painting department of the Estonian Academy of Arts in 1999. Painting 2013-2015 TEK, Restoration 2016-2019 EKA, Art History and Visual Culture Studies, MA 1999. Freelance artist, exhibiting since 1994, starting out as a photo and installation artist. Further painting studies at EKA and additional studies in the master's programme of Cultural Theory at EHI reinforced the basis for cultivating existential painting and a striving for realism in art. The main method in Tiiu Rebane's art has been a synthesis of documentalism and distinctive mannerism, with themes of space, human being and time. Works with painting, photography, collage and video. Since 2013 she has been engaged in curating independent art events.
b87983f7893c9abf73b53aaebe6d4abfc1f25814: Writer; Studied at Niitsaadu village school in Penuja parish, later continued as an autodidact, in 1871–77 and 1891–92 lived at Pöögle-Maie village school, where his brother Jaan was the teacher. Worked in 1872 in Pöögle as an assistant parish clerk, from 1873 in Pornuse and elsewhere as a court clerk, later in Karksi, Polli and several other Mulgimaa parishes as parish clerk. In 1893, due to lack of knowledge of Russian, had to leave the clerk's post, worked briefly as the economist of the Viljandi Farmers' Society, from 1894 as bookkeeper at the spirits factory of Kalkuse manor near Daugavpils, from 1898 in Riga as head of department at the Phoenix wagon factory, 1901–04 in Tartu as business manager of Postimees, and 1904–20 as a bank official of the Livonian Mortgage Society.
42acbce1232dc28db1fab45925e4ec97bc440924: I was born in 09.1974 in Kiviõli, Estonia. I graduated from the art department of Tallinn University. I currently work as an art teacher at the Kohtla-Järve School of Arts, and I also teach art therapy at the Kohtla-Järve social home for people with disabilities. I am the head of the virtual branch of the Russian Museum in the White Hall of the Oil Shale Museum. I received the "Teacher of the Year" and "Favourite Teacher of the Year" awards. Since 2009 I have been a member of the Kohtla-Järve Union of Artists, since 2012 a member of the Union of Russian Artists of Estonia. From 2008 to 2020 I participated in more than 70 exhibitions, of which 10 were solo exhibitions. Pictures drawn by me are in the collection of the Pushkin Museum, as well as in private collections in Finland, Russia, America, Germany and Estonia.
78d81ff5a7a1aff101067ee01e51f72be27a091b: Grew up in Järvamaa, in Nõmküla parish, at Remmiku farm. Studied art from 1901 at the drawing courses of the Paide Karskuse Kuratoorium, led by Rudolf Lepik, in 1906 at the Stieglitz School of Technical Drawing in St. Petersburg, in 1907 in the studios of Michael Zeno Diemer and Heinrich Heidner in Munich. In 1910 continued his studies in St. Petersburg at the art school of the Society for the Encouragement of the Arts, where his teacher was Ivan Bilibin. In 1913 received the qualification of drawing teacher. In 1909 exhibited for the first time at an art exhibition in Tartu. During the First World War he served in the Tsarist army, making front-line drawings. In 1918 Roosileht was the drawing teacher at Põltsamaa Realgymnasium, from 1919 a teacher at Paide Gymnasium. In 1920 married Magda Angelus. Perished by shooting in August 1941.

In the upper right corner, a house with large glass windows, a balcony, a staircase and an archway, towards which a man in a hat is walking, holding by the hand a small girl in a yellow dress. In the upper left corner, the silhouette of a town in reddish-brown and ochre tones, with a sculpture on a pedestal in the middle of the square.
df90dfc782aa545ab0bcb80c8b36f810221f997e: He received his basic training from his artist father Johannes Hau in Tallinn. From 1830 he studied for a couple of years at the Dresden Art Academy. In 1836 he came to Tartu, where he began his large series of professors' portraits (Sammlung von Portraits der Professoren an der Kaiserlichen Universität zu Dorpat seit dem Jahre 1837 nach dem Leben und auf Stein gezeichnet von E. Hau), which was printed in 1837–1839 at G. Fr. Schlater's lithography workshop (a total of 6 issues with 30 portraits). In 1839 he left Tartu, probably soon moving to Saint Petersburg, where he worked mainly as a portraitist and later as an interior painter, depicting in watercolour the interiors of the imperial palaces in Saint Petersburg and its surroundings. In 1854 he became an academician. He died in Tartu.
bd1e5695906151254604f2923160938d811d251b: A sketch-like composition of two figures with a window behind them. The half-figure at the left edge of the painting is painted in a frontal view. In a reading pose, the head turned slightly to the right, resting on the hand. The half-figure in the foreground, in the centre, slightly to the left, is in profile, facing right, the right hand, bared to the shoulder, supports the head. The left is stretched forward onto the table. The window surface mainly occupies the upper right part of the painting. Through the window, indistinct outlines of trees and landscape can be discerned. The colouring of the painting consists of strong pink-green tones. The figures' clothing is white, marked with green. The narrow table between the two figures is light: greenish-white. The part of the room is ochre-brown. The window surface is pink.
654272554ee38e0485616849f1df899fa43ee51c: Üllar Varik (1961) works as a planner and designer at the design company Varik Projekt. He began his art studies at the decorators' studio of the Kohtla-Järve Oil Shale Combine (1980), later continuing his education at the Tartu correspondence art courses (1983) and in Finland at the Lestinjokilaakson Taidepäivät courses (1992-1994). He has been head of the Põlva Art Club (1992-1994) and Põlva town artist (1993). He was awarded the main prize of the Põlva „Järve“ exhibition (1992). He has compiled and edited two art catalogues: Andres Sütevaka's „Väike ja vihane“ (2011); Herman Talvik's „Ma põlen“ (2016). Üllar Varik has participated in exhibitions since 1990, and his paintings and prints are held in private collections in Finland, Sweden and Estonia.
dfc9ad11b3856d0838f898ebb4ea3c35336dc6cd: A fantasy landscape given from different viewpoints: in the foreground lies a naked red-haired woman on bright green grass thickly studded with wild strawberries. On the left, on a limestone bank, two lilac-pink columns ending in spheres and pyramids, between which crouches a lion-headed human figure in a green translucent robe. In the middle, between fields covered with snow and bare trees, a wide river flows towards a bright blue sea on the horizon. On the right, on the shore of the sea, the tiny ruins of the Pirita convent throwing out flames, and behind them a gigantic naked man in the pose of a thinker. As if beyond the sea and the horizon, the topographically distorted silhouette of Toompea appears like a dream city. At the top edge, a yellow and lilac-blue sky.
9cfe85161e43a58b32f9dfb38b9d909c34d784ee: Kruuse (b. 1959) considers art to be visual poetry. But poetry does not speak only of what is beautiful and good. According to Kruuse, it is important to notice small things, details, which, through their great impact, are no longer small things. In his paintings, Kruuse addresses the individual's relationship with society, with nature, with another person, and the destructive behaviour of man towards nature, that is, towards himself. The artist invites us not to rush, not to shuffle through life like a yellowing leaf. He mainly paints with oil and acrylic paints on canvas, and some works are also made on wood that is decades old. In that case, the wood becomes a second creator alongside him. Lately he has been experimenting by combining photographs he has taken himself with acrylic.
736af0edf452efba0a35e790b1077cac0e4e887a: Mari-Liis Rebane (b. 1988) has worked in the sphere of audiovisual culture as a thinker, idea initiator, curator and critic. From 2013 to 2015 she headed the largest international animated film festival in the Baltic countries, considering her main goal to be expanding and redefining the concept of animation and linking animation with other fields of art. She has taken part in audiovisual field festivals as a foreign expert (jury member of Ars Electronica 2016, moderator of the Prix Forums panel discussion of the «Radical Atoms» festival). In 2015 she began studies at the Estonian Academy of Arts' department of new media, focusing on sound art (supervisor Raul Keller).
1868974cfc34aa34d1d63ee1e8fbf89ad9a83db6: Various shapes are arranged somewhat chaotically on a red surface. In the upper third of the middle part of the painting there is a slightly relief quadrangle with a purplish tint, diagonally bisected by a relief line. The quadrangle is connected to a stair-like shape located on the left. At the bottom, in the left margin, there is an irregular quadrangle composed of several rectangles in pink-purple and red colour nuances. Slightly to the right of the middle of the painting there are two shapes. Below is a red triangle with a reddish-white square on it. To the right of it is a tall, trapezoid-like bluish-red shape, from which grows a relief looped arched line culminating in a glowing red painted rectangle. In the lower right margin there is a blue edge.
997a9f96cc25bd6a35c73b957ae1f23b40c86e5b: Born into the family of a customs official, in 1897 the family moved to Tallinn; in 1914-1915 he travelled in France, Spain and Scandinavia. In 1915-1919 Reindorff worked at a securities printing house in Petrograd and Moscow. In 1920 he opted for the Republic of Estonia. In 1920-1943 he was a lecturer at the State School of Applied Art, initially a teacher, from 1922 head of the printmaking workshop, and in 1936 head of the printmaking department. He founded the school's printmaking class, the lithography workshop (1920) and the printing and zincography workshop (1923). In 1922-1932 he worked as a consultant in cooperation with the State Printing House, and also worked with the advertising agencies Ilo, Ole and Gravis. In 1932 he was a founding member of the Applied Art Society RaKÜ. In 1950-1958 he was a lecturer at ERKI (EKA) (professor in 1951)
406e40ae4e2283f641ce4608edd3320e3ee93227: Gudrun Heamägi is a visual artist who mostly uses printmaking, photography and installation media in her works. Her creative output can be characterized by a poetic and narrative approach. She is interested in endless narratives that constantly repeat in time like mythical snakes devouring their own tails. She graduated from the master's programme of the Graphic Art Department of the Estonian Academy of Arts in 2013, and continued her studies at Aalto University in Finland. In 2019, she was the laureate of the Wiiralt Prize. Her works are in the collections of several galleries, art centres and other international institutions. Gudrun Heamägi is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association, the Estonian Association of Printmakers and the offset lithography workshop "Ubu Noir".
2b105dd23d4eb94217cfb32baa3cfe1ea5b40067: Sofi Aršas (1965) is a glass artist who deals in her work with situations related to a sense of danger and security, both in a general and personal context. Recently her sphere of interest has been the expression of the sensory experiences of different spaces, the objects found in them, relationships lived through, and also dreams. Aršas has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally, and is one of the people expanding the boundaries of Estonian contemporary glass art, having curated several exhibitions. She graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in glass art (1992) and currently teaches at the Tallinn Art School and in her own studio Mustvalge. Aršas is a member of the Estonian Glass Artists' Union and the Estonian Artists' Association.
0863c2f0a1da57fba39e93853cc52ba74a9ccbaa: A dense mass of people depicted with broad brushstrokes in contrasting colour tones, with four figures standing out more clearly. In the centre foreground, seen from the right side, head in half-profile facing right, a three-quarter figure of a young woman with long, straight hair and a high, light forehead, a shapeless white object on her shoulder, which she supports with her right hand. Next to her on the left, a young woman similar to the previous one, head tilted to the right side, in half-profile facing left. The latter's head is partly hidden by the face of a young man wearing glasses (turned slightly to the right). At the right edge, the smiling face of a young man, in half-profile facing right. Yellow sky, bordered on the left by a blue and on the right by a greenish-grey rectangular area.
b4352ffc959938f75530231c13ef35e66e251b4c: He received his art education from his father, the Stuttgart court artist and keeper of the Ludwigsburg painting gallery, Johann Friedrich Grooth. He worked in Dresden, Danzig and Prague. He came to Tallinn at the invitation of the Governor-General of Estland, W. von Loewendael, and moved on from there to St. Petersburg, where he became court artist to Regent Anna Leopoldovna and, after 1741, to Empress Yelizaveta Petrovna. In 1742, together with L. Caravaque and I. Vishnyakov, he took part in decorating Moscow for Yelizaveta's coronation festivities. From 1743 he was keeper and restorer of the imperial art collection, and was also involved in expanding it. From 1743 his brother, the animal painter Johann Friedrich Grooth (1717-1801), also worked in Russia.
17abb6fcac152a9abb27c4ac3c5d6b982321410e: Hando Tamm (b. 1980) graduated from the painting department of the University of Tartu in 2004. Tamm began exhibiting in 1999, his first solo exhibition took place in 2000 in Tartu at the Sebra gallery. Already during his studies he began working as a performance artist, appearing then and later both in groups and as a solo performer. His painting is characterised by an expressive yet sensitive treatment of colour, in both figurative and abstract forms. Characteristic is a humorous or slightly ironic approach to chosen objects. Member of the Tartu Artists' Union since 2013. As a painter Tamm has so far had 12 solo exhibitions and has taken part in numerous joint exhibitions both in Estonia and elsewhere.
f0a635a8ebafb85bf10765bb0e694afb81d0fa09: A painting reminiscent of a family portrait from the turn of the century, depicting a family sitting on a bench in front of a house, posing for the photographer. On the left the father of the family in a dark suit, holding a flat oval object on his knees, next to him a larger boy, in front of whom a long fair-haired child sits on a small bench, wearing a sailor suit; next to the boy the mother of the family, in a white dress, with a baby in her lap; next to the mother stands a small boy in a sailor suit, his left hand on a toy horse. In the background on the left, along the white wall of the house, reddish bricks, a pile of pipes, a flowering bush and a number of various ceramic vessels. The upper half of the painting depicts a view of a rural area, with two farmhouses between a white building with two tall chimneys. Predominantly pale green tones.
c8857e283c6ec5de84d5bb61b07bb797a51c92f2: A group of figures consisting of five parts, spatially imitating Eduard Ole's painting "Reisijad". The side directly following the painting consists of two parts and depicts a group of four seated figures, three men and one woman; only the man on the right is fully modelled in the round, the remaining figures are painted onto the bronze surface, with the knee, the left hand and the hat formed as a separate part. The part supporting the four figures (like passengers on a train, backs facing each other) consists of three separate details, depicting a man and women sitting; of these, one woman and the man are modelled in space, while the flat, unmodelled-faced woman holds a plate depicting a copy of E. Ole's painting.
f05190fbf52bdcb8c0efdfbd672426c5ac395da7: The photo-film remixes archival photographs from the Kreenholm Manufaktuur with a radio play based on Elfriede Jelinek's play "What Happened After Nora Left Her Husband or Pillars of Society". Black-and-white propagandistic photographs from the 1950s–1960s of women working in the textile industry are placed in the context of the play's 15th scene, in which Nora has come to the factory to warn the female workers of the company's impending closure and to call on them to embrace emancipation. The work was part of the exhibition package of the 2012 Manifesta art biennial, for which Marge Monko was awarded the internationally prestigious Henkel Art Award, established to support contemporary art in Central-Eastern Europe.
c516a6c2c04377dfcc2719b920b82fc21002a842: Mark Antonius Puhkan (b. 1994) is an Estonian freelance artist, graphic artist, illustrator and lecturer. He has obtained a Bachelor's degree in Graphic Art and a Master's degree in Contemporary Art from the Estonian Academy of Arts. In his free artistic practice he has exhibited in galleries mainly in the mediums of drawing and printmaking, both in Estonia and abroad. As an illustrator he is active in the fields of fiction, journalism and scientific illustration alike. He is a lecturer of graphic art and drawing subjects at the Estonian Academy of Arts. In his artistic position, an important place is held by the observation of being human and the recreation of physical and mental bridges between man and wild nature.
6606e8e7301108af6cd8158a78437740d548e93a: An early-spring cityscape with bomb explosions and fires, in the background on the left wind generators, a group of panel buildings and a cloud of smoke from an explosion, on the right a tower carrying a high-voltage line and a panel building. In the foreground a wasteland lined with bare trees, with metal containers, aircraft wreckage and a herd of pigs under the trees. Brownish colour scheme, in the background a partly cloudy evening sky. The work belongs to the competition project "Makrorajoon" of the Estonian exposition at the 13th Venice Architecture Biennale, in which Kadarik Tüür Arhitektid continue the discussion on the theme of the development of Lasnamäe. The series presents a fragment of a Lasnamäe district, whose landscape has been turned into a productive and locally functioning macro-neighbourhood.
754c0c2d0f1a2e4f0fbdc7da9dd7174349c742e4: A Baltic-German man of letters, Estophile and pastor. His father was a postmaster. He worked as a pastor in the congregations of Tori and Pärnu. From 1813 to 1832 he edited the first scholarly serial publication on Estonian subjects, the journal Beiträge zur genauern Kenntniss der ehstnischen Sprache. Under his leadership a theatre building was built in Pärnu in 1821. In 1814 he founded a school for Estonian schoolmasters in Pärnu, which was the first known pedagogical institution where teaching was conducted in Estonian. He published schoolbooks and organised the staging of the first plays in Estonian. With the help of pupils and confirmands he collected folklore. For decades he was engaged in collecting and bibliographing Estonian-language books and manuscripts.
45e948117928f6eb12a4530c3963278ee2e1f355: Elo-Mai Mägi (1989) has obtained Bachelor's degrees in Semiotics and in Painting from the University of Tartu, as well as a Master's degree in Painting there, and has furthered her studies in painting and textile art within the ERASMUS+ programme at the Strzemiński Academy of Fine Arts in Łódź, Poland. Her main medium is oil painting. Her work frequently features the psychological (self-)portrait and the abstracted figure, drawing inspiration from psychological-emotional states, illnesses, or, more philosophically, from being human, normality and the like. She has been a member of the Estonian Painters' Union since 2014, of the Tartu Artists' Union since 2017, and of the Estonian Authors' Society.
b5a38c09c786f8cd0eb9bec1913ef67ca253a0c8: singer (baritone); ETL 1945; 1930 Pärnu Boys' Gymnasium; 1938 TK (A. Arder's class); was a soloist of the Vienna Volksoper in 1938–39, of the Kassel State Opera in 1942–1943, and of "Estonia" in 1940–41 and 1944–1988; worked from 1940, with interruptions, as a lecturer at TK; professor from 1947; performed outside Estonia; was also known as a chamber and oratorio singer; also appeared in film, and several films were made about him; first place at the international singing competition in Vienna in 1938; Honoured Artist of the ESSR 1945; People's Artist of the ESSR 1952; People's Artist of the USSR 1954; Soviet Estonian Prize in 1949, 1959, 1967; since 1993 a fund named after him has operated at the Estonia Society to support voice students, and singing competitions are held
4854561aca9a84ad323d85977a851a5baad083e1: A composition rich in narrative, genre-scene detail, in bright, sharp tones and contrasting light-dark gradations. In the middle ground, at the centre of the painting, a green forest conveyor beside wagons running diagonally from the right edge to the middle. In the right foreground, in half-profile facing right, a man with a bared upper body binding logs; to the right a man in profile facing right with a boat hook; to his right and slightly further forward, in half-profile, a man bent forward facing right with a hand-held chainsaw. On the left edge, in the middle ground, a small pile of logs, fuel tanks and a shed. In the background, from the middle to the right edge, and on the left edge over a width of a quarter of the painting, forest. Simplifying modelling of forms.
2460d10ccf4309d36d61cd7a88f98c4a7c792f1e: In the mouth of a cave opening to the left, on a small plateau falling steeply backward on the right, in a pose of stepping out of the cave, a bearded, naked male figure - Heracles. On his head and shoulders a large lion skin forming a headcover and a loosely hanging cloak. In the raised right hand of the strongly muscled hero, resting on his shoulder, a large wooden war club; his left hand, stretched downward, drags after him a large, resistant, three-headed dog with bared fangs - Cerberus. The background consists of the cave's walls and ceiling - dark in tone at the top, lightening downward into a red glow of hellfire visible beyond the edge of the cliff. Beyond the visible cave mouth on the left, a darkening sky can be seen.
593e8050d5b8f44dffca54d879c94b969e57ccf2: A dim tavern room with grey walls and a low ceiling, with a six-paned window in the back wall. In the middle of the room a brown tavern counter with bottles. Behind the counter, in bright light, the innkeeper and two glass-doored cupboards. On the left a door, above which hangs a picture. A peasant is looking in through the doorway. On the right a low door with a picture above it; in front of the door sit an old man with a cane and a younger man in a wide-brimmed hat, engaged in conversation. In the middle two peasant men in coats converse leaning with their backs against the tavern counter; of the two conversing, the one on the left is shown side-on, leaning on the counter with his elbows. In the lower left corner a wooden bench with clothes and a wooden vessel. Under the window, baskets with bottles stacked on top of one another. From the ceiling hangs a burning oil lamp with a large round shade.
f7adaf1aca470730cf7a3826e5f343d02e43bab3: A late-summer suburban view, in the background a large rusting industrial building and two panel buildings, in the foreground a sunflower field, bordered by a meadow lined with apple trees and a lower group of buildings. In the area between the sunflower field and the meadow, sheep and shepherds on horses; in the tall grass of the meadow, fully equipped soldiers. A late-summer warm colour scheme, in the background a yellowish evening sky. The work belongs to the competition project "Makrorajoon" of the Estonian exposition at the 13th Venice Architecture Biennale, in which Kadarik Tüür Arhitektid continue the discussion on the theme of the development of Lasnamäe. The series presents a fragment of a Lasnamäe district, whose landscape has been turned into a productive and locally functioning macro-neighbourhood.
40154d378f86e8f63b0a09aff72e41b2f80e710c: A surrealist depiction of a cross-section of a gable-roofed house. In the picture, in the front centre, the half-figures of a married couple face the viewer, on the sides wall-height children's faces bound the space. In the house, symmetrically, four small-paned windows with a bright landscape view. In front on the left a round table with a roast, further back on the right a drum piano surrounded by beings. In the centre of the dark ceiling, at the tip of the gable, a wide-open mouth is depicted, teeth bared, a muscular hand-wing in the form of an appliqué on the right, a skeletal part on the left. On both sides, at the border of the ceiling and wall, movable depictions of a hand holding a sword. The picture also contains a number of drawn/painted, three-dimensional details. The composition is bordered with wooden strips, the backing paper is fastened with adhesive tape.
513c1285808559536b28e16618ad6e007b41b024: In the centre, a young woman with long dark curly hair, in profile facing right, in a black trouser suit and a wide-brimmed hat. The figure is cropped at knee level. The head is turned slightly to the left, the gaze directed forward. The woman has sparkling eyes, a smiling mouth. With her right hand she is bouncing a small white ball. Behind her, on the left, in blue trousers, a semi-nude figure in a three-quarter turn to the left, left hand raised to the back of the neck. On the chrome-green background, on the left, a figure can be discerned, a white vase with plant motifs standing on a pedestal. Below in the background whitish flecks, at the lower edge colourful, energetic brushstrokes. Painted at places pastosely with short brushstrokes, at places with broad smooth palette-knife strokes.
2c8bf08cc114aae12f6162ff1282f412f3b2e162: He practised tonal woodcut, drawing and painting. He became known for the monument to J. Kapp and the woodcut depicting J. Köler's sarcophagus. His woodcut-technique caricatures and decorations appeared in the years 1899-1908 in the Viljandi newspaper "Rahvaleht", in the supplement "Ulak" of the newspaper "Kodumaa" (title decoration) and in the supplement of "Postimees". Also in the holiday albums published by J. Ploompuu, and in the Russian picture magazine "Нива". He painted portraits of cultural figures and society activists of Suure-Jaani and its surroundings. He designed the flag of the Suure-Jaani Fire Brigade Society and the stage curtain of the fire station. Of his reproductive graphic works, the most well-known and technically most successful is the woodcut of I. Repin's painted portrait of L. Tolstoy.
f8ad978729bdb97f6a622466e7e51ce7224ea77e: Orest Kormašov (1964) is a painter, icon scholar and restorer. His paintings are inspired by nature, people and moments of everyday life, but reflect deeper layers of life and offer food for thought. Kormašov graduated from ERKI in the field of painting (1990), obtained a master's degree in art history at Tallinn University (2001) and worked for a long time at the Institute of Art there. He has participated in exhibitions and also organised them, published articles, worked on the conservation of ancient Russian icon art, and since 2014 has been conducting a number of thematic tours at the Icon Museum. Kormašov is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
3a061ccdd18531f80dfecca6d6f12c1c83b642d6: Nelly Drelli's (b. 1979 in Tallinn) work stands out for its bold and realistic treatment and abundance of figural compositions. She is not afraid to experiment with different art styles – so among her paintings one can find hyperrealistic cityscapes, national-romantic festive scenes, as well as all manner of other styles, from baroque to classicism. The artist is equally versatile in her choice of themes; her works include colourful sporting events, dramatic scenes from history, playful nudes, expressive portraits and landscapes in equal measure. The treatment of form and choice of motifs vary, but the main focus – people depicted harmoniously – remains.
9774d6a58ba1a190f8b137da7f521368ac85d333: In the foreground on the right sits a female figure on red cushions on a golden chair, the body in a 1/4 turn to the left. The left hand is raised. The woman is wearing a brownish draped garment, above her head a golden halo, on which is written in Cyrillic "Maria". On the left stands an angel in a 3/4 turn to the right, in a dynamic pose. The angel holds a thin staff in one hand, the other is raised to bless Mary. On the angel's halo is written in Cyrillic "Gabriil". He wears a red cloak, under which a greenish robe, wings in red and green. The background to the figures consists of two buildings, on the left red, on the right green, the background brownish-gold. In the upper part the symbol of the Holy Spirit – a small white dove heading towards the dove.
9c0f636203783aa5678d0d3de1475ee5a6db4bda: A street scene seen from an interesting angle, where human figures are shown to the chest or waist. In the foreground on the left, a stout old woman in a long grey robe and grey boots, in her left hand a book with purple covers and a basket filled with eggs and vegetables. To the left of the old woman, a beggar in rags, cap held out, asking for alms. On the right, a lady in silk stockings, black patent-leather shoes and a dark blue skirt, towards whom walks a gentleman in a solid grey suit, with gloves and a walking cane. On the right edge a billboard post with a tattered green announcement, in the foreground a pink cigarette box lying on the street and a white dog with a red bow. The background is a wall of red brick.
dc098b088d45e0c06abd999833567831040b3af9: A late-autumn cityscape, at the centre of which a large rusting industrial building, around it bare trees and lower buildings, and in front a meadow, in whose tall grass a yellow excavator and a group of fully equipped soldiers. The colour range is late-autumn warm, the sky menacingly dark and cloudy. The work belongs to the competition project "Makrorajoon" of the Estonian exposition of the 13th Venice Architecture Biennale, in which Kadarik Tüür Arhitektid continue the discussion on the theme of the development of Lasnamäe, sketching through virtual reality the future of a district that carries a Soviet utopia. The series presents a fragment of a Lasnamäe quarter, whose landscape has been transformed into a productive and locally functioning macro-district.
010d380ac81e9a07906912b9f6aa8e2689d62298: A seaside fish-cleaning scene: in the centre foreground, between barrels, sits a barefoot woman in a beige blouse and skirt, a white headscarf tied at the nape of her neck, her hands rummaging in a nearby box filled with fish. The woman has an apron in front and a cutting board with a knife and fish scraps on her knees. On the left, a young woman with an apron and headscarf supports a box heaped with fish on a barrel. Behind the woman on the left a net shed. Next to the shed, in the middle ground, stands a thin old man in half-profile, a cap on his head and a pipe in his mouth. In the lower right corner sits a light-coloured dog, its head hidden under the fish boxes. In the background on the right the sea and a shoreline with boats, with boats drawn up onto the shore. The texture is pastose in places.
29a7bd2bc3d2ff69723e14531298cefd67e83c28: Hanna Piksarv (b. 1989) is a sculptor and visual artist, who obtained a master's degree in sculpture in 2015 at the Estonian Academy of Arts. Since 2009, Hanna Piksarv has participated in group exhibitions in Estonia and Austria; in recent years the main focus has been on collaborative projects and solo exhibitions. Among them the solo exhibition "Hea ja halg", dealing with the theme of body, time and work, at the Tartu Art House in 2014, and the project "Excellence in Ebensee", weighing the values of craft, within the framework of the Festival of Regions programme in Austria. A currently ongoing project dealing with the synergy of thinking and handiwork will likewise reach audiences in both Tallinn and Vienna.
9adcc216d6bb3311233f02950f76369750eb28a2: A geometrically generalised composition of colour planes. In the foreground, two branches of a greyish-blue river flowing together from the left golden section and the right corner; between them, in the foreground, a green headland on a dark brown (unprimed canvas) surface; on the horizon the river narrows into a horizontal streak. In the middle ground on the right, a mass of trees as a large brown (unprimed canvas) colour plane, in front of it a smaller pinkish-beige deciduous tree. In front on the left an articulated riverbank in brown tones (unprimed canvas), with a greenish-grey and muted greyish blue-green mass of trees. On the horizon, above the skyline and partly on the water surface, greyish-blue colour planes. A greyish-white sky.
a6a9814caee37254d06a8decfc97c82e5ace7cfc: Stanislav Antipov (b. 1976 in Izhkar, Udmurtia) graduated from the art department of Udmurt State University in 1998 and obtained a master's degree at Tallinn University in 2008. Since 1996 he has participated in more than 50 solo and group exhibitions in Udmurtia, Estonia and Finland. He is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Painters' Association. Stanislav Antipov's works can be found in the J. Laidoner War Museum, the Estonian Health Care Museum, the Kihnu Museum, the Udmurt State Museum, the Pushkin State Museum, and in private collections in Estonia, Russia, Germany, Spain, the Czech Republic, the USA, France, Switzerland, Italy and the United Kingdom.
44848bfe399983707ec33a849a98096ab97a3576: In the foreground, shallow water, into which, from the shore in the centre, a young dark-haired woman is stepping, lifting with her right hand her red-bodiced skirt, in front of which is an apron. On the apron, at the upper and lower edges, a broad appliqué embroidery. She wears a blouse with a deep neckline, on her neck a two-row coral bead necklace. In her left arm's crook an empty red copper water jug, on her head a flat-bottomed basket in which sits a fair-haired child. Next to the woman, on the left, a dark-haired little boy stands with his feet in the water, with his right hand lifting his shirt above his navel, with his left holding onto the woman's skirt. In the background a mountainous landscape; on the left a large deciduous tree casts some shade on the group of figures, the picture is generally sunny.
203d032f810141dc724ef86bd427c40813d2969b: August Joost (2003) is a painter who works mainly with figurative oil painting. He tries to understand whether historical painting techniques and forms of viewing can say something about contemporary bodies, values, games and realities. He wants to depict the violence necessary to fit into the normative bodily ideal, as well as a body collapsing under the weight of its own meaning. He graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts, Painting speciality, in 2026, and has received the EKA Young Artist's Prize in 2026, the Young Painter Prize in 2025, and the Astrid and Arnold Kalmus Memorial Fund scholarship in 2025. He is currently studying in the Estonian Academy of Arts' Contemporary Art master's programme.
b51b7e0b0575b98e35b296ba85a3cd192a3da35e: Figural composition: of men bathing in a river and women peeking at them from a barred building. In the foreground on the right side, the surface of the river water in which the bathing men are frolicking. 32 naked men in various positions are depicted swimming in the water, splashing water, sitting on the shore, lying down, wrestling. The men have been depicted rather realistically, mainly in pinkish-brown tones. The genitals are also painted in detail. In the lower left corner of the painting, viewed from above, is depicted a room with barred windows and an open upper part, where 3 women in hats and long costumes are peeking at the swimming men with binoculars. On top of the wall lie 7 red bricks with a bell.(eesti)
c5d4e8ce642663704a16bf43b1ef07b6dc33dcbf: Oskar RAUNAM (1914, Paide – 1992, Tallinn) was an Estonian painter and pedagogue who created realistic landscape, flower and portrait paintings as well as figural compositions; he also published several textbooks, e.g. "Akvarellimaal" (1952) and "Joonistamise ja maalimise õpik" (1961, 1963). Raunam obtained his art education in the decoration painting speciality at the State School of Applied Arts, in the drawing and draughting teacher speciality at the Tallinn Pedagogium, and in the painting speciality under the guidance of Johannes Greenberg at the State Higher Art School. He worked at ERKI as a teacher of drawing and painting, as vice-rector for study and research, and as head of the general painting department. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
f870d877bc6ea1b1d8e2ace39fa7ba4b79ede8f8: Armenian mountain landscape. From the lower left corner, running diagonally in relation to the composition, a road runs as a deep track into a deep narrow valley, with a greenish slope in the background on the right side, cutting into a flat, spacious plateau and conditionally dividing it into two parts in the composition: a pinkish field in the background, and in the foreground on the right a triangular strip of land covered with large stones. On this, at the edge of the picture field, a fragment of a light two-storey wooden pile dwelling with a balcony with a balustrade on the second floor, on which red plants are drying on a line. The road, on which a lone woman is walking, is bordered on the left by high cliffs. On the horizon on the right, a bluish flat mountain.
bbbd2c90d51d3c5a2ce05ff46c9eeb27df2f5f18: Vjatšeslav Semerikov was born in Russia in 1949. He graduated in 1977 from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in the speciality of graphic art. His main fields of creative work are free and applied graphic art, book design and painting. He has participated in numerous joint exhibitions since 1988 and has also organised solo exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad. His works are in galleries and private collections in Estonia, Russia, Finland, France, Italy, Greece, the United States of America, Japan, Sweden and the Netherlands. Vjatšeslav Semerikov is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and of the Association of Russian Artists operating in Estonia. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
db363f741be671c8ff2ea31f6b7116506263ec7f: During a festive ceremony in the assembly hall of the University of Tartu. On the north wall of the hall, palms are placed on both sides of the lectern. A speaker at the lectern, with two students standing guard of honour on either side of him. Facing the lectern, the audience is seated. Ten rows of chairs, plus seats arranged in a semicircle on both sides of the lectern. A beadle with a staff stands by the door. Uniformed students stand along the sides of the assembly hall. Above the lectern, a life-size portrait of Tsar Nicholas I in a baroque gilded frame. On the left, on a wall fitted with doors, a life-size portrait of Alexander I. Columns with Ionic capitals support a balcony full of ladies. Garlands are attached to the columns and to the lower edge of the balcony. (eesti)
665f4ebbd0617b516ba82443ffe014ff06fbefd9: Estonian watercolourist, poster artist, stage designer. Lived in Yugoslavia, the family moved to Estonia in 1922. Pilar received his general education on the Adriatic coast in Kotor, and in Haapsalu and Tallinn at the Russian Municipal Gymnasium. He studied art in 1935-1938 in A. Kaigorodov's studio and in 1938-1941 at the State School of Applied Arts. In 1941 he was mobilised into the Red Army, and in 1942-1944 he was in Yaroslavl, where he was the administrator of the Estonian SSR State Art Ensembles. At the end of World War II he lived in Tartu and was engaged in founding and managing the local branch of the applied art centre. In 1944–1948 he made decorations and costumes. Having settled in Tallinn, he was responsible secretary of the Estonian SSR Artists' Union in 1959–1962 and 1969–1971.
7ea56526c53dea2078d20047df07b9a5efa55115: Created free sculptures, tomb monuments and Soviet monuments. F. Sannamees was in 1927 the author of one of the more artistically mature War of Independence monuments, the Reaal Boy. In 1929 he took part in exhibitions introducing Estonian art in Helsinki, Paris, Lübeck, Kiel and Königsberg, and in 1930 in Berlin, Cologne, Copenhagen. In 1937 Sannamees's work "Mother with Child" (plaster) decorated the Baltic pavilion at the Paris World Exhibition, he took part in an exhibition of Estonian art in Kaunas, and a solo exhibition was held at the Tallinn Art Hall. In 1939 he took part in exhibitions of Estonian art in Rome, Budapest, Warsaw, Kraków, Antwerp. In 1943 he was named Estonian SSR Honoured Art Worker, in 1946 he was awarded the Order of the Red Banner of Labour.
ed88daf0d65c0e2ec8bfbb26e45ab3b04680d9e7: Esti Kittus (born 7 April 1948 in Tartu) is an Estonian theatre artist and art teacher. She studied in 1963–1966 at the Tartu Art School and graduated in 1966 from the Tartu Evening Secondary School and in 1972 in the speciality of theatre artist-pedagogue from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute (supervisor Mari-Liis Küla). Kittus worked from 1972 to 2003 as an artist at the Vanemuine Theatre. She has also designed the Tartu song and dance festivals. In 2004 she founded the Puka Art School and worked there until 2021. She is a member of the Estonian Theatre Union (1974), the Estonian Association of Stage Designers (1993; honorary member) and the Estonian Artists' Association (1995). She also belongs to the Tartu Artists' Union.
dcded4e1eab369e199e6d6c74f6010084d859328: A small-town landscape painted in muted broken tones, with details and colour shades melting into an overall tone within forms bordered by a dark thick contour, viewed from a high viewpoint. In the foreground below, a grey greenish-blue river with two small sailboats floating side by side. In the middle ground on the riverbank, low stone buildings with orangish-red roofs: on the left a building with a four-sided little tower behind it; in the middle a building with a stepped roof and a four-sided little tower, connected by a low wall with a gateway opening; on the right a low colonnade with a roof on a terrace. Behind the buildings, two large deciduous trees. In the background on a hill, a medieval fortress with densely arranged defence towers.
67a995f46af2eb4573d785f604340dfeae109b1c: Aleksander Koemets was born in Moscow into a factory worker's family; at the beginning of the First World War his father returned with his son to his native land, Estonia, where A. Koemets received his elementary education in Võru and Pärnu. After finishing evening secondary school in Tartu in 1931, he studied from 1936 at the State School of Applied Arts, graduating in 1941 from the J. Koort State School of Applied Art. He furthered his education in France and Belgium. He was mobilised into the Red Army, was a front-line combatant in the Second World War, and was wounded. He continued his art studies and graduated in 1948 from the Art Institute (EKA) as a book graphic artist. He was an art editor at the publishing house Ilukirjandus ja Kunst, and from 1957 to 1970 chief artist of the publishing house Kunst.
e50cfd0147235179868ab770dba1ef7238bd8a71: Elfriide Maran (1905–1997) began her art studies in 1916–1918 at the School of Applied Arts in Pskov, in the ceramics speciality, studied painting in the early 1920s in Tartu in Konrad Mägi's studio, and worked for years as a seamstress of women's clothing. She then began sculpture studies in 1945 at the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, graduating from the ESSR State Art Institute in 1951. In the late 1950s, her work's limited realism following nature was replaced by a freer, more generalised formal effect. She has made works mainly in ceramic techniques, more rarely using marble. The portrait genre and decorative figural sculpture predominate in her work.
0b06e1529e2e351f72026ea58913c41498925fbd: A composition of a smoking battlefield on which a contest has just ended. In the foreground in the centre, large and tall, reaching to the edge on the right, and slightly further from the viewer on the left, burnt, twisted, deformed upright piles of steel wreckage, painted with straight, in places rounded, bent sharp lines (mainly brown and black, with light blue, red, yellow, green and other colours also on the larger dark surfaces). The ground, depicted as a straight brown line up to the horizon, is covered with multicoloured patches of colour. A cloudy and smoky sky, in which light blue shows through as small patches. Between the middle and left-hand piles of wreckage, on the horizon - a burning tank.
2bbb3001d3f46cac62c797190ce0a9130abc4ad0: In a vaulted cellar, into which weak light falls from a window opening in the upper left corner, two male figures engaged in an activity in front of a half-open coffin between them. The left-hand figure, in clerical robes, holds a lantern in his right hand and a thick book in his left. The right-hand figure, apparently a young man, half-bent over the coffin, holds in his right hand some object glowing in the light of the lantern, while with his left he places something on the book held by the clergyman. From under the half-open lid of the coffin between the men, a figure that had been lying there is pushing itself up to climb out. In the background on the left, other coffins, also pried open. The sketch is done in black in the grisaille technique.
336326a001cd14e75bad3b50ff9519435fae2365: At first glance, it may seem that this is just a stage, but actually…it is not a stage. It is a sculpture. The work was completed by EKKM board member and artist Neeme Külm in the course of the TDK exhibition that took place at EKKM in 2009. It vividly demonstrates how funds for art projects can be transformed into something much more practical, which is needed at the time. Since the completion of the work of art is an adventure worthy of Ostap Bender and the symbolic exchange in the form of its miraculous transformation was an element in the structure of the work from the start, it is of course one of EKKM’s principal assets.
1a3ef6e8e9054a5d01ae355ba50ab2828494916a:
Born in St. Petersburg as the son of a Swedish father and a Russian mother. In 1916–1917 studied at the Karl May Gymnasium in St. Petersburg. Came to Estonia in 1921, graduated from the Narva Russian Gymnasium. Studied drawing in Tallinn under K. Zeidler and E. Verber. In 1926–1928 studied graphic art at the State School of Applied Art, and in 1928–1930 studied painting at Pallas in Tartu (in the studios of N. Triik and A. Vabbe). Continued his training in Paris and worked in Estonia as a painter.

He repeatedly visited the Pechory Monastery and at the age of 19 converted to Orthodoxy. After World War II he lived in Paris, entered monastic life and devoted himself to icon painting. He died at the Skete of the Holy Spirit near Mesnil-Saint-Denis in France.
38669d6121d5fc061b54733573479e2620c4e242:
From 1898–1913 he was a lecturer at the S. G. Stroganov Moscow Institute of Applied Art. In 1912 he became an academician of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, and in 1916 a full member of the Academy of Arts. From 1923 he lived in Riga.

Although he belonged to the Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions (Peredvizhniki) from 1880–89, his work (especially from the 1910s onward) is nevertheless characterised rather by the impressionist manner of the Union of Russian Artists (VKL). He was also a founding member of this society (1903). At the same time, he has also been called one of the best-known members of the Peredvizhniki group.

He painted genre scenes, portraits, interiors and landscapes, mostly in a bright and sunny plein-air style. The best part of his work was created during the period when he was active in the VKL.
6145a95a6d91c627ffd7e597861e2f30394efaae: In a realistic style, the painting shows in close-up a young couple kissing on a wooden bench. A young man with glasses, brown hair and a brown jacket is sitting and holding an open red umbrella in his right hand. His other arm is around the neck of a young woman lying in his lap. The young man's legs are wrapped around the girl's body. He is wearing blue jeans and black sneakers. The girl's head is turned 3/4 upward, her gaze glancing at the viewer from the corner of her eye. Her hair is light-coloured, she is wearing a dark dress and a whitish-grey coat. The dress is open at the front, partially revealing her breast, and her thighs are also uncovered. The background is a dark grey stone wall, brownish ground. Next to the girl on the bench is a small white down feather.
0ebca752cbdcbb8e1bea29556669abe734c60f17: Consists of 29 figurines (28 plaster + 1 stearin), painted with spray paint (car primer paint, dark grey), some covered with PVA glue, on some the costume details are painted with acrylic, 1 covered with natural yellow wool) + 1 figurine of white stearin. Height of figurines 21.5 cm; width 9.5 cm, depth 7 cm. The figurines are placed on a base covered with burgundy-red synthetic plush fabric. The base with the figurines is covered with a plexiglass dome measuring 80x80 x h 70 cm. The entire composition is surrounded by a barrier formed of four brass-toned metal posts and four barrier ropes covered with red plush. A red silk ribbon is tied around the figures.
a4e033662c2ffda15688a251285af7e5b4f664f0: The spatial installation marking the working rooms of the State Archivist consists of a larger room and a smaller room built inside it, separated by partition walls and an open door. In the larger room, along the wall in an unbroken row, are framed and glazed drawings depicting small birds in a realistic style; in the smaller room is a repository of new accessions with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves filled carelessly with book-shaped objects made from a mass of grey, crumbling waste paper; behind the shelves, in a separate corner, is the archivist's desk with a radio playing a work by J. S. Bach, glasses placed on the desk, and unfinished drawings of birds on archive forms.
80f736798c3c72a1bb0bc702e3ddefc365e9508f: Lembit Palm (1944) mainly cultivated decorative sculpture in the 1970s, interested both in the symbolic value of the work and in the expressiveness of form. His figurations and decorative sculptures reduced to primary forms have been rendered in bronze as well as in tin and stone. He has also created character portrait sculptures with lively modelling. He has extended his creative possibilities into fields such as international ice and snow sculpture symposiums and competitions, and has taken part in urban sculpture symposiums, where works, mostly of dolomite or wood, resulting from a short working process are placed in urban space.
1d3f91fcda5889bf2db23da46c4dfa53cacfee1c: Born in 1974 in Tallinn, Katrin studied fine arts at the Estonian Academy of Arts from 2005–2012. Most important recent exhibitions: "MIS VÄRVI ON ARMASTUS", Kunstiruum Gallery, Tallinn, Estonia (2021), MERRILY, MERRILY, MERRILY, Sakala Centre, Viljandi; Kõnnu Viinaköögi Gallery, Estonia (2021), IN THE LIGHT, Fruttis Gallery, Brazil, Abadiania (2021), 20th Spring Exhibition of Estonian Artists Association "Kunstnikud maalivad kunstnikke", Tallinn Art Hall, Estonia (2020), GAIA, Sargvere Manor, Estonia 2020, TROPICAL PASSION, Caminho Encantado Gallery, Brazil, Abadiania and in Kõnnu Viinaköögi Gallery, Estonia
9e2e2b47b309b7a693b002c06f5d63119c5125a0: Juhan Soomets (1975) is known above all as the author of the sound space "Kunstnike tuba" ["Artists' Room"], which has been exhibited in Tallinn, Viljandi and Riga and which brought the author the first Baltic Young Artist Prize. In his work Juhan experiments with interactivity, participatory art and user interfaces, combining low-tech elements with contemporary practices in his works. Having relinquished the position of author, the work of art comes into being either through the participation of the visitor at an exhibition, or is created from beginning to end by a generative machine (the Mandala graphic series). He graduated with an MA from the New Media Department of the Estonian Academy of Arts (2016) and with a BA as an art teacher from Tallinn University (2004).
07cb259ced2a2740521c20eb4089dcd5538d3dfa: Elisabet Kiverik is studying for a bachelor's degree in jewellery art at the Estonian Academy of Arts. She has furthered her studies in Germany at the Burg Giebichenstein University of Art and Design in Halle and in Lisbon at the Ar.Co art centre, in both cases in the field of contemporary jewellery art. Kiverik has participated in several group exhibitions, including "Lahkheli" in the Telliskivi Creative City, the Burg Giebichenstein annual exhibition in Halle, the international enamel art biennial in Vilnius, Tallinn and Sigulda, and the exhibition "Anna uus elu" at the Pärnu Museum of New Art. Her work focuses on memory objects and dreamlike narratives, in which material acts as a playful companion and guide.
bb404a90d31fff702485d594bd7bacd83047847e: The kinetic object "Oranž torn II" ["Orange Tower II"] consists of a tower-shaped body that tapers upward in stages and a brass tube positioned above it. The body grows out of a round base with a diameter of 32 cm, on which rests a rectangular block with dimensions h 83.5x19.5x19.5 cm. On top of this, in turn, is a rectangular block with dimensions h 58x7x7 cm, on the front of which are three amplifiers (the lower one also being a loudspeaker). At the top of this block is a cube-shaped part with a loudspeaker on its front. The sides of the cube are 13.5 cm long. Above the cube is a disc with a diameter of 13.5 cm, out of which emerges an upward-directed polished brass tube, on the front of which 20 small bulbs (flashlight bulbs) are lit.
57293a1c39ca7f13a943742450929c5b0597a0a6: On the left side of the sheet, depicting a fresco bounded by architectural details and sculptures, are two putti positioned one above the other. On the right, a caryatid, with braided hair around the head, supporting an entablature and a console. The caryatid is surrounded by four putti. The fresco depicts a kneeling soldier in front of a square altar, on which a fire has been lit, his head down, supporting himself on the ground with one hand. A man standing on the right is stabbing him in the neck with a spear. Another man is pressing him down and raising a dagger to strike. On the left, a soldier in a helmet and toga kneels before the altar; two armed men are standing. To the right of the altar stand lictors with bundles of rods (fasces). City walls are visible in the background.
6bbdf86fea877db565f53c4e025e7fc4e90e8a55: On a flat, abstract grey field with a low horizon, viewed from a high and close vantage point, are over-life-size vegetables — in the centre a mass of pink cabbage leaves, on the left a red beet with parsley on top of it, beside it bean pods and a section of a green cabbage head, fruits in the back. On the right, parsley leaves with carrots and a turnip. In the foreground, on each side of the composition, a slice of squash, with two table knives between them. Behind the still life, a view opens from a high horizon onto individual buildings in Tallinn: on the left the slope of Toompea and the building of the design institute, on the right the hotel "Viru" with the tower of St. Olaf's Church. A pale blue sky with whitish-grey cumulus clouds.
67c7345056824f202216397cbdf9c20d96694aa2: A street crossing of a snowy provincial town, painted in delicate, broken tones. From the lower left corner to the golden section point near the bottom of the right edge (in relation to the height) runs a snowy, wide embankment. In the foreground on the left, overturned black boats (the one closer to the viewer right side up). In the foreground on the right, a fragment of an overturned boat and a section of a low wooden protective barrier. Parallel to the street, in the background, irregularly placed greenish and greyish-brown one- and two-storey houses. On the left, a brighter green house with a mansard storey; next to it, at the left edge, a windowless pinkish-brown taller stone building. A greyish-green, darkening sky.
c3b192d38e8ecc79f06996bd6c0545ad27120240: At the ERKI, Uno Uibo studied theatre decoration painting as a student of Prof. Voldemar Haas and Natalie Mei. His diploma work in 1960 was Anton Chekhov's "The Cherry Orchard". While working at the Pärnu Lydia Koidula Drama Theatre (Endla), he designed, for example, the productions: M. Lassila's "The Wise Virgin", Lope de Vega's "The Dance Master", Th. Wilder's "Our Town", K. Saja's "Puutuvid" and others. From 1985, as a freelancer, U. Uibo practised watercolour and pastel painting (landscapes, cityscapes, flowers), participated in review exhibitions of theatre artists and held solo exhibitions in Pärnu, Tallinn and Vaasa. In recent years the artist was a valued teacher at the Pärnu Children's Art School
37a71937464e5cbb979cb1dc9d7282b23b42a92e: In the lower half of the composition, across the entire width of the picture, a table: semicircular on the right side, angular on the left, covered as if by a tablecloth with geometric colour planes. In the background on the right a green bottle, slightly in front of it, in the centre of the composition, large-flowered blossoms in reddish and greyish shades as a lush bouquet in a tall cylindrical vase. In the middle ground, in the right golden section, a large thick-walled wine goblet of blue glass, on the right a brown clay bowl with two green fruits, on the left edge two books stacked on top of each other. In the foreground, Estonian-language newspapers are used as "papiers collés". The background consists of geometric colour planes.
832e8af68179d8e84514131619ba6b9e124b2725: The fresco depicted on the sheet is bordered by architectural baroque decorations and sculptures. On the left an atlas figure with two small fauns holding cornucopias, and with two putti. On the right two putti, one above the other. The fresco depicts a violent scene. In the right foreground three soldiers in plumed helmets are attacking a bearded man in armour, whose beard one of the warriors has grabbed. A second soldier has clutched the man's hair and holds a short sword in his hand, a third pierces the bearded man with a spear. At the feet of the man being attacked already lies a lifeless old man on the ground. In the background soldiers march with flags and spears. On the left in front, three soldiers with weapons.
606276c3c3190bb7868ac16b4532b02a487d4f57: Eva Jänes (1942) graduated from the Tartu Art School in 1962 in the speciality of art teacher, and from the Estonian Art Institute in 1970 with a diploma in painting, specialising in monumental painting. In the first decades of her creative period, the artist mostly focused on monumental painting, executing numerous sgraffiti, frescoes, secco paintings, stained glass windows, and mosaics both in Tallinn and in various other places, mainly in Virumaa. In recent decades the author has devoted herself to easel painting. Jänes has arranged dozens of solo exhibitions, participated in national art exhibitions and group exhibitions, and has also put together numerous displays as a curator.
d1c5599c83056f723c19f13c010c35fef0f2f635: A figural composition, whose individual elements are more brightly lit in the night-time light. Upper right two panels with black concentric circles, of which the left one shows, from behind, a figure in a blue blouse and hat, a woman with a bright red mouth, sunglasses, and a hand outstretched in a forbidding gesture, next to whom is a bent male figure. To the right of the circles, in blue, a woman, and lower right a man with his hands raised to his mouth as if calling out. Lower left and centre, fragments of the figure of a reclining man in white trousers and a woman with bare shoulders. At the bottom centre a large crumpled wad of paper. The background is dark, with white, black and blue tones dominating.
42ef1cf69ca4d9d3d66e2d5ab15e08bda392d892: Studied at the Dresden Academy of Art. Came to Estonia in 1809 at the invitation of the writer August von Kotzebue to be a drawing teacher for his children. Later worked as a drawing teacher in Hageri at the church school founded by pastor F. Ignatius, and from 1815 at the Tallinn Cathedral School. Retired in 1850, lived at Kaiu Manor, which belonged to his daughter. He mostly painted altarpieces (in the churches of Tallinn and Kuressaare, in Ambla Church, etc.), as well as portraits; drawings depicting the ruins of St Olaf's Church after the fire of 1820 originate from him, after which lithographic sheets were also made. He founded the first lithography workshop in Tallinn. He also carried out commissions for portraits of Russian tsars and ceremonial portraits
2e86cf097c4ceb547a2071f64db491f74a10210a: A composition in frontal view with four figures. In the lower foreground, centre, the bust of a dark-haired woman painted in a lighter colouring. To her right - an infant. Behind the woman, half-figures of three standing people. On the left a man in greenish clothing, in the centre, facing front, a woman dressed in orangish-brownish tones, on the right edge a woman in yellowish-greenish clothing. The gazes of all three are directed down towards the centre. The right hand of the woman in the centre is raised above the head of the woman in the foreground. Behind the person standing on the right, a shadow in reddish tones is visible. The head of the young woman with bared shoulders in the foreground is turned slightly to the right, directed towards the infant.
6ec59a265a058445a743d053ead49c03a632fc0b: His oeuvre is divided into several different periods. The sculptures made in the 1950s belong to the finest examples of the realistic style of the time (a joint work with his wife Signe Mölder is the now-relocated monument to V.I. Lenin in Jõhvi (together with Enn Roos)). Arseni Mölder's most outstanding monumental work remains the monument to N. Pirogov in Tartu, executed in a classicist order (1952, together with Juhan Raudsepp), the bronze relief "The Battle of Assamalla" of the F.R. Kreutzwald monument (1957), and several memorial plaques executed in precious materials, among other works. His finest free-standing sculptures ("The Moulder" (1950, bronze 1964), "Relay Runners" (bronze, 1956)).
95ec2bd571a62648796bc334d8568111893fc4a3: A still life emphasising flatness through perspectival "errors", with closely placed objects viewed from several different heights in relation to different objects, set against a background of irregularly arranged geometric colour planes and on an irregularly articulated, geometricised base in various colour tones. In front, in the middle, two red fruits in a deep quadrangular vessel of flowing forms. Behind it on the left an old-fashioned hand coffee grinder, on the right a tall oriental jug with a thin, upright spout. Above, against this background, a colourful bouquet of flowers and leaves. On the table, lower left, a branch of mahaleb cherry with leaves and orangish-reddish berries.
fe6fc3519d70f436570aae9b4efa849d1108d113: Matti Pärk (b. 1945) has graduated from the Tartu Art School in the speciality of woodworking and from ERKI in the speciality of book illustrator. He has worked as the head of the art editorial department of the ENE [Estonian Soviet Encyclopaedia] and as a lecturer at the drawing department of EKA (from 1984 to the present). He has presented his drawings and pastel paintings at numerous solo exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad, and has also participated in group exhibitions. He has designed, laid out and illustrated nearly 200 books (several of which have received recognition at competitions). At the last drawing triennial, Matti Pärk was one of the nominees for the main prize. He is currently working on preparing a solo exhibition for the Kuressaare Town Hall Gallery.
6225d16ce44e1952be3944cb666d49902fa3ec13: A room with a floor of brown-coloured planks and white walls, in the middle of which stands a dark brown three-legged stool. On the stool a white round vase with cornflowers and ears of grain. In the lower right corner an easel, on which stands a landscape painting in green tones with rocks and junipers. Behind the easel a larger summer landscape, from which mainly the sky portion is visible. On the left, leaning against the wall, a landscape showing a pre-thunderstorm sky, green meadow and yellow grain field, and part of a mowing machine painted red. On the back wall of the room a landscape with fields in the foreground. Behind the fields a farmhouse with a white roof sinking into the trees, in the distance a strip of forest and a yellowish sky.
c547e8734ffa31aa8c16f7185285b58e9238740c: A large-format composition, of which about 6/7 is taken up by greenery: trees, bushes, an abundance of various plants and flowers. In the lower right quarter, three recognisably rendered light-purple asters; lower left, slightly below the horizontal centre line, four dark red rose blossoms in a rectangular vase or bottle. To its left a large glass jar with a bouquet of flowers. At the bottom edge, centre, a doll and a glass bowl with apples, to their right a single glass with a yellow flower branch. At the top edge a cityscape based on strict horizontals and verticals can be discerned. The work is painted throughout with dense brushstrokes, predominantly in dark green colouring.
a99205e96a4df26991c828dadd322ac2a00deedc: In the interior of a photography studio, two blonde, long-haired women sit on a small black sofa; the one on the right is wearing a blue dress and black high-heeled shoes. The girl's hands are in her lap. The one on the left is wearing a yellow dress, the young woman sits with one leg crossed over the other, wearing black lace-up boots, with one hand holding sunglasses at her forehead, the other hand in her lap. Leaning diagonally on the sofa is a man in pinkish trousers, a spotted shirt, a striped tie and a greyish hat, wearing glasses. To the right of the women stands a second man. He holds a light raised in his hand, dressed in black, with yellowish-greenish suspenders. The man stands in profile with his head facing front.
30baf0cc7b115cc3308cc6b8fe6d2771cd41288f: Alar Tuul (b. 1982) is one of the most recognisable and distinctive-styled artists among young Estonian authors. Tuul's automatistically naive picture surfaces, reminiscent of Karel Appel or Jean-Michel Basquiat, have over the years moved from isolated details towards ever greater generalisations. Stick figures and ring-eyed creatures have been preserved, but individual scenes no longer form a complete composition; instead they are parts of larger panoramas. Emotion (colour) has replaced calculation (line), the subconscious a clear motive, and from these views one can read out thousands of stories and construct ever new worlds.
87222ce8f2c295172476dd2b2e265e4f18aa2018: Regina-Mareta Soonsein (1991) graduated from the Pallas University of Applied Sciences in 2019 in painting, but in recent years has focused her creative work on linocut. Her authorial position encompasses the subjectification of line, the beauty of coercion and destruction, and the themes of deviation, fragmentation, introspection and archetypes. She has participated in group exhibitions, held solo exhibitions and created expositions in public social spaces since 2017. She has received the Biafarin Award at the NordArt exhibition, the Wiiralt Prize audience favourite title, the best stage design award at the I Land Sound festival, and the title of Newcomer of the Year from the Estonian Association of Independent Graphic Artists.
bdc5886af22162c4a1e299ba5205fc32aec14c5f: Mia Mai Seppel (2003) focuses her work on painting and monumental art techniques. She began her studies at the Estonian Academy of Arts in 2022, and has also studied as an exchange student at the University of Fine Arts Hamburg (HFBK). Seppel's work combines (finished) text with visual art; the word is the starting point for a search for symbols and visual rebirth. Text and image begin to give meaning to one another, the past becomes contemporary, and the contemporary in turn notes that life seems never to have changed at all. Recurring themes include corporeality, mythology, Rorschach-like mirror images, and desire as a force driving human beings.
6e676cb80d402451a1ab3af735cff288c0e509fe: Tiiu Lausmaa (b. 1989) is an artist and illustrator living in Tallinn who graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in 2018 with a bachelor's degree from the Department of Fine Arts. Her main media are painting and drawing. Her works cover a wide range of interests, such as the relationship between humans and non-human animals and nature, environmental problems, and the effects of mass production and the information age on the human mind. A large part of her life and work philosophy is inspired by Taoist texts, which she studied during her earlier studies. Her most recent solo exhibition took place at Staapli 3 gallery in June 2020.
f97717b81e5c2a17df04167830d5ffbc8c099b17: A people-free early summer street crossing. In the foreground and middle ground, a narrow street end lined with classicist buildings leading into a street running perpendicular. In the foreground on the left, a narrow two-storey house with an oriel window; next to it in the middle ground, a corner house: a tall, steep-roofed three-storey building with its upper floor lit by the early morning sun. On the right, three-storey houses, one of them with a balcony. In the background, the slope of Toompea with ochre-yellow, tall-roofed and chimneyed buildings lit by the sun. In the background below, at the foot of the hill, a mass of deciduous trees with a red house roof rising above it. A darker bright blue sky.
ec1e3e6532ac6c33947f5b4127509d9adbb6a8a2: A large figural composition with portraits of the most important Estonian artists of the older and younger generations. On the left wing, lower right, a self-portrait of E. Okas. The portraits of other artists alternate with various realia. On the left wing below, a dog and painting implements, a cake, and building structures at the upper edge. In the middle section below, a mannequin in a pink airy dress with a red wig, a glass bubble, and a nude figure above. On the right wing below, an open book with the numbers and names of the artists depicted in the picture, a quill, an owl. At the upper edge of the right wing, buildings with stairs and columns and a galloping horse. Between the portraits, plants, flowers and stalks.
737efe5ad6c15577cdbade5d17787515868c7b75: Kalevi Tamm (b. 1965 in Tallinn), after adventures and hard trials in entrepreneurship in Cuba, took a "time out" and found his calling in photography, more seriously so from 2008 onward. He considers self-education both his weakness and his strength. His main favourite themes have become architecture and street life and playing with shadows and silhouettes, while nothing else that crosses his path is excluded either. As a style, he prefers black-and-white geometric regularity. Worth mentioning are his win at the LIFE magazine international photography competition in 2011 and his participation in the SOHO Arthouse graphic and photo exhibition in New York in 2014.
fa4f2ffbbfd2ee6e9beda8a8d4db8c96d824f816: They carried torches and thyrsi and veils woven from ivy. Sometimes ivy was woven into their hair. They dressed in the hides of wild animals. The maenads sang songs praising Dionysus and wine, danced and drank wine. Together with Dionysus they wandered over mountains and through forests. They also used musical instruments: tambourines and other light percussion instruments, as well as flutes. Often, due to alcohol abuse, they fell into ecstasy and were then unaware of their own behaviour. Drunk, they feared no wild animal and attacked even lions in groups, not to mention others. They ate the raw flesh of the animals they killed.
0f8f75759f6fa07acae019176bc876e4b1df267f: Reet Heinla (born 27 August 1952 in Tallinn) is an Estonian artist whose work focuses mainly on oil paintings. She graduated from Tallinna Reaalkool and Tallinn University of Technology with a degree in economics. Heinla began painting in 2005, furthered her education at various courses and studied the techniques of watercolour, pastel and oil painting. Since 2009 she has remained faithful to oil paints, as she finds that they allow her to express herself best. She has studied oil painting at the Tartu Popular University and, since 2014, has actively participated in the activities of the art studio "Suvi" under the guidance of artist Robert Suvi.
52fbde6f3f7703a720c35f96bc84b7372710cc15: Voldemar PEIL (1907, Narva – 1999) was an Estonian theatre artist who, among other things, also practised realistic easel painting (flower and landscape pictures as well as portraits). As a stage designer he designed about three hundred productions. His style is mainly of a genre character. Alongside painted scenery, Peil also made effective use of projection and lighting. He received his art education in the painting speciality at the Pallas Art School under Jaan Vahtra, Voldemar Mellik, Villem Ormisson and Ado Vabbe, graduating from the art school with the qualification of drawing teacher. In scenography he furthered his education at theatres in Moscow and Leningrad. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
