b3dbc8a30e8997f60527993c84b60ece8caadc55: Maria Hommik, known by the artist name Marmiamum, is an artist-musician born in Võrumaa and living in Tartu. At the moment she enjoys painting with Chinese ink, to which she devoted herself in her final year at the Pallas University of Applied Sciences. Her next goal is to incorporate homemade paints that are both health- and nature-friendly, so that making art would also be good for the earthly world, not only for the spirit. She sees creative work as a good opportunity to share a unique perspective, the essence of her soul. The mystery of life, questions and a few rare answers find a place in her art and music. Marmiamum's working method is largely intuitive, improvisational, spontaneous.
ec6f302c3285587cac4ff4b6e8e96c7e5ac7b288: A print with a historical scene: the Prussian Queen Luise on her deathbed. In the centre of the picture, the queen lies in an Empire-style bed, wearing a white lace cap. At the head of the bed, the dying woman's two sons kneel. Luise gazes fixedly at the crown prince. In front of the bed, on a chair, sits the queen's husband, holding her hand between both of his. Behind the head of the bed stand two sorrowful ladies and an older man. At the foot of the bed stands a statesman with a high decoration(?), and, with his back to the viewer, another man with a tall top hat under his arm. On the left in front, a table with a fringed cloth, two flowerpots, one of them with a hydrangea. On the wall, two landscape paintings.
41cf7c18f8e6972a65efefc2fb2661fdbb30432f: On an ochre-brown background, a woman in a blackish-brown robe with a gold border, with the Christ Child on her left arm, her right hand raised in blessing. The Christ Child wears a green-gold robe, and both figures have a gold nimbus around the head. To the left and right of the Mother of God's head, and above Christ's head, symbols painted in white in Cyrillic script. On the sides of the icon, four saints are depicted one below the other: upper left, the martyr Nikita with the attributes of a hunter, below him Saint Simeon in a red-blue robe. On the right edge, upper, the martyr Agatha, below, Saint Martha in a dark cloak with a greenish robe beneath it. The figures on the edge have gold nimbuses around their heads, with their names above the depicted figures.
61b42021590fb646889fce5df6215349f796eef4: All edges of the composition are bordered by industrial forms, between which a view opens into the distance (dark red at the top, passing through orange down to yellow). Against this background, in the golden section on the left, a man seen frontally with gloved hands raised, in a sea-green undershirt with white shading and long red trousers. In the lower left corner, two large metal wheels with low teeth, with dark blue and purple reflections; in the lower right corner, five parallel S-shaped forms. In the upper right corner, a large curving ventilation pipe. Above the man's head, a metal beam with three reddish-yellow round protrusions.
5d24a353ad39c9fcb5cb468500912652a52109b9: Tiina Tammetalu (1961) prefers to define herself as an artist of fluid identity, transcending media and not to be pigeonholed, who realises herself simultaneously in several different creative fields: painting, graphic design, illustration, and, among other things, also curates exhibitions of living Estonian painting classics. Tammetalu graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in painting (1989) and furthered her education in the interdisciplinary arts master's programme at the Estonian Academy of Arts (2003–2006). She has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and elsewhere, and her works belong to several collections. She is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association
dd969fa8b6da3e5e6a1c454345cee6ffa033f6ac: Kaido Ole’s mural titled New Model appeared on the wall of EKKM in 2010 in connection with the Next to Nothing exhibition, and soon a plan was hatched to include the work in the collection. Artist Kaido Ole, understanding his limited choices – to have the work survive it would have to belong to the collection, otherwise it would just be destroyed – agreed to have EKKM store the work of art unconditionally until 7 o’clock on 23 July 2013, when three years will have passed since it was displayed to the public. Thereafter, the agreement will be reviewed and a decision made whether to renew it or not.
e67432c971bafdbc11c184cb2308ad7cba55ee04: From 1972 to 1977 he worked as an artist-copyist in the animated film group of Eesti Telefilm. In 1977 he began studies at ERKI, graduating in 1983 as a painter-pedagogue. He began participating in exhibitions in 1982. From 1983 to 1984 he worked as an artist-painter at Tallinnfilm's animated film studio. From 1984 to 1989 he was a teacher of artistic special subjects at Tallinna Kergetööstustehnikum. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1989. Works are held in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, the Tartu Art Museum, the Ministry of Culture of Russia, the Tretyakov Gallery, the Alma-Ata Art Museum and the Uzhgorod Art Museum in Kazakhstan, as well as in private collections.
8557a0d4646db2cc88dc9e67adf5ff0182f68acd: Still life with apples, pears, grapes, wine goblets and a carafe on a table. The central part of the painting consists of fruit arranged on an evenly white surface-plane. The fruit is painted three-dimensionally, realistically. Apples of different sizes and colours (6 pcs), pears (7 pcs) all of similar shape, size and colour. Apples and pears on the left side of the table, on the right side, in pinkish-purple tones, 2 wine goblets filled to the brim on one plate, behind them a wine jug in the same tones, the jug's stopper separate on the table. Bunches of grapes seem to border the aforementioned objects. Background evenly grass-green in two tones, the right side orange.
ba8f9ec5ed668c3271c7f1257d0fc748605fda4b: Viive Noor (1955) studied at the Estonian State Art Institute and has, since 1978, participated in more than 400 exhibitions in 33 countries, from America to Japan. She has had 96 solo exhibitions in total. She works with graphic art, book illustration as well as exhibition curating. In her work Noor deals mainly with universal human themes, but also touches on ecology and world events. Noor's work and activities have received numerous accolades, including the Order of the White Star, 5th Class. She is the initiator and organiser of the Tallinn Illustration Triennial and a member of the Estonian Association of Graphic Designers and the Estonian Artists' Association.
62b560e1b65c9207c31c03b2536704fbfe192226: Triin Kerge's (1986) work focuses on themes of personal and collective memory, intimacy and belonging, combining a documentary approach with a poetic and installative mode of expression. Her works interweave photography, textiles and spatial solutions, exploring human relationships and the formation of identity in time and space. Kerge holds a master's degree in contemporary art from EKA (2020) and has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad, receiving several accolades, including the special prize of the Riga Photobiennial for the publication of an artist's book (2024). Kerge is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
f0f5bf629ca5177bfc2bca38aa45f6e27361e3f5: Belliisi Seenemaa is an artist and art teacher. Belliisi has studied at the Tartu Art School in decorator-stylist specialty and at Tartu Art College Pallas – textile specialty. She has furthered her education in Berlin in the field of combining e-textiles and technologies, studied archaic leather art techniques in France, and traditional methods of processing plant fibres and dyes in Estonia. In previous years her interests have centred on symbolism, ritual themes and objects. In recent years, however, her work has focused primarily on closeness to nature, nostalgia and experimentation with pigments and minerals.
486bfee10a9d01cc1e6eedd57554e90a520f9a8f: Stanislav Netšvolodov (b. 1935 in Ukraine) is an Estonian sculptor, medallist and painter. He graduated from the Kiev Institute of Civil Engineers with a degree in architecture. Netšvolodov has created bronze, wood and stone sculptures and monuments and also works in painting and graphic art. Netšvolodov's favourite pursuit is medal art; he is the author of several medals of the University of Tartu (including the university's honorary doctorate medal and the Skytte Medal). Netšvolodov has been active in sculpture since 1962. In 2002 Stanislav Netšvolodov was awarded the Anton Starkopf Art Prize. He is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and F.I.D.E.M.
b8d399a6b36349838082210b9a81e45ae5c28794: In the foreground on the right a table covered with burgundy-red velvet, on which stands a wine glass, a white plate with grapes, a crystal jug. In the foreground on the left, behind the table, with his back to the viewer, a man playing guitar in a dark wood armchair. The man has short hair, dark bushy eyebrows and a moustache, wearing a dark blue suit and a white shirt. Opposite the man, on the other side of the table, a lady in an evening gown and fur, her head tilted, gaze gently lowered, holding a grape in her left hand resting on the table. To the right of the lady, on the wall, a mirror or painting in an oval carved frame. To the left of the man a tall dark green houseplant. The background dark grey.
4fab5a719b09240fce0c83a1781f7b02ef38830d: Born in Tallinn as the son of a merchant, he studied in Tartu under A. M. Hagen and, from 1834 to 1839, at the Dresden Academy of Art, and worked in Riga, Tallinn and St. Petersburg. In 1838 he unsuccessfully applied for the position of head of the drawing school at the University of Tartu. In 1845 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. From 1850 to 1871 he was an art teacher at the Tallinn Cathedral School, and in 1853–54 ran a photography studio in Tallinn. In 1871 he moved to Dresden. In the 1850s he made a series of watercolours depicting Coastal Swedes, which were lithographed and published in 1854–1856 in C. F. W. Russwurm's scholarly book (Eibofolke...). He also painted landscapes, genre paintings and townscapes.
94ec45b3d42953c052757a8cea940af58a40305f: A freely, thickly brushed painting with frequent impasto strokes. Two thirds of the picture surface is covered by a beach, on the right a narrow strip of sea with a small headland and bay. On the beach on the left a small house with a tall, steep roof, with a long pole leaning against the edge of the roof. At the left end of the ridge an upright pole. In the centre of the composition a spruce, beneath it an upturned boat. In the foreground two groups of sawn tree trunks; on the left two side by side, on the right two trunks resting crosswise on a thick trunk block. In the foreground on the left two lambs, behind them a woman heading left carrying a bundle of brushwood on her head. On the right, by the shore, a sailing boat and a group of people.
23044a0fb81e1f0d78ed9ee4135a902e5ee2bcea: A middle-aged man sitting at a table, facing forward, as a three-quarter figure, with a slightly smiling face, grey short hair, wearing a dark suit with a tie, hands folded in his lap, a white sheet of paper in his right hand. In the foreground, slightly diagonal, a brown tabletop with light-coloured paper, spanning the width of the image. On the table, from left to right: white sheets of paper, a dark-purplish telephone set, brown-framed glasses, a lighter, open glasses case, an open book and a yellow fountain pen. Behind the table a dark grey background, up to the upper edge of the image a light blue sky with a horizontal white cloud band, within which a round solar disc.
93ef8c3f2eacca37206cef4dcc99f711170aefe0: Kippasto has been engaged in art for 25 years and is the winner of the 2016 linocut competition. In addition to Estonia, she has sold her graphic art to Japan, America, Mexico, Ireland and elsewhere. Accolades LAULUPIDU (SONG FESTIVAL) (2014, linocut), TYPA linocut competition 2016 winning work Participation in exhibitions 2003 Tartu vaade (View of Tartu). E-kunstisalong (E-art salon) 2016 Linocut competition and exhibition. TYPA. winning work Laulupidu (Song Festival) 2018 Linocut competition and exhibition. TYPA 2018 Tartu Art Annual Exhibition 2018. Tartu Art House 2021 Linocut competition and exhibition. TYPA 2023 THKS 25 years of activity retrospective exhibition. St. John's Church 2023 New Art Museum Recycling exhibition GIVE NEW LIFE
39fe4133561b3074435f06bfa448d8260a77bebb: Merike Sule-Trubert (b. 1974) has, since 1996, appeared in numerous group exhibitions in Estonia and abroad, organised solo exhibitions and participated in several international competitions. Sule-Trubert graduated from the Graphic Art Department of the Estonian Academy of Arts in 2001; after completing her studies she has worked mainly in drawing and photography, but has also created installations and artist's books. Alongside her artistic work, Merike Sule-Trubert has supervised art students and has also taken part in the organising committee of the Tallinn International Print Triennial and the triennial seminar (2012 and 2015).
ef6bf19682405e8dd7c3e0418d3dc0050b5d2144: A single-figure composition of a soldier falling forward, chest-first, hovering in a hazy mist, dressed in a whitish-brownish-yellow summer soldier's uniform with sharp brown shadows. The legs and head dissolve into the haze, losing their tones. The legs bent, the shoulders almost in profile. Across the whole composition a T-shaped red border, at the upper edge a madder-lake-red vertical border, dividing the composition into two equal parts, with a bright red tint and in the middle a narrow dark red, partly black central stripe. In the greyish-yellowish neutral background, above, to the left of the border two bullet holes, to the right four.
257236aef75495445b247ad6c2ca9e226c404eea: A southern landscape with large trees in the background. On the left buildings with leaf-covered roofs, enclosed by a fence. In the foreground, beside a round table, sits a grey-haired gentleman in a blue coat and riding boots, embracing a barefoot boy in a brown suit who has come up to him. On the other side of the table sits an older lady in a white dress, holding in an embrace a girl in a blue dress. On the table stands a basket of fruit and a tied bag. On the right an older dark-skinned woman sits on a log stump, a bowl on her knees. In front on the right a dog lies, behind, two saddled riding horses. Beside them sits a black man smoking a pipe.
c69111fc0ade3a5fc53c087a4f20434f815b9aef: Studied 1914–1916 at the Faculty of History and Linguistics of the University of St. Petersburg and 1924–1928 at the Faculty of Law of the University of Tartu. Took part in the First World War in 1916–1917, was a prisoner of war in Austria in 1917–1918, and served in 1918–1919 at the staff of the British North Russia Corps in Arkhangelsk. 1919–1921 military representative of the Republic of Estonia, 1921–1923 chargé d'affaires in Lithuania. 1923–1927 head of the political department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 1924–1925 chargé d'affaires in Paris and Brussels, and in 1926 counsellor at the Moscow legation. 1927–1931 assistant to the Minister of Foreign Affairs. 1931–1934 envoy to Italy and Switzerland and permanent representative to the League of Nations, 1934–1971 envoy to England.
1a7959377f9d32cd9a1eedcad41699bcde78fd99: Per William Petersen (b. 1955 in Denmark) is an artist and designer who has lived and worked in Tartu since 2006. He has experimented with numerous media and techniques, incl. painting, 3D-painting, sculpture, film, photography, etc. Petersen deals with themes related to the people around us – society. He is interested in people's ways of living, dreams, survival tactics. But what interests him most is everything connected with freedom, the right and opportunity to do something freely, since freedom can be considered the most important foundation of life and the development of humankind. Per Petersen is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
d437fccbcc6b401fa30196e283b2bdeefed5f7b3: Ott-Kaspar Sults is both an active artist and, for the past 12 years, a working emergency physician, which has given him the opportunity to experience more of life's absurdity than most people could ever imagine. It is precisely these everyday oddities that nourish his creative work. Sults has obtained a bachelor's degree in painting (2025) from the Tartu Art College Pallas. His work encompasses painting, installation and mixed media and has been represented at numerous solo and group exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally, attracting the interest of private collectors and public institutions throughout the Nordic and Baltic countries.
e8a4155b3ac99ee0a505e91a730e4d88f16b1d18: Leili MUUGA (b. 1922, Maima village, Altai Krai, Russia) is a painter who began in Estonian art with multi-figure compositions that were novel in their treatment of subject and manner of expression. Her paintings display a lyrical view of life and of people. In the portraits of creative people there is intimacy, the character is clearly presented. She has also cultivated flower, landscape and seascape painting, and later abstraction. The palette is mostly tonal, with light-radiating patches of colour serving as accents in some works. Muuga received her art education at the Tartu State Art Institute and at ERKI, where she later also worked as a teacher. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
e661cda6f1cd74545df44fb9c69b73d0f11806be: A seven-part light-coloured decorative composition on the merging of cells. I On a silvery surface, a bright yellow arched surface on the right. II On a golden background, a light blue arched surface on the left. III The intersection of a yellow and a light blue convex surface on a beige background, the intersection surface with light-coloured stripes. IV A yellow boat-shaped figure on light blue, on the left on yellow a blue diagonal figure ending in a wavy line. V On a yellow boat shape, above, a silvery wedge with three light-striped figures. VI On a light blue background, a boat-shaped figure in transitional shades of blue and yellow. VII A turquoise-blue arched surface with stripes at the bottom.
e0aa1c2e6446dfa2b0a579cb1127adf27616919b: Sculptor and draughtsman, known primarily as the author of views of Estonia, Livonia and Courland in the steel engraving technique. Born in Kuldīga as the son of a merchant and owner of a lending library, he worked as a land surveyor and cartographer. After studying in Germany, he worked as a sculptor at home from 1849, drawing outdoors in nature during the summers. In 1857 he began publishing a series of steel engravings, which appeared in 10 fascicles, each containing 3 sheets. The engravings were published as albums, printed in Darmstadt, together with texts, in three volumes in 1866–67. In 1913 a reproduction album of Stavenhagen's works was published in Tallinn (39 drawings and 4 sculptures, publisher Carl Meissner).
7396abf73ae866c460e5f89624516ef3924176d2: Sohvi Viik (b. 1991) graduated in 2016 from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a master's degree in sculpture and installation. Earlier studies in the photography department of the Estonian Academy of Arts gave her a strong foundation in contemporary art and photography, and an exchange period in 2013 at the Bergen Academy of Art and Design in Norway added a deeper engagement with the themes of video projection, sound and space. Sohvi Viik has taken part in numerous joint exhibitions and has also organised two solo exhibitions. Her main media are video, photo, sound and installation. She finds inspiration in art from the works of Janet Cardiff and George Bures Miller.
d8550e942538ba97d90e3c74a930cdcdfc269448: Against a background of architectural motifs, a group of six young people, a small tree in the middle. On the left, before a bluish brick wall and a blue drapery, at the wrought-iron corner of the wall sits a woman in a light summer dress and a hat, turned half-way to the right, hands in her lap, gaze directed forward, expression serious. To her right, on a suggested hillock, grows a young bare deciduous tree. On the right of the picture, against the background of part of the town wall with the Gate Servant's Tower [Väravaorja tower], in half-view, a woman with a girl, the child's gaze directed at the viewer. Behind them the figures of a woman with an armful of flowers and two men, facing the tree and the seated figure. Pale pastel tones, executed with great generalisation, mostly painted with a palette knife.
907e4077207df3717d59e1fbfadb032c04ed1177: Tartu town councillor and painter. Graduated from the gymnasium in Tartu in 1876, studied oil and watercolour painting in his home town under Woldemar Friedrich Krüger and Julie Wilhelmine Hagen-Schwarz. Continued his art studies in Vienna under William Unger and in Berlin under Gustav Richter. Ran a brewery in Tartu from 1880 to 1897. Became a citizen of Tartu in 1881 and was a town councillor until 1897. Was a Tartu town councillor in 1888–1889. Worked as a bank official in Pskov, Łódź, Šiauliai and Riga from 1898 to 1920. Painted landscapes in oil and watercolour technique. Exhibited in Tartu, Riga, St. Petersburg and Moscow. - Wikipedia
c1676fd5cbfc6027a9dae46357e1ee5bf3a411bc: The painting surface is divided into four by a brown strip. Upper left, the head of a brown-haired girl and, in profile facing left, the head of a dark-haired young man. In the same section, on the right, the head of a young woman wearing a white cap, turned to the left; behind her, seen from the back facing the viewer, in a white sweater, a dark-haired woman. Lower right, a bust portrait of an old woman with strong cheekbones and narrow, pressed-together lips. In the same section, on the left, against a dark background, in the middle a red and greyish horizontal wavy line, in the upper left corner a yellowish glow. In the upper part, a seascape as background. Painted in dark, pastel tones. The contours are blurred.
495a4bdbc3859811df136f97cb719113ccfea7e9: Alvar Reisner (b. 1979) studied painting at the Estonian Academy of Arts and worked there as a lecturer from 2005 to 2013, teaching mainly colour theory and painting. Reisner has taken part in exhibitions since 2003, and in 2005 he was awarded the first Wiiralt Scholarship intended for young artists. Since 2013 Alvar Reisner has worked as a freelance artist and interior designer, and several poems have also been published by him. Among his larger interior design projects one may mention the popular lounge restaurant Manna La Roosa in Tallinn and Kuur Resto in Kärdla, on Hiiumaa.
ca9a289946c4c17a267c57b89c6c24b210caeb09: Valev Sein (1964) creates works ranging from miniatures to monumental pieces. He experiments and plays with materials – by adding glass, wood, textile, pieces of mirror etc. to conventional painting media, he creates assemblages that connect with surrealism. The artist has executed stained-glass windows as commissioned works both for private homes and for churches. Sein graduated from ERKI in the field of painting and monumental art (1990), has taken part in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally, and was also one of the driving forces behind the Nelja Nurga gallery, which operated for a long time on Hiiumaa. He is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
bddf0ae4c15321cad1bcf5dab4c83fc77f706380: A winter seaside townscape, in the background on the left a pylon carrying a high-voltage power line together with low industrial buildings, in the foreground a frozen sea and, by a hole sawn into it, on the ice, a chainsaw and a fisherman working with a net. The colour scheme is winterly-sunnily bright, in the background a blue sky with cumulus clouds. The work belongs to the competition project "Makrorajoon" of the Estonian exposition at the 13th Venice Architecture Biennale, in which Kadarik Tüür Arhitektid continue the discussion on the theme of the development of Lasnamäe. The series presents a fragment of one Lasnamäe district, whose landscape has been transformed into a productive and locally functioning macro-neighbourhood.
27bc10e2a0bd0181045855fc6c7bd7f615b3952d: Anu-Leenu Uustalu was born in Tallinn into a schoolteacher's family. In 1940–1941 she worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn, in 1944 she fled to Germany, where she worked as an artist for the American Red Cross and as a drawing teacher at an Estonian elementary school and gymnasium. In 1949 the artist moved together with her sister Benita Uustalu to the United States, to the city of Milwaukee, Wisconsin. She worked as a technical draughtswoman, and from 1977 worked as a freelance artist. In 1968 all her earlier work was destroyed in a fire. In 1979 A. Uustalu designed a clothing display introducing Estonian folk culture in the permanent exhibition of the Milwaukee Public Museum.
a05e5282bc1171fcf72913e6c4c7dd7a6c2b0cd2: Elisa Ritsing is a freelance multidisciplinary artist who creates through painting and dance. She has obtained a bachelor's degree in choreography from Tallinn University and later studied painting at the Open Academy of the Estonian Academy of Arts. In her work she focuses mainly on two themes: femininity in its various forms; and the subconscious and the resulting unconscious patterns of thought and behaviour. Ritsing's works have taken part in exhibitions in various places in Estonia: at the Pärnu New Art Museum, the ArtDepoo gallery, the Design and Architecture Gallery, the MA EI SAA ARU art festival, and elsewhere.
0a73ee1c15a71a37927607935346625fd4dc1468: The installation consists of: a Diasec photograph leaning against a column or wall, attached at the top with an air compressor coil hose, with blue silicone cushioning under the corners resting on the floor. On "puddles" formed from sea sand painted with cobalt blue pigment are placed two UV-printed plexiglass sculptures and a tablet holder with UV-printed heat-treated plexiglass. A video plays on the monitor with sound coming from headphones. In front of the monitor are 3 fibo blocks painted dark grey, cushioned with memory foam and wondergel seat cushioning.
7b69dc3df115a5672752367bd4ae41dba5d7ebb0: A composition generalised to geometric forms depicting lighthouse roofs. The entire painting field is surrounded by a blackish-brown frame (unprimed canvas). At the bottom foreground, two white horizontal battens, the upper one stepped. In the right golden section, in the centre, a greenish-grey roof gable with a tall blackish-brown (unprimed canvas) door. Behind it a purplish-brown lighthouse roof with a chimney, and on the right, lower down, part of a small white roof gable. Behind on the right, a green mass of trees. On the left a black roof gable with a chimney, to the right of it a fragment of a white roof gable. In front of them a green mass of trees. A whitish light-blue sky.
c00ae1d7b69856c8a86e61f66fdc5dddf5ce9cf2: Kai Kiudsoo-Värv (b.1968) graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a bachelor's degree in glass art in 1995 and obtained a master's degree there ten years later, in 2005. Since 1995 she has worked as a freelance artist and has presented her works at exhibitions. Since 2002 Kai Kiudsoo-Värv has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association. She has been a member of the Estonian Glass Artists' Association since 2001, and on two occasions, in 2002-2004 and 2010–2013, Kai has been president of the Estonian Glass Artists' Association. In 2010 Kai received the honorary title "Recognised Glass Artist 2008-2009".
30843956788fcf1bcb85790ffe2821d05896bd78: Sasha Tishkov (1989) is a visual artist and carpenter whose work focuses on the dynamics between peripheries and centres. His sculptural objects and installations explore environmental and human phenomena. In his work he uses natural materials and traditional craft techniques, such as woodworking and weaving – his interest in craft began in childhood, which he spent in Matsalu National Park. Tishkov obtained a master's degree at Central Saint Martins in London (2019) and works both in Estonia and internationally. He is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
64f33a3b31fbe4dd120f05540e8082280cc0b8fa: Two photographs in one frame. FV 43/1 Upper photograph. Paired photographs of three naked men and one woman in an interior. On the left edge sits a dark-haired naked man, leg crossed over the knee, hand on his cheek, holding a magazine in his left hand. Beside him stands one who leans with his right hand on a cloth-covered stand holding scales. A little further forward on the right sits a woman in an armchair, her upper body turned slightly to the left. Her head is in profile, wearing a dark curly wig, dark sunglasses in front, holding a box with weights in her lap. Behind the woman on the right stands a man, hands behind his back, gaze directed diagonally downward - towards the woman.
9d333bed9e251d35eb9901512fa75542c9618632: Rosita Raud (1962) graduated in scenography from the St. Petersburg State Theatre Arts Academy and has worked in various theatres in Estonia and abroad; in total she has designed more than eighty productions. She currently works as the chief designer of the Estonian Theatre for Young Audiences. Raud has exhibited her work since 2000, and her practice is characterised by object-centred visual thinking that interweaves theatrical elements with sculptural and installation techniques. She is a member of the Association of Estonian Scenographers and the Estonian Artists' Association.
9cf86f08683cd49b9fa7b6c6da338112e3b8cd88: A triangular plate, 4 cm thick, on both sides and edges, on a bluish-grey background geometric surfaces in blue-green-orange-red tones. On one side a triangle of coloured, triangular surfaces, outside three oval shapes with red edges, two blue inside, the third red. On the other side a square of blue surfaces, on top of which a partially green square. Inside the latter an oval with a red edge. Below, partly on a blue surface, on the left and right an oval with a red edge. Along the sides, elongated triangles, at the bottom a blue-red square and two ovals - green-blue and red-green.
a17f5e708e78f86c918bc4c1ec84eefbaa8a044f: Aleksandra ANISA Ianchenko (born 1988) is a visual artist, university researcher and exhibition curator. An artist with a background in fine arts and art history, she recently defended her doctoral degree at Tallinn University (Estonia) and Åbo Akademi (Finland) with the dissertation "Estranging Trams: Atmospheres of Trams in and through Art", which is based on her artistic practice. In her work she is interested in creating imagined worlds rooted in everyday observations. These worlds can take various forms — from paintings and drawings to performative interventions and filmmaking.
a1c2e996636def9c95e59c8c4ad9890f45b36b3f: In the foreground, slightly right of centre, a half-figure of a young woman with glasses seen frontally, her head tilted slightly to the right, brown medium-length hair curled downward. The woman's arms are bent, her clearly painted hands positioned at chest level, her body dissolving evenly into a light surface, which transitions into a whitish sheet stretched taut behind the figure. Behind the latter, painted in a semi-diffuse manner in bright yellow, blue, brown tones, three female figures, the one on the left holding the sheet with her hand, and a number of quadrangular shapes. Above them a deep blue vertical surface. The painting is strongly textured in the area of the figures' heads.
81bb521e12d40ea7dfb2dea8cce2a9b6bf929c8f: Anna-Liisa Sääsk is a young artist and designer whose work focuses on graphics, performance and various fields of visual media. Her earlier recognitions include the Ilon Wikland Young Artist Award and recognition for organising the contemporary art festival "Kunstikompott" for young people. From Kunstikompott and a small group at the art school arose the art group TEMA, which has participated in several festivals with its performances and installations, such as the Diverse Universe performance festival in Pärnu, Tartu Valgus, Viljandi Tuled and the Made in Estonia marathon 2024.
0d097269e1ba10391aec8cd74ce62a17e0245cde: Liisi Örd has completed a master's degree in the painting department of the University of Tartu. Her work is characterised by a sensitive and reflective approach, in which the visual language speaks of silence, melancholy and the inner strength of the northern landscape. Örd's painting style can be described as "broken realism" – an approach where at times one is very close to precise depiction, and at times moves toward abstraction and perceptual space. Form never dominates over idea, but stems from what the artist currently considers important. This flexibility creates works that are visually diverse and conceptually layered.
bdf12e1bcfbca96899036df9d07a26c9d54fa1ae: Karl-Erik Talvet (b. 1991 in Paris) lives and works in Tallinn. In 2018 he completed his master's studies in painting at the Estonian Academy of Arts, and has also spent time abroad during the 2016/2017 academic year at the Brera Academy of Fine Arts in Milan. In 2019 Talvet went on a military mission to the Republic of Mali, where he served as an interpreter, and has used the experience gained there in his subsequent works and exhibition. Talvet mainly works with painting and comics and has participated in numerous exhibitions. He is a member of both the Estonian Painters' Association and the Estonian Comics Society.
09b1d069f2a7b67ee56bb55e4e4113a035271894: Liisi Tani (b. 1988) has studied painting and mural restoration at the Tartu Art College (2008-2012). She began actively participating in exhibitions already during her studies and has exhibited her works at numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad. Tani is an enthusiastic painter who mainly expresses herself in oil and watercolour painting and mixed media. She mainly cultivates figurative composition in oil technique and abstract treatment in watercolour. Her explorer's spirit constantly puts her to the test and invites new challenges. Tani is a member of the Estonian Watercolourists' Association.
226228b73f5fad4e9499f9116d743a898cbba39e: On green grass a colourful crowd of people in summer clothing. Five figures in the foreground given more clearly: on the left a man in blue trousers, white shirt and peaked cap, tie in red and green stripes, brown jacket over his right knee. To his right a woman with copper-coloured hair in a yellow dress, hands leaning back, a bag beside her. Further on a short-haired girl sitting with her chin resting on her hand. In the lower right corner a smiling blonde in a red-and-green patterned pinafore, beside her a dark-haired woman in profile. In the middle ground of the composition, people are rendered as a play of bright colour patches. Above, a bright blue sky.
28af83e73a9b1520d780d69d0b286707acbe5e65: Marit Loitmets is a painter interested in what happens to memories once no one personally carries them anymore. Her work draws on family archives, photo albums, inherited objects and oral stories, exploring the connections between memory, identity and belonging. Moving between the borderlands of photorealism and abstraction, she creates works in which personal and collective layers of memory intertwine through colour, pattern and fragmentary images. In her works, nostalgia does not signify a longing for the past, but an attentive gaze at what is already becoming fragile and fading.
1b55fe8bad382b3404ea80dd014914a60014c9b8: Broken, earth-toned painting of an old town courtyard with a front yard and back yard, separated by a fence with a gateless passage in the middle. In the background, slightly left of the central axis, the end wall of a high-gabled medieval house with a tall chimney on the right side of the roof. In front of it, slightly to the left, a similar lower house. In the foreground on the left, part of the façade of a greenish-grey house, with two doors, and one window on the second floor. In the middle ground on the right, an ochre-yellow, classicist-style two-storey house with a large canopy on the side facing the viewer, with a horse-drawn cart beneath it. In the foreground, in the golden section on the left, a cart in the yard.
8bdbfe43b5309bc46e81788326aa9bf3a62b3efe: Andres Koort (b. 1969 in Tallinn) is an Estonian painter, scenographer, designer and curator. He graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in stage design (1987–1993) and furthered his studies in painting at the Academia Minerva in Groningen, Netherlands. Koort has participated in exhibitions since 1991 and has served as a board member of the Estonian Painters' Association since 2002. He has created stage designs for productions at the Estonian Drama Theatre, Tallinn City Theatre, Endla Theatre in Pärnu, the Estonian Puppet Theatre and Theatrum. The artist's works can be found in the collections of the Tartu Art Museum and the Lithuanian Art Museum.
5438b7a0e85935bdd7d41a47c231a8a19cef600c: Tauno Ostra is currently a first-year Master's student in Fine Arts, specialising in graphic art. He considers his most important exhibitions to be the solo exhibition "Identiteet", which took place in 2015 at the Haapsalu City Gallery and in 2016 at the Võru City Gallery, and "Sümmeetria" in February–March 2017 at the Viljandi City Gallery. Among his major group exhibitions are the 5th Tallinn International Drawing Triennial and the Spring Exhibition (2016) at the Tallinn Art Hall, and the Baltic Drawing Biennial in Imatra, Finland. In addition, this year's Mirror Face To Face at the National Library and in Vicenza, Italy.
90a24dc3a58edcfde568dabb679837c4c63a835d: A large truck is driving on a dark road, with an illuminated screen at its rear. On the screen a film is running, showing roadside views of America?, but during the daytime, with plenty of sunshine. The truck has been filmed from a bus driving behind it. The screen alternately moves further away and closer, cars come towards it and pass by. Towards the end, the approach to the screen becomes so close that the night-time road is no longer visible, and then quickly pulls back. Finally, the vehicle ahead comes to a stop. Toomik talks with the policemen sitting in the vehicle and then it drives off. The bus does not follow the vehicle. Soundtrack: faintly audible comments from the bus passengers.
3ae251ab73e435a8ead0e7a21cdbfffe6a94c553: Against an even, light bluish-green background, fragments of an interior: on the right an old sewing machine, the back of a chair visible behind it, in the upper right corner of a frame a furniture decoration motif, in the upper left a small depiction of a treadle sewing machine. In the centre of the painting, a fair-haired young woman and a laughing girl with a cat in her lap are sitting in an armchair. The woman is wearing a spotted blouse and long trousers, holding the girl and the cat in her arms, her gaze directed at them. Behind them, on a stool-like stand, a man's head, hat over his eyes. A slide has been used, reflections, shadows painted flatly with clearly delineated patches of colour.
bbc9838c2f4629e8a344ce36cdf46daf2ebf6e11: The painting was in Rector Toomas Asser's office from 2021-2024. Universitas Tartuensis 2021 no. 6, p. 11: With the arrival of the coronavirus period, Rector Toomas Asser decided to remove a large black cabinet from his office, which he calls depressing. To decorate the freed-up wall space, he chose Jaan Elken's 1978 painting "Kusagil Eestis", which belongs to the collection of the university's art museum. "I don't know what it says to the new generation, but there are a lot of meaningful things here. Up there, for example, is 'KG', that is, KGB, and then you can see changes of direction - that something is changing in Estonia," the rector describes while looking at the painting.
32ca06e34bb231ae7e0d20e1e378a5b0d7c6198d: Mirja-Mari Smidt (b. 1977) works mainly in the field of free graphic art and painting (watercolour, oil, author's technique). She graduated from the graphic art department of EKA in 1999 and also studied interdisciplinary arts there (M.A. 2002). Thanks to what she learned there, dance, singing and body culture temporarily entered her work, which were later replaced by an inward turn. Her last major appearance was at the Muhu Print 2017 overview exhibition at the Kuku Club. In Mirja-Mari's works, an autobiographical thread (birth, death, being in harmony with nature, longing for perfection) runs alongside reflections on the themes of faith, history and the environment.
794830e2964d42e5848b65bdc79df71036e021e2: A two-figure composition, in the foreground grass and meadow, in the background against a landscape backdrop. In the foreground, in the centre, the half-figure of a girl in a white dress with orange circles and a red hat, in half-profile facing left, her head tilted to the left side, a plant between her lips. On the left edge of the composition, a girl with a red hat, a blue blouse and a knitted vest, hands behind her head. Between them, in the middle ground, an improvised table on which lie brushes, a bottle of ink and a small composition of young people around an old-fashioned tractor. In the middle ground, on the right edge, on the grass, vessels with food on a tablecloth with red circles.
0d42d6b4198b4ba0a0e2186ebfc51229a6925581: A plywood box fastened to the centre of a black cardboard base, itself divided lengthwise into two by a partition. The inner walls of the box are of reflective metal, with brightly coloured portrait silhouettes painted on the bottom. Both halves of the box show a similar depiction in different colour combinations: on the right the back view of a man in a hat, on the left a frontal view painted flatly in blue, yellow, green and red. On the bottom of the box, beneath the figures, a pink strip, to which a brown, leafed metal tree branch is attached. On the black base, on both sides, a traffic light figure with three green glass signal lights placed one below the other.
724df153d33e73d66cbd3faa3470bd0a05f26dff:
Laura Kuuse's photo-series "Knife" was first exhibited at "Hullumeelsus", an exhibition held in EKKM in 2008. "Knife" consists of two movie-like shots that draw attention to the structure of conversation. A story is automatically put together from the two photos, but many vastly different interpretations for the narrative are left possible.

The work was acquired in 2011 on the condition that the artist receives an invitation to an exhibition in 2013. Due to this agreement, the 2013 exhibiton "Kõrvalnähud / Side Effects" was curated by Laura Kuusk and Pascale Riou.
32745c0de50b98abdfb5a7ee752277b3e56e90bd: "Sugar Free" is an installation based on the author's experience of a madhouse, in which the central place is occupied by an antique wooden cabinet moving in a semicircle connected by a metal rod. On the wall is an 18-photo-fragment image of a building. Next to it are photos of the author, under which are signs "After" and "Before". Inside the cabinet, a metal birdcage filled with sugar cubes is suspended on metal cables, above which burns an electric light bulb hanging on a cable. A soundtrack sounds from the cabinet (in the first version the author reading paragraphs of the Constitution, in the second version an excerpt from the Gibson Brothers' song "Paranoia").
d108d3f9103633f3b706d6008e07563bad1eae82: Indrek Köster (b. 1970). Studied sculpture at the Tartu Art School and the Estonian Academy of Arts. Graduated in 2018 from EKA's Faculty of Fine Arts Master's programme. First exhibition participation at the Tartu Autumn Exhibition in 1992. More active exhibition activity in 2006–2021 with the artist duo Johnson and Johnson (together with Taavi Talve). Several solo exhibitions and dozens of group exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2011. Annual award of the Cultural Endowment's Visual and Applied Art Fund in 2013. Works in collections: Art Museum of Estonia, EKKM, Tartu Art Museum, Ludwig Museum.
9df70871b980c69ce9f397a867a48e0f36bf4d3d: In the foreground on the left two geese and a girl leaning on a fence. In the centre, a peasant boy with a woman on a load of logs watering a horse in the river. On the road, further back on the right, horses with peasants moving. By the roadside an inn with stopping horses. On the right edge of the painting, at the foot of a bridge crossing the river in the centre, a cart on which a woman sitting on the load pulls at the reins of a bolting horse, while a standing man in front of the horse holds the shaft with his right hand. Coming towards them at great speed is a cart with two horses and two peasants. To the left of the bridge, by the riverside, a peasant waters a horse. To the left of the horse, a herd is heading home.
c415271e4a111bf1356c593afd6829f9d1e603f0: He was born as the son of a manager of a cattle-farm estate. He studied at the Valga town school. He took his secondary school graduation exams in Petersburg. He studied, with interruptions, at the Petersburg Mining Institute from 1907 to 1921, while at the same time being an auditor at the Petersburg Institute of Archaeology. He worked at a pharmacy in Kronstadt, as a war-industry instructor at the Ural factories, later as a representative of the Ural state factories and as assistant director of the Petrograd Mint. He served as the representative of the Republic of Estonia on the Petersburg Option Commission and, in 1922–1924, as vice-consul in Petersburg. In 1924 he moved to live in Tallinn and in 1927 was appointed director of the Estonian Art Museum.
ea92fa057fdd9e32644667e940dee5f93c4474d9:
Related to the event - A hereditary nobleman, born in the Kamenets-Podolsk Governorate. He graduated from the Kamenets-Podolsk gymnasium, attended lectures for two years at the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics of the Imperial St. Vladimir University in Kiev.

In service with the 92nd Pechora Regiment from 16.04.1879. He passed the officer's rank examination at the infantry cadet military school in St. Petersburg and returned to the regiment. He took part in the Russo-Japanese War in 1904–1905. Retired due to age from 02.11.1913. At the beginning of the First World War he returned to service with the 92nd Pechora Regiment. Due to illness he was discharged on 30.03.1917.
a23cf392d1af09233d10ef41294132a784d7f710: Maik Kalberg (born 1987 in Tartu) is an Estonian painter and filmmaker. He studied at Tartu Art Grammar School in a class with an art focus and obtained higher education in film art at the Baltic Film and Media School. He currently lives and works in Tallinn. As an artist, Maik wishes, both with his existence and his creative work, to create positive energy in the world and to seek, at the very least, even a useful and practical pattern of behaviour. A person's task in this world is not merely to burden and consume the environment in which they exist, but to give birth, through their presence here, to something uplifting.
2780dc058241731365120a0e44dec326a58b3e54: A marshland landscape with reeds bending backwards, bordered on both sides by mole-like embankments, converging towards the horizon located in the middle of the picture. The sky above the landscape is painted as broad horizontal planes of chrome green and cherry red. Against this background a huge quantity of fruits and vegetables rises from the horizon like a smoke-like plume. In the foreground a cut pumpkin, pepper pods, cabbage, carrot etc., all painted emphasising the roundness of their forms, at places with a strong texture. The dominant chrome green tone in the central part of the painting turns beige towards the edges of the picture, painted as a surface with broad strokes.
043e71a788e65fb8b76998ac6291c4402c789625: Sven Saag (b. 1968) is an Estonian painter and graphic artist. He studied painting at the Chair of Painting of the University of Tartu from 1991 to 1994. The artist has participated in numerous exhibitions both at home and abroad. The artist says of his painting: "Like a restorer who removes layers of paint and finds ever new figures, views, faces beneath them, one can also approach one's own paintings in depth — scrape the paintings and discover ever new and old images beneath the layers of paint." Since 2001 a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and since 2008 a member of the Estonian Painters' Association.
7e217444368332e431a47a0c357df0c0d96de83d: A man standing behind a red stage reads out an appeal. To his right a man wearing a peaked cap sits at a table and writes on a white sheet of paper. He is partly obscured by a man standing at the right edge of the table, leaning on the table with his left hand. The standing man's right leg is obscured by a bench. Behind the bench three women and one man can be seen. To the left of the table 12 people, some sitting, some standing, listening to the appeal. Of these, on the bench in the foreground sit a man in a white shirt and winter cap and a woman with a red kerchief. Behind the group of people a window can be seen. On the wall between the window and the gate hangs a poster.
abd2aa1bdf548d7bd94a5fe091394878f4d74811: Olesja Semenkova (1992) lives and works in Tallinn, Estonia. Her works were exhibited in Tallinn, Estonia and in Brussels, Belgium. Olesja experiments with and includes different mediums into one artwork. Her practice can also be called installation art as she enjoys questioning and playing with the spectator's role in the exhibition space. Finished Tallinn University in 2015 as Bachelor of Arts in Humanities, from 2017 studying in Estonian Academy of Arts, Contemporary Arts, MA, improved her skills at LUCA school of Arts, Fine Art department, Brussels.
7580d3326171b03b36d40ae57e9884743429aaeb: A print depicting a forest with a meandering stream, which widens into a pond in the foreground. In the middle of the picture, on the bank of the pond, two undressed women are about to go bathing. The fair-haired woman, whose hair is interwoven with pearls, covers her breast with a veil, sitting with her right leg in the water, while the other leans on the grass by the bank and looks fearfully to the right. The dark-haired woman wears an elaborate hairstyle, bends towards her companion and also looks fearfully to the right. She stands in the water and rests her left knee on a stone on the bank. From the right, out of the forest, comes a satyr with goat legs and horns, his gaze on the bathers.
7717f43b8b07fb0e401261a357e800d1ee370e5d: was born into a joiner's family, obtained general education at Nõmme City 1st Primary School and Tallinn City Boys' Secondary School. He studied art from 1931-1937 at the State School of Applied Art (decorative painting), and from 1938-1941 at the State Higher Art School (painting). In 1941 he was mobilised into a labour battalion of the Red Army, and in 1944 belonged to the Yaroslavl collective of Estonian artists. After World War II he studied at the Moscow Academy of Arts. From 1944 he was a teacher at ERKI (TKÜ, EKA), and in 1993 became professor emeritus. In creating his works E. Okas travelled in 1958 to the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, in 1961 to Italy, in 1962 to France, in 1963 to Japan
56e80304679dd4d8f73df9c1f8090c05e439fbf0: A print with an allegorical scene. On the clouds sits a large group of women, each holding an emblem characterising a field of science or art. In the centre are the allegories: Sculpture with a hammer and a figure on a coat of arms, Painting with a bundle of brushes, Geometry with a compass, a triangle and a ruler, Music with a kantele, etc. Highest of all stands, in bright light, a female figure covered with a veil, from whom a crowned young man tries to tear away the veil. Above, in the background, a round building with Ionic columns can be seen. On the left in front, beneath the clouds, stands a group of men who look up and offer a censer with incense on a tray.
392e3506ec5b87dd56fc1b872578db02835e0e21: A city street with four figures in the foreground: in the centre a woman in half-profile, in a brown coat with a furry collar, with a handbag and grey high-heeled shoes, wearing a low brown hat. Around the woman three men in white smocks and grey caps. The man on the left, standing with his back to the viewer, and the bread carrier on the right, shown in profile, hold yellow oval bread baskets. Behind the men, on the right, the rear end of a brown bread van can be seen. In the background a tall yellow garden wall, behind which houses with brown roofs can be seen. In the upper right corner a piece of greyish-blue sky.
2b9b98de3082da2276cdd76bafe6b64fcc2b592a: In the foreground, parallel to the lower edge, a river, by which, slightly to the left of the vertical centre line, a reddish-brown horse harnessed to a water barrel stands. By the horse and the barrel a woman in a white blouse draws water from the river, and a man in a cap pours water into the barrel. From the horse a narrow sandy path leads up the hill; on the hill, to the right of the path, an electricity pole, to the left large green trees and bushes. By the river, on the path, a fair-haired woman, to her right three children splashing in the river. At the top of the hill, in the centre of the horizon, two white towers or chimneys, on the left edge a clump of trees. Above, a light blue sky with cirrus clouds.
74a0fd8beed0dcd67981ef416aa878662d677fa3: Ülle Raadik (1948) has focused on decorative textiles both in public buildings and private homes – on textile as both a decorative and usable element that influences the entire space. The main protagonists of her printed and painted textiles are transparency and multi-layeredness, and the flowing force of colour. Raadik graduated from ERKI's textile speciality (1975), has worked as an art teacher, and has been actively involved in the work of the Lühikese Jala Gallery, as well as participating in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and in neighbouring countries. She is a member of the Estonian Textile Artists' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
7b86cec1e36f57a1f8e4a605a8d085f4ec89f3e7: On a yellow background, three seated female nudes painted in a sketchy manner. The left and middle figures are sitting with their right side towards the viewer. The head of the left-hand woman is turned towards her right shoulder, her gaze looking down. The woman's head and hands rest on her left bent knee, her right leg lower. The middle figure is painted in the most sketchy manner. Both of its legs are drawn up hooked under the chin. The woman on the right is in a more upright position, with her gaze directed towards the middle ground of the picture. In terms of colour scheme the painting is yellow, with black contours providing the tone, and red, greenish and black colour contrasts.
131a2210d6700bdd84db3d4cba05f26e383ab2e1: In 1902, on the initiative of teacher Wieckmann and with the permission of the Consistory, the winged altarpiece (B. Notke, 1483), as a Catholic-era object unsuitable for a Lutheran church, was replaced with a new altar wall. In 1929 the parish council had agreed to donate the winged altarpiece to the Museum Society, but in connection with the church's renovation works in 1933, efforts began to have it returned. The Museum Society did not agree, despite expert assessments that considered the storage place in the Cathedral unsuitable for the altarpiece. Only on 18 December 1942 was the winged altarpiece reconsecrated in its own place. (source: National Register of Cultural Monuments);
ec6149f041120a4e180784b6b5b12eb46f35dea1: Lauri Kulpsoo is an Estonian photographer and drummer. He is a graduate of Tartu Tamme Gymnasium and has studied geography at the University of Tartu. Lauri Kulpsoo has worked as a photographer for the newspaper Postimees and the magazine Pere ja Kodu. He has also contributed to several other Estonian and Finnish media publications. Kulpsoo's photographs have been used in several books. Kulpsoo has played drums in the bands Lloyd, Tartu Popi ja Roki Instituut, Jaan Pärn ja Pahad Seemned, Honey Power and Kuma. Since autumn 2008 Lauri Kulpsoo has been making "Fantaasia" programmes on Klassikaraadio.
6cd1252ecf78aa41e13127380b07909bb7b2a57a: MAIKRO is the artist of the Micro Gallery being established in the Ülejõe district of Tartu, who has also worked as a creator before. In the late 1980s and early 1990s he actively participated in exhibition activity, mainly as a painter, and occasionally also creating installations. In addition he tried his hand as a fashion designer, creating mainly alternative garments based on recycled materials. Since the gallery network at that time was focused mainly on representing and selling mainstream artists, MAIKRO, who at the time naturally appeared under a different name, continued working as a stage and interior designer.
ef2f3983fa8dc18028c1e7ece619e789730872ab: Six children in Ukrainian folk costume in the foreground, on the left in golden section, around a narrator gesturing while seated in profile facing right, wearing a fur cap and a long brown coat. In front of him, on the right side of the composition, sit two girls dressed in dark blue, behind them stand an elder in a white blouse leaning on a wicker fence, and at the right edge of the composition a younger girl with a long braid leaning against a gatepost. To the narrator's left hand are two boys in brown half-length coats and fur caps. Behind them a river landscape opens up.
5de63526a93ca2ed526d4320704a6f2f213f88fc: An elderly man sits in profile in a red wooden chair with carved back and armrests, legs stretched out. The man's left hand rests on the armrest, in his left hand a book, a finger keeping the place. His right arm is bent at the elbow and supports his head. The man's crown is bald, with short, heavily greying hair at the sides, and gold-rimmed glasses on his nose. The man wears a black suit and shoes, a white shirt and a grey tie with red stripes. The background is a room corner with dark grey walls. On the wall to the left hangs a landscape picture, in the upper right corner a quarter of a picture hanging on the wall is visible.
0c24b703379871d01c7370aae88e297d2c8bf56f: The broadcast action "Kodumaa uudised" ["National News"] was on Kanal 2's programme on 27, 28 and 29 September 1996. Based on the daily news, poetic texts-poems are created, rhymed banality. The news covers economic, political and cultural events taking place in Estonia. The alienation device is the lack of rhyme in the delivery. It is read by actors, preferably a woman and a man in the frame at the same time. They have been instructed beforehand. The process is polished and staged. The result is presented on three different days via Kanal 2 immediately before the official news. Total length one and a half to three minutes.
71bcdfbfeb9cd92e5e3b20f4fe8f8d49ae17ba13: A composition consisting of three parts, the background of which is formed by advertising prints given in series of a woman and a boy sipping a drink through a straw, and views of Tallinn. Four red wooden-knobbed coat hooks and 8 small aluminium cake tins are screwed onto the middle part; to the right of the vertical central axis of the middle section, long twisting sheet-metal strips are attached to the surface of the picture. The background covered with prints on the central panel of the picture is partially covered on the left with black, on the right expressively with black, white and red paint. On the right-hand part, above, broad brushstrokes drawn in black and yellow.
652fdeaef91caa8f2fa1bdac7861d37b93fe3dd6: A. M. Hagen was born in Vijciems in Livonia (present-day Latvia) as the son of a manor leaseholder. He studied at the Cēsis district school and in Karl August Senff's studio in Tartu (also working as his assistant), and travelled to Germany and Switzerland in 1820–1823. In 1826 he was an art teacher at the provincial gymnasium and in 1826–1832 at the girls' gymnasium, and in 1838–1851 he headed the drawing school of the University of Tartu. Commissioned by the Russian Emperor, he made a series of views of the Finnish islands (with influences of C. D. Friedrich), and in 1837 received the title of member and free artist of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. He retired in 1851, but from 1855 engaged in photography in Tartu
6c48d4fe4c48327ca595eea14d1e84a8a8b4496e: I graduated in 2021 from the Kõrgem Kunstikool Pallas in painting and restoration, and further trained in Portugal and Hungary within the Erasmus programme. I deal with research into monochrome visuals. For this I use charcoal and graphite. Charcoal inspires me with its primordial and sketch-like feel. As a canvas I experiment with surfaces of different texture and porosity, such as paper, linen fabric, concrete, wood, etc. As themes I address the journey between the real world and a person's sentimental memory images, containing both deliberately evoked and involuntarily arising memories.
7283dfe5b820c122d7ca6d54185362c7378da37d: He was born in Tallinn as the son of a Ukrainian coppersmith, studied painting at "Pallas" in Tartu in 1922–27. In 1929, 1936–37 and 1939 he was on study trips to Paris. In 1939 he married Anita Obst (Oeste). In 1927–37 he was a free artist in Võru, in 1937–41 a teacher of graphic art at "Pallas". In 1937 he received an honourable diploma at the Paris World Exhibition, and in 1939 and 1940 the Estonian Book Fund prize. In 1940 he joined the reorganisers of art life in Tartu. He was arrested by the Germans on 26.05.1943. The portfolio "Põlevkivitööstus" ["Oil Shale Industry"], the signature of which includes bars, was partly completed in prison. He was presumably executed on 23.07.1944 near Tallinn.
aabb8e1cbaa28551bb4a4f195d935a358bb3854e: On the right edge stands a nude female figure seen from the side, hands with long dark red nails stretched out parallel to the lower edge. The woman has a heavily made-up face, black short hair held in a hedgehog-style hairdo on the forehead. Around the woman a grey background covered with jagged blue brushstrokes. In the left edge of the painting, as if only suggested, a male figure: black suit, white dress shirt, red tie and a top hat. Around the man a black background densely filled with small white triangles. Triangular and quadrangular pieces of mirror are glued onto the black frame. The painting surface is in places relief-like due to the thick layer of paint.
bcb287b700af493787db9dc4564cd03df3f9137a: In a studio, under an open window, a female nude lying on her back: her head turned towards the window, her right arm bent at the shoulder, her left lying on her side on a light-coloured drapery that extends over the windowsill and out. Her right leg is bent at the knee, her left lying straight on the other. Near the model's head is the corner of a leather armchair, part of the heel visible. The light falling from the window makes the body pale, creating blue shadows. The surrounding background is painted as abstract patches of bluish brown. Almost half of the upper part of the picture depicts a view from above through the window onto a pinkish-brown, greenish forest floor under pines, which is reflected in the window panes.
8287d12d91d013db21d45032db41308f1343b9a6: Vadim Jerohhin was born in 1962 in Kunda. He studied art from 2000 to 2015 in the "Stupeni" studio under teacher Vladislav Kuznetsov. Since 2009 a member of the Association of Russian Artists in Estonia. Since 2010 a member of the Narva artists' association "Vestervalli", since 2017 a member of its board. He is also a board member of two artists' associations, "Kunsti Sadam" and "Symbol 4". Kunsti Sadam has organised 8 international art camps, 16 solo exhibitions and nearly 200 group exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad (Russia, China, Italy, France, Serbia, Slovakia, USA)
0fb1a294749f2bb70c447d68fece2a169122f5c1: Against a light sky, women in Estonian folk costume greet soldiers. On the left a group of five people: three young women in Harjumaa costume (blue-striped skirt, lace blouse, coins on the chest) turn towards soldiers standing in front of them on the right, wearing greatcoats and helmets. The left-hand man is seen from behind, the right one in side view. On the right of the canvas two soldiers conversing: in front on the left a man in a straw hat with a rifle on his back, seen from behind, opposite him on the right a soldier in greatcoat and helmet seen frontally. In the background, in the centre and on the right, figures in folk costume. The painting is in light greyish, brown tones.
e3a222bb983f668f23c43d1e1610b0d04462e57d: A pasty, lush, quivering vegetable garden with a broken wooden fence in the middle ground, and behind it tall deciduous trees. In the upper left corner, one above the other, two abstract room walls with rectangular panelling, on which hang two brownish-red framed pictures. On the right edge, emerging from the grass, a jib-sail-shaped, white surface with formless greenish and pinkish shades, and beside it a small, yellow, slender mast with one shroud. Textured brushwork. Above, a whitish light-blue sky, greyish-white above the horizon.
254111a3b1f93204aa15a528046f37ca70fb523c: The sheet depicts sculptures bounded by baroque architectural details, and a fresco on which a she-wolf suckles Romulus and Remus, the founders of the city of Rome. On the left is an atlas figure carrying the ceiling's supporting beam, surrounded by four putti. To the right of the fresco two putti positioned one above the other. The fresco shows a river landscape, with the she-wolf and the boys lying in a basket in the foreground. To the left of the group a raven with spread wings and open beak. On the riverbank on the viewer's side is a hill with a solitary tree, while on the other side of the water a low bank with solitary trees, a hurrying young man, mountains in the distance.
076b0829d906ca9d4c3ffea8c8ea80339150792b: A composition combining architectural elements with a spatial impression. Predominantly Gothic architectural buttresses, tall pointed-arch window and door openings, portals, motifs of stairs and blocks intermingle. Beams of light penetrate from the left between the geometric shapes, forming patches of light in the centre on a suggested floor. Behind the motifs, two pairs of figures, and in front on the right the half-figure of a photographer in a top hat, seen from the side. In the centre of the composition brown, beige tones, above in the background greyish-blue shapes striving upward.

01f70374aa087eb13f2450a4bfb53e8b9393257a: H. E. Hartmann studied art in Tartu under A. M. Hagen, at the Düsseldorf Academy of Arts and in Munich. In 1841–44 he worked in Latvia as a schoolteacher in Bērzaine, from 1845 in Tartu as a drawing teacher and city treasury accountant. In 1845 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, and from 1860 he was conservator of the collections of the Learned Estonian Society. He painted portraits and landscapes, but especially significant is his Estica-themed graphic art. Hartmann's woodcuts of Estonians appeared in the publications: Talurahva Postimees, Tartu Postimees, Das Inland (in German), Pasaule (in Latvian), etc
12c96bfa189ea26792ff6804451cfa5394a29aaf: Danel Kahar (b.1990) is an artist who lives and works in Tallinn. He graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts, Department of Fine Arts, majoring in painting, BA (2016). His first solo exhibition took place in 2017 at Draakoni Gallery; the same year he also had a large-scale exhibition together with Grisli Soppe-Kahar in the great hall of the Tartu Art House. In the summer of 2018 he was in residence together with Grisli Soppe-Kahar in Italy (Mazzano Romano). His most recent solo exhibition took place in 2021 at Gallery Metropolis, where he presented objects in which painting is blended with assemblage and sculpture.
ab11f67c980cf269c89d66aaaea92ebfd259569e: Interior of an evening café, groups of people at round tables covered with white cloths. In the foreground, a lady with brown hair, in a dark green striped dress and black hat, her face turned toward the viewer. Half behind her, on the right, a waitress in a purplish-red dress with a white cap and a tray. At lower left part of a table is visible, on which stands a squat little bottle of spirits, and the left hand, holding a glass, of the person sitting at the table. In the background at left, at a table, sits a company consisting of ladies in pink and yellow dresses and a gentleman in a blue suit. In the background, on a greyish-blue wall, two wall lamps.
455acd7904528b35c551c2972a1f47d01e555a20: He studied painting and furniture art at the Pallas Higher Art School (1926–1932). After graduating from Pallas he worked as a freelance artist in Tartu, where between 1934 and 1937 he ran the legendary café for cultural figures, "Ko-Ko-Ko". After the war, between 1945 and 1947, he worked as a drawing teacher at Tartu 1st Secondary School, and from 1947 to 1950 as chairman of the Tartu bureau of the Art Fund. Later he made illustrations for ERM publications and magazines and created caricatures. He was a member of the Central Union of Estonian Visual Artists from 1932 and a member of the Estonian SSR Artists' Union from 1945.
879e3ecbeda12d457a57347f71031123a93b9873: A composition of kitchen dishes and utensils on a brown base, against the background of a sharply contoured, modelled folded yellow drapery in which sharply delineated beige, mustard-yellow, light brown, and lilac shades appear. In the foreground, in the centre, a pot stand from a gas stove burner, on the right edge a spiral whisk. In the background at left, an enamelled green teapot, next to it a soap dish with pinkish soap, in front of them a large white mug with a blue stripe. In the background, in the right golden section, on a white sheet of paper, a primus stove, to the right and behind it a large glass jar.
59c0bb0233834cc744df36937b04dfd11519177a:
. During the perfomance the two artists, dressed in suits, carrying well-executed copies of Warhol's Brillo Boxes, walk around the city of Tallinn. The search for suitable context for these pieces of symbolic art within the local enviorment fails because nobody seems to be interested in them. A farewell to Warhol's aesthetics, deemed useless in the periphery of Europe, ends the video.

The title comes from Ariel Pink's song with the same title which can also be heard in the background. The work was acquired by EKKM for one conceptual dollar.
9c6ef8606c28d223ec8e1526c56a9162605b843f: Kaili-Angela Konno (b. 1970 in the town of Valga) has participated as a painter in numerous exhibitions since 1997. Konno holds a bachelor's degree in painting from the Estonian Academy of Arts (1999). "I have sought internal and external shifts in space and in the person. This lets things appear from an unusual viewpoint, which creates connections and convergences on a new plane, which ultimately balances into a whole," the artist herself says in explanation of her work, in an interview given to Vano Allsalu, the current president of the Estonian Artists' Association.
329dbd76022e4f4fdc0ee262f3d04070cfedb34f: Half-figure of a bespectacled man sitting in a brown waistcoat and shirt, his body slightly turned to the right, head tilted slightly to the left, in three-quarter profile to the right, a sharp gaze directed at the viewer; hands resting loosely in his lap. A straight, short, slightly protruding nose, grayish-mixed hair combed back, a wrinkled face with a determined chin, lips with downturned corners of the mouth, all modelled with sharp straight lines. At lower left, at the corner of the table, a small flat bottle with a dark cork. A greyish-green neutral background above, below geometricised dark green and brown surfaces.
73a27f68fa74928f4c057c4db23e7ff01e805ced: As if placed on a stage, among the scenery, are two legless (with wooden legs) figures in carnival costumes. On the left one, a hat with a red base, bells on the edge, a black mask, a wide lace collar, a red doublet, a white apron, a black scarf around the neck, a wooden sword in hand. On the right one, a golden-yellow wig, an enormous mouth instead of a face, a white lace collar, a blue blouse, a red coat and trousers. The sleeve of the coat is attached to the scenery with a large safety pin. In the right corner, a white goose on wheels cut out of plywood; in the centre, at the edge of the scenery, a loaf of bread covered with seeds.
48845a3e94dcbf468cdd0e0127d5b54d45d59d23: Marta Stratskas (b.1986) is an Estonian artist living in Berlin. She graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a master's degree in painting. Marta's bold and textured paintings combine old Baroque and Gothic elements, contrasting them with contemporary pop motifs, interweaving sacred, extreme human conditions and borderline situations. In her works theme and execution merge. A study of colour, light, and the presence/intention of the artist in the moment. Marta Stratskas has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2014 and has participated in exhibitions since 2009.
12cccc4fb5605433ca6218f3a7d4e473255cc10b: Eldar Jakubov (b. 1987 in Tallinn) is a young artist who graduated in 2015 with a master's degree in installation and sculpture from the Estonian Academy of Arts. The artist on his work: "I remove unimportant objects and concentrate my gaze on the human body, on its character, mood, and above all on relationships between people. I am interested in society and the processes that make it work, and the illusions that give us the feeling that we understand this system. Every social problem and illusion, as well as physical ones, can be discussed piece by piece."
6ba23fd4514735506be0223f4dab2ffc0473c480: Print with a view of the Emajõgi River and the Stone Bridge in Tartu. In the foreground, the left bank of the Emajõgi with two rowboats. In the middle of the river, a single-masted sailboat with reefed sails. On the far bank a wooden fence along the shore. On the corner of the Great Market a three-storey stone building, to its left a low Classicist building with arched windows. On the right, the Stone Bridge across the river. The Stone Bridge is carried by two semicircular piers made of square stones, between them a lifting section with a two-arch-like gate structure with three openings. In the middle, in the background, the Great Market and the town hall. On the right, across the bridge, the tower of St. John's Church.
a5ebbc174444d9f5a441c2caf30d9621e681093a: In the upper part, two carpets are depicted with quotations from Russian painting (Three Bogatyrs, Alyonushka) painted onto the carpet coverings. In the central part, the crossroads of Viljandi town centre, at the corner of a light-coloured two-storey building, formed in relief. On the roof of the building a dark red velvet flag. In front of the building on the left a relief street lamp post, a truck with a black box approaching from the left. In the lower part of the painting, the corner of a carpet with colourful ornament. On it, a small girl in a carnival costume with a yellow creature, with the inscription below: "Õ-JUTA". In the lower right corner, a palm tree on a stand and a car drawn with a child's hand.
88aad241ed6622ce18a9f1e4be04e329dddcbbaa: Helina Menning is a freelance painter and interior architect who lives and works in Tallinn. She graduated in 2011 with a degree (BA) in interior architecture, and completed further studies in painting at the Estonian Academy of Arts (2017, 2019). In H. Menning's creative self-expression, the disciplines of interior architecture, design, and painting are blended together. Her inner creativity and the expression of feelings in her painting are characterised by an abstract, expressive painting style and a slightly textured painting surface. H. Menning has had several solo and group exhibitions in Estonia.
31c8d865dd7098c76cadab7f7e4734ead7aabdbc: Margus Meinart (b. 1969 in Tartu), after graduating from the Estonian Institute of Humanities in 1993, began studying furniture design and restoration at the Tartu Art School, graduating in this field in 1998. In 1994–1995 he studied painting in Norway, and in 1991–1996 in Tartu in Konrad Mägi's studio. Margus Meinart received the "Pallas" scholarship in 1998, as well as the Aino Järvesoo scholarship. He has been a member of the "Pallas" Art Society since 1994, and Meinart also belongs to the Tartu Artists' Union and the Tartu Restorers' Club.
145f04c235ab64ef325bc841c4a403009763f959: 2014 – Artist's Day. Vehicle painting. Narva Museum Art Gallery 2019 – Winner of the Street Art Battle. Jõhvi Street Art Day.
