bcff0bce5ce1ab1946b1c0bf4d65442db8941879: On the right a rocky seashore, further back on a hillock ruins, on the end wall of which are men's figures around a bonfire. On the left fishing boats with sails at anchor, beyond them the sea. Upper left the moon (pastose), from which a gleam of light falls onto the sea. Dark, sombre colour tones.
209ade17783429319167906a174228b26289e764: A battlefield, in the foreground a bunker, from which two men are emerging. The first with a helmet on his head and, between the coat collar, the insignia of the SS corps visible. On the left 6 men beside the bunker and on the right 2. Behind the snowy field a row of destroyed buildings is visible.
ff302d300d26a24e4bdb1ca6e36da64d1eac18f5: A winding body of water bounded by a dark contour, with a bright red evening sky and a glowing solar disc above on a black background. In the lower right quarter a wheel-shaped white prohibition sign with a red diagonal stripe. Expressive style, black-red contrasts.
7e848e4d0f49438a284bff411149d3214cef3c53: Against a background of geometric shapes in blue tones, a grey trellis-like construction converging from the right centre towards both corners on the left. In the right centre a cluster of young people depicted in black and white. Black and white splashes across the surface.
ae98e73146ee30652db3fba0839b8832a9644e54: Under a sky covered with greyish cumulus clouds, a brownish-green clearing, behind it curly deciduous trees with wind-bent crowns. On the left, two house roofs are visible through the greenery. Painted vigorously, in the sky area the plywood is in places left uncovered by paint.
c2b9e2f6f6bb17f59bb06cb1d6c84913fa24357f: Sitting in a row, three round-faced women in long red robes, with kerchiefs on their heads. All the women have children in their laps, the middle one is breastfeeding a child. On the left edge, part of a jester figure. The painting is smoothly painted in reddish-brown tones.
cae54b0e1d150af88b4316678c2d43bc46cb91df: On a small brown and ochre chequered table a tall vase widening towards the top, of glass, with red, pink and yellow roses. Throughout the picture the canvas shows through the sparse layer of paint. The background covered with sparse brushstrokes of purplish-red.
a0822f3769668ee0415ad68f811bc32ee45e0baf: On a dark hilly landscape, in the foreground on the left a white horse in profile, on the right five sheep grazing. In the background solitary stones, on the right a stunted pine. On the horizon solitary trees against a background of a cumulus-cloud sky. Painted in dabs, pastosely.
f23f0220a1c50747a46b9aeb439bf6a5d4c53c8b: Abstract composition: on a dark brown background a dark blue rectangle filling almost the entire picture surface, covered with lighter blue intermingled lines so that, at regular intervals, horizontal blue stripes run across the picture surface.
d843210e31f986fba45d20d5b44e63015b6845f1: White, yellow, blue, green and red geometric surfaces, separated from one another by thick black contour lines. A large part of the picture surface is white, which is divided by a web of black lines into a mosaic of geometric shapes.
4bee76071946425a737ba582b64456b2ba927dbf: In the foreground a city street receding into depth (Müürivahe tn.) with houses on both sides. On the right, above the roofs, the town wall is visible, ending in a point - a defence tower. On the street two groups of people are visible. In the foreground on the right, on the side of a house, a sign "Söögimaja".
91539381813e8356ade98f7c4ae3095f5243b6b0: In the foreground a river running from left to right with a road along the bank. On it two workmen repairing a protective fence along the riverbank. In the centre three horsemen, further away from them a group of walkers. In the background, on both sides of the river, a settlement bounded by steep mountain slopes.
3a1fb9e4dddeddd08957ab6a9e7406f8d816488a: Portrait of a serviceman: the head of a young soldier with a garrison cap, seen head-on, the cap tilted towards the right ear, a five-pointed star on the front of the cap; an elongated face, straight nose, pouting lips, protruding ears; the head rests on a rectangular, open-sided iron stand.
c271b3e7800309a4859eb21e69bf19ad31e4c98d: A luminous road leads from the front left to the back right onto a hilly surface. In the foreground juniper bushes on the grass. From left to right a pole fence, with an opening in it below the road. In the centre, on a higher hillock, 3 pines in one group and 2 pines singly. The sky cloudy.
644d73df1597b15d339e072607e31624d995a053: A half-profile portrait of a young woman or girl. The girl sits sideways towards the portraitist, wearing clothing in a dark blue tone. Her dark hair is tied together over the crown of the head with a red ribbon. Behind the girl's back, on the wall, a hung painting is visible.
f61e1be69d040f88309d04d347c7f33a241ff615: Active in the 19th century in Tallinn as a painter, drawing teacher, art dealer and publisher of lithographs. His best-known work is the series of lithographs "Album von Reval" (max 29 different sheets). The lithographs were printed by F. Schwabe in Berlin
0de59075efb507a5719f2364d7dffa6bb473a837: Born in Moscow into a family of intellectuals with Russian and Polish roots, he arrived in Tallinn with his lawyer parents in 1956. Having finished Tallinn Secondary School No. 19, he entered the Estonian State Art Institute, completing his studies in 1972 as a sculptor.
b9ddaa884a0c1f0238b1c918e2f2028b5063ccc0: Maarja Nõmmik (b. 1991) has obtained a bachelor's and master's degree in painting at the University of Tartu. In addition, she furthered her studies in painting, multimedia and conceptual textile at the Strzemiński Academy of Fine Arts in Łódź, Poland.
cadc7f757b7a866575b2a71b971485d866db4204: Illusion of a view through a window with a ribbed blind, in stripes of light and shadow. The painted surface is divided vertically into two, 1/3 on the left being the shaded side. On the right, the stripes of light become wider and lighter towards the centre. Bluish and grey transitional tones.
49da5125cbbf29f13b38c1306cc645fe8ce661cf: collage attached to cardboard: a light-coloured patterned panel with a rectangular opening containing a woman's half-figure on film. Upper right two red roses and on the left a pair of hands (magazine cut-outs). Below, a ring with spiral soldering, above which is a man's dark half-figure
3a1e76006013c21c60ef0db88401d71b88816670: Chest portrait of an older man, in profile. Strong, slightly hooked nose, narrow, pressed-together lips, small, deep-set eyes. Sharply defined wrinkles around the mouth. Wearing a hat on his head, a dark, brownish coat. Dark colour scheme.
850771859d14a06f41edcd81abb2ac54df645c25: Two elongated, slender male nudes with strong muscles standing side by side in frontal view: legs apart, body weight on the left legs, upper bodies turned to the right, heads tilted to the left. Both arms bent at the elbows at shoulder height
b5f9282580e54804fc066b6cdbb1789b5f5fdb5c: Portrait of a fair-haired girl with short light hair and dark blue eyes, in a three-quarter turn to the left. Wearing a collarless dress in blue tones. Background in bluish-grey tones, painted with clearly distinguishable long brushstrokes.
0e671b3bed9b543ffb67f5d43b05ca93cf462419: Three figures in cubistically geometricised form, surrounded by elements of musical instruments. The figure on the right, a woman with closed eyes, gloved left hand in front; the figure on the left with yellow skin tone; the rear figure swarthy, wearing a red cap.
bc03360791f4aa199aa4902da0a8773d9a9060b0: Four nude figures move across the picture surface from right to left in a dance ecstasy, making writhing bodily movements. Background dull blue, ground green, bodies brownish, lower right a red disc. The sheet consists of several pieces glued together.
642d4ddfb4a10e0a057a8a34b6ae57212d5ba2dd: On a grey background densely worked with a brush, in the lower right corner a composition of geometric shapes, consisting of a thick black vertical line, a grey egg with a red outline, a segment, and a yellowish base surface.
9811da67cb99c937fb257d56a692f83e88b36481: Half-figure of a seated older woman in profile to the left. Right hand resting on a table. ffec5e21681728b2b3e123224377d4a22fc38882: In the upper part of the painting, against a light blue background, a large multicoloured striped fish in flight. In places the surface is impasto, in places (in the shape of the fish) the canvas is left uncovered.
055a75b79422fecf0b3810563b607a4f6234ed61: View of an open sea: in the foreground on the left, cliffs rising out of the sea with two staffage figures sitting on them. On the right, a light blue sea reaching to the horizon with a lone sailing boat. Above the horizon, yellow, and higher up a dull blue sky.
39d3c32e7c31be582c554b9be39d21cd3daf0250: On a grey shimmering background marked with whitish brushstrokes, and on a base painted in light nuanced tones and impasto, a pink vase holding a narrow, upward-directed bouquet of red flowers and green leaves.
c28f907529d50cb95988587875c37b349f596a98: A panoramic landscape in intense blue, red and yellow tones, painted as a combination of almost abstract expressive patches of colour. On the right, above the horizontal centre line, a bright blue body of water. The sky dark blue.
1b037577a0a36fcc393b86796c18774d17ca1a1d: In the foreground, a seated woman in folk costume - a herder with a goat and three cows (two sleeping). In the background, fields with grain stacks, on the left a lake fringed with groves of trees and suburban houses; on the right a view of the town of Viljandi. The sky cloudy, the edge pinkish.
f68868405b3766b648110f2cf0642527cacbfd9e: In the foreground on the right one can discern a large tree with drooping, curving branches, against a background of an abstractly rendered hilly landscape covered with groves of trees. In bright blue, red and yellow tones. Painted with broad, expressive brushstrokes.
bc0866636197ed84f169d78a2ae0ea4a2333c80e: The yellow background of the canvas is painted crosswise in a checkered pattern with regular broad brush strokes in white, so that three yellow vertical stripes remain visible in the centre of the painting. The painting is bordered on the sides by a regular row of nails covered with paint.
9ea0e5340838475543c8d28be3a5c704ad88cfc5: Female nude with the head turned towards the right shoulder, the top of the head and the feet cut off; the right arm cut off at mid-upper-arm and the left above the head; strong hips, the form between navel and breasts hollowed into a narrow band; mounted on a rectangular wooden base
6d9a875c9f2a17242abd0c8fbf85d15d6243ebd9: Face of a young woman in frontal view. The area around the eyes made up in strong blue-brown tones. Dark hair. Glossy red lips. The right hand touches the left cheek, the thumb with a lacquered nail spreading lipstick from the corner of the mouth. Dark background.
6091c5ffcdb5d49f5c351035dccb27d7f7792b2c: A low sandy sea shore, with brown streaks in a greyish overall tone. The surface of the water light greenish in the evening light, with dark blue streaks. Low on the horizon, dark blue clouds with a bright orange patch in the middle. Higher up, the sky in sunset colours.
fd2f3862a219225c37959561d1f3331f9bb1dbe3: brown leather folder, on the front cover a silver plate attached with a depiction of the Lalev factory (etching), an engraved German-language dedication and signatures, inner pockets on the inside of the front cover, at the bottom a company mark, in the centre an inner cover attached with a leather strip

6bebba77400209b249360aabba446f711cbfd4e2: Osvald Timmas was born 17.09.1913 in Saaremaa, Kärla parish, Pai village, died 27.10.2005 in Toronto, Canada. He studied in the humanities branch of Saaremaa Joint Gymnasium and at the Tondi Military School in Tallinn, which he completed in 1934. He then studied at the Estonian Consumer Cooperatives Central Union (ETK) Cooperative School and 1937–1944 at the Faculty of Economics of the University of Tartu. He was a member of the fraternity Rotalia. In art, he took private lessons in 1939–1942 from Nikolai Kummits and in 1942–1944 from Günther Reindorff. In 1944 he fled together with his wife Erika to Sweden, where he worked in the field of life insurance. 1947–1949 he studied on illustration courses in Stockholm. In 1951 he moved to Toronto, Canada, where he likewise worked in life insurance. In 1956 he received Canadian citizenship. In the 1960s Timmas drew attention with watercolours depicting geological strata and the underwater world, as well as views through a microscope. In 1972 he devoted himself entirely to art. In 1961–1968 Timmas was president of the Colour and Form Society and in 1971–1975 vice-president of the Ontario Society of Artists; Timmas was also a founding member of the Estonian Arts Centre in Ontario in 1974. In 1973 O. Timmas was elected a member of the Royal Canadian Academy of Arts. In 1977 he received a decoration from the British Queen. In 2005 O. Timmas was awarded the Order of the White Star, 5th Class, of the Republic of Estonia. In his will he established the Erika and Osvald Timmas Memorial Fund, with the aim of preserving and developing Estonian culture and art. This fund has, for example, supported the construction of Kumu, the activities of the Tartu Art Museum, the exhibition of Estonian exile art in 2010–2011 in Tallinn, Tartu and elsewhere. Solo exhibitions in Estonia took place: in 1990 at the Adamson-Eric Museum, in 2003 at the National Library and the Saaremaa Museum.
1cad0abe1478fad98e033affa1f1f60ba87dd40f: He became, in the 1970s, a renovator of Estonian modernist sculpture. Alongside his formal searches based on the interaction of plastic volumes and space, an exceptional striving for elegance appeared in his work. Soans has managed to poeticise bronze as a precious sculptural material, and his bronze sculptures are created with a pure silhouette effect. He broadened the thematic range and communicativeness of Estonian sculpture, bringing existential reflections into his works about the possibilities of man and humanity in a technology-based, alienating world. Soans can be regarded as an intellectual and teacher, followed by both his students and colleagues. The general public knows him mainly as a monumentalist. He has created more than 30 monuments and public sculptures and immortalised great national figures: for example, the monuments to A. H. Tammsaare (1978), Voldemar Panso (1980) and Michel Sittow (1982) in Tallinn, the monuments to Kristjan Jaak Peterson (1983) and Jakob Hurt (1994) in Tartu, and the August Gailit monument in Valga (2009). He has also created abstract large-scale forms in Estonia, Finland, the Netherlands and Argentina. Soans's work of recent years is carried by a cheerful intellectual play with the field of meaning of images. The bronze of past decades has been replaced by steel, wood and other less durable materials, as well as ready-made objects. In his spatial installations one encounters recognisable recurring motifs, reflections on the essence of sculpture and its relations with time and space. Jaak Soans is Professor Emeritus of the Estonian Academy of Arts. He has received the honorary title of Meritorious Artist of the ESSR (1980) and People's Artist of the ESSR (1986), the Kristjan Raud Art Prize (1974 and 1986), the Grand Prize of the Riga Sculpture Quadrennial.
3198cca708b437bd4e8257ca51c2f48fae53d0d3: Edgar Viies (1931–2006) is one of the most important Estonian sculptors of the 20th century. His innovative formal explorations and modern choice of materials (aluminium, clinker, welded iron, sheet metal and concrete) marked the beginning of the modern era in Estonian sculpture in the 1960s. His work brought, for the first time in the post-war years, a stylistically pure abstract formal culture to Estonian sculpture. He appeared with modernly generalised portrait works in exhibition halls already at the end of the 1950s, attracting attention with his unusually pure silhouette effect and having an influence that invited emulation. Quite a few of his works from the 1960s–1980s have become classics of Estonian art. Besides the aesthetic problematics that were especially important to Viies in the first half of his creative work, the experiential quality of his works and their relation to universal human spiritual and emotional life must also be considered valuable. He brought creative experimentation into the comparatively conservative and rather dull sculpture of the early 1960s, directing sculptors' attention to the relations between space, form and material. It can be said that it was precisely Edgar Viies who gave impetus to decorative sculpture, which at that time existed in a kind of suspended animation. His numerous free works belong to the golden fund of Estonian modernism. Viies's public sculptures in Tallinn, Tartu and Viljandi remain captivating to this day. The best known of these are the monuments to Johann Köler (1976), Jaan Koort (1983) and Friedebert Tuglas (1986), the "Mermaid" (1981) adorning Viru Square, and the soaring "Pegasus" (1963) at the café on Harju Street in Tallinn, which was, for several generations, the first modernist interior sculpture known in Estonia. Edgar Viies studied in 1951–1952 at the ESSR State Art Institute.
a07d5ad9e367f0b27eff92b8440b015b14e82a7a: Painter, graphic artist and pedagogue. At the beginning of his creative career he drew pictures of political content for Estonian satirical publications, including caricatures (pseudonym Vaikne). The first work to attract attention was the figure "Tulekandja" ["The Fire-Bearer"] on the cover of the "Noor-Eesti" ["Young Estonia"] I album. He made illustrations and design based on Art Nouveau stylised ornament and symbolic imagery for G. Suits's poetry collection "Tulemaa" (1913) and the "Noor-Eesti" V album (1915). While in Norway he focused on landscape painting ("Decorative Norwegian Landscape", 1908). In his early painterly work the influence of symbolism appears, especially in national-romantic compositions based on legendary material and depicting heroic scenes of struggle. Triik was one of the most highly regarded portraitists, emphasising spirituality, inner dignity and dramatism (K. Mägi 1908, Juhan Liiv 1909, M. Levin, I. Menning and Viktoria Martna 1910). Later his manner of expression became more expressive compared to the initial one (portrait of A. Laikmaa, 1913). The freehand drawings "Märter" ["Martyr"] (1913) and "Katastroof" ["Catastrophe"] (1917) express the split personality and tragedy characteristic of expressionism. The drawings "Vabaduse sünd" ["The Birth of Freedom"] (1919) and "Ulguv koer" ["The Howling Dog"] (1921) reflect events after the First World War. From the second half of the 1920s comes a number of drawn, individually characterised portraits (F. Tuglas 1928, H. Raudsepp 1932, G. Suits 1933); in the 1930s he again cultivated landscape painting more, the most outstanding being the landscapes made near Paldiski at Leetse-Lepiku and winter views of Tartu. He also created applied graphics (the "Siuru" publisher's mark, 1917) and the design for the Cross of Liberty (1920).

He was born as the eldest son of Karl August Senff, drawing teacher at the University of Tartu, and studied at the University of Tartu from 1823–27. He was meant to become professor of architecture at the University of Tartu. On 12 December 1827 K. J. Senff received a silver medal for answering philosophical questions; as a student he compiled a textbook on perspective for self-taught landscape painters (published in 1825). In 1827 he received the degree of Candidate of Philosophy at the University of Tartu (the prize-winning work "Systematische Darstellung der Hauptsätze der Geometrie im Raume" was printed at the university's expense). In 1829 he received an imperial travel stipend for 3 years from the funds of the Russian Ministry of Public Education and travelled to Jena, where he obtained a doctorate in philosophy, then went to Prague and Vienna, where he studied architecture. In 1831 he stayed in Munich. He made 10 aquatint illustrations for his work "St Vitus Cathedral in Prague" (published in Berlin in 1831). Together with his uncle Karl Adolf Senff he travelled to Italy in 1831, where he lived in Rome, visited Naples and Pompeii. On the way back he fell ill with nervous fever and was taken unconscious to Milan, where he died.

His works are held at the Art Museum of Estonia, 72 of them (3 of disputed authorship) and at the University of Tartu Library. Bibl: G. H. Vogel, manuscript of an article, 2011.

In 1923 E. Ole was a founding member of the avant-garde Estonian Artists' Group, and from 1927 belonged to the Central Union of Estonian Visual Artists, later becoming the union's vice-chairman. E. Ole visited Paris repeatedly, first in 1927. In 1937 he travelled with Juhan Raudsepp to England, Belgium, France, Italy and Central Europe. In 1943 the artist fled Estonia for Finland, and from 1944 lived in Sweden, in Vällingby in western Stockholm, working at the Nordic Museum. In 1946 Ole undertook a trip to Lapland together with Eduard Wiiralt.
4bb86f26aa0c8a1322ad7d845f4caa70424c1037: Born according to the old calendar on 29 November 1795 at Teenuse (Stenhusen) manor in Läänemaa, studied 1804-1810 at the Herrnhuter school in Neuwied and 1811-1812 at Tallinn Cathedral School. Served 1812-1820 in the Russian army, worked 1820-1822 in the archive of the University of Tartu, studied under the guidance of C. A. Senff at the university's drawing school. In 1822 travelled in Berlin and Dresden, until 1827 furthered his education in art in Italy. In 1824 met the artist A. L. Richter and in 1825 travelled together with him, staying in Civitella. Lived 1827-1829 at Teenuse manor, in 1829 settled in Tartu, where in 1835 he founded a wood engraving workshop. Began the series of copper engravings (+etchings) dedicated to the history of Livonia "Viiskümmend pilti...", of which the 1st issue appeared in 1839 and the 2nd issue in 1842, plus two more sheets. Produced graphic teaching aids, painted portraits and altarpieces (1835 Saarde church, 1837 Ruhja church, 1845 Põlva church). Maydell's paintings for Tallinn's St. John's Church have been destroyed. He was also a sculptor, a designer of silverwork and woodwork. From 1829 he worked on the restoration of Tallinn's St. Olaf's Church (completed 1840). Died according to the old calendar on 6 September 1846 in Tallinn, buried in the Kullamaa churchyard.
921b540ad81e44d2ffb0814194da7209834552e0: Before World War II, August Vomm's oeuvre consisted mainly of portrait busts and about ten labour-intensive gravestones. He has portrayed Ruts Bauman, Ants Lauter, Hugo Laur, Gustav Ernesaks, Romulus Tiitus, Ferdi Sannamees and others. As one of the few artists who spent the war years in his homeland, August Vomm adapted to the new demands already in the first post-war years. In 1945 he joined a brigade of sculptors, creating reliefs symbolising the union republics for the Estonia Theatre. In 1947 a monument to those fallen in the Great Patriotic War was completed in Viljandi, in 1952 the Lenin monument in Tartu, again created by the brigade method, was unveiled, as well as, together with Lagle Israel, the memorial to Nikolai Burdenko on Toome Hill in Tartu. His monuments to the revolutionary figures Johannes Vares-Barbarus and Hans Pöögelmann in Tallinn have since been relocated. For the Lenin jubilee exhibition in 1970, Vomm created a giant oak portrait bust of V. I. Lenin, for which he, together with Elmar Kits and Avo Keerend, received the state prize and the honorary title of Merited Artist of the Estonian SSR, as well as all-Union recognition in the press.
8470741393273cc79a68c39d145e493be540f3a0: Kristjan TEDER (1901, Kuigatsi parish, Tartumaa – 1960, Tartu) was an Estonian painter and gardener who practised mainly flower painting, and to a lesser extent landscape, portrait and genre painting. His early work is New Objectivist, characterised by clearly defined forms and a dull brownish colour scheme. In the 1930s his manner of painting became impressionistically nuanced, the colouring bright and, in some works, vividly coloured, and the depictive style at times shows a naivist roughness. In the flower paintings made after World War II, Teder focused attention on bringing out spatiality and modelling with light and shadow. Alongside baroquely lush flower paintings, he also produced landscapes and townscapes in a more restrained colour range. In the second half of the 1950s Teder painted mainly vividly coloured flower pictures and landscapes. Teder received his art education at the Pallas Art School, first under Konrad Mägi and then under Ado Vabbe, and in Paris at Vassili Shukhaev's private academy. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
11f5ac7b34e532b754d64b63201fd11a82028aa5: Illimar Paul (b. 1945) began his graphic art studies at the Estonian Academy of Arts (ERKI) in 1964. He continued his studies at the Leipzig Higher School of Graphic Arts and Book Design, from which he graduated with a diploma in 1971. He has participated in more than 300 joint exhibitions both at home and abroad, and has had 68 solo exhibitions. "Illimar Paul's cityscapes in the hyperrealist style of the 1970s, made in the serigraphy technique, belong not only to the classics of our graphic art, but were at the time among the most innovative works of graphic art, both in terms of technique and manner of depiction. In his work Paul has used several techniques – besides silkscreen printing, other graphic techniques (linocut), but also watercolour, coloured pencil drawing, mixing them together, moving from a two-dimensional mode of presentation into space, making three-dimensional collages etc., but his love of detail has remained to this day. Moreover: detail has always meant something very personal and emotional to him." Reet Varblane, 2015.
d305f111a5881286f25e04a98be8cf53d27ef660: VÕERAHANSU, Johannes (1902, Keo, Raikküla parish – 1980, Tallinn). Johannes Võerahansu is considered one of the most outstanding Estonian landscape and genre painters. The light-filled, silvery-coloured paintings poeticising Estonian life and nature, made in the second half of the 1930s, are among the top works of this genre. The artist also depicted nature expressively as the background for paintings on the theme of farm work made during World War II. From the very beginning of his creative path, Võerahansu also practised portrait painting, several of which belong to the classics of Estonian portraiture. In the 1960s-1970s he moved away from painting and focused more on drawings. Võerahansu received his art education at Ants Laikmaa's studio school and under Ado Vabbe at the Pallas Art School. Later he worked as a teacher at the Higher Courses of Fine Art, at the Tartu State Art Institute, at the Tartu Art School, and as a professor at the Estonian State Art Institute. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
a884e2671b953555b04cb63229f9874c1efeeb6f: Self-taught portrait photographer from Ida-Viru. EU Commission photo contest "Me and Europe" prize place 2013 Nikon photo contest "Friendly Estonia" 2013 1st place Pentax portrait photo contest of the year 2015 3rd place Louvre Museum's 2015 group exhibition "Exposure awards" Sony World Photography Awards December 2015 winner Global Encounters Snapshot contest 2015 Personal photo exhibition at the University of Tartu Narva College gallery 2016 Pentax portrait photo contest of the year 2016 2nd place Sony World Photography Awards National Awards 2nd place 2017 Sony World Photography Awards group exhibition Somerset House, London 2017 Nikon 2018 contest "Kuupilt" (Moon Picture) winner in October 'What Lies Beneath' 500px group exhibition Toronto 2019 Bridgeman Studio Award January 2019 2020 shortlist Group exhibition ZE+F, Objekt Multimedia Future Hub, Narva 2020.
ce9eec9aa806c842b73767da00965dbc4a45adc9: Grigori (Georg) Tõnisson was born in Pärnu as the son of a gymnasium caretaker. In 1911 his landscape vignettes and stories were printed in Postimees's supplement Sädemed, and soon his caricatures appeared in the newspapers Kilk and Meie Tallinna Ajaleht. In 1913 he moved to Tallinn and went to work for the magazine Leek. In 1915 he was mobilised into the Tsarist army, and in 1915 fell into German captivity. In 1918 he returned to Tallinn and, together with Hendrik Saar (Kivilombi Ints), founded the satirical magazine "Sipelgas" (published 15 issues), for which Gori was both a prose and picture author (in woodcut). From 1920 he was a member of the editorial staff of the newspaper Vaba Maa, and in 1938 of the editorial staff of Rahvaleht. In 1941 Gori was arrested; after his release he worked at the newspapers Rahva Hääl and Sirp ja Vasar. During the German occupation he was imprisoned twice; the artist's date of death is 7.10.1944, the cause of which (suicide?) has remained unresolved. Buried at Tallinn's Siselinna Cemetery.
960606cdeb5a2d5ac8b876e2abf5224689d929a7: Kuno Veeber was born as the second of six sons of the manager of Adila manor. He studied medicine at the University of Tartu and served as a medic in the Estonian War of Independence. His art studies began at Ants Laikmaa's studio, continued under Nikolai Triik and Jaan Koort. In 1922-1924 Veeber studied at the Pallas Art School and graduated in its first class in 1924. In 1923 he stayed in Germany, in Dresden, living at the home of the artist Magnus Zeller. In 1924-1926 he furthered his studies in Paris under André Lhote, being the senior student of his studio. In Paris Kuno Veeber's style as an artist took shape. In 1926 he married Agathe Kanto (Veeber). In 1927 Veeber spent half a year in Italy on a Cultural Endowment scholarship, copying Tintoretto's wall painting in the Doge's Palace in Venice. Kuno Veeber took his own life on 1 January 1929, buried at Tallinn's Rahumäe Cemetery. The gravestone monument, made by Jaan Koort, has been vandalised.
595147398b169ce0bfd3009813f5a0f697207083: Ballerina, ballet master, ballet pedagogue; Honoured Artist of the Estonian SSR (ENL) 1940; Honoured Worker (ETL) 1959; graduated from the Tallinn Russian gymnasium; studied dance in 1921-25 at E. Litvinova's studio; 1928-29 in Berlin under V. Gsovsky; 1932 in Paris under O. Preobrazhenskaya, and 1934-36 in Riga and 1943-44 at the Moscow choreography school; performed in Riga and Stockholm, was 1925-30 the ballet soloist of the Flemish Royal Opera Theatre in Antwerp, then in Central Europe; was 1933-35 ballet master and soloist of the Liepāja Opera Theatre; in 1937 dance teacher at the Paris cabaret Folies Bergère and performed in 1938 with H. Fleming's troupe in Italy; was 1940-41 "Estonia" ballet pedagogue and director, and there 1944-51 ballet director and ballet master, belonged to ERKA; initiated the founding of TKK, was its director in 1946-48 and 1951-65, and until 1966 a teacher of classical dance; Honoured Cultural Worker of the ESSR 1959; Soviet Estonia Prize 1948.
1e17c096db4f3b2ac1a2f4ae32c48337fe04e5d5: Graduated in 1915 with a silver medal from the Tallinn Girls' Crown Gymnasium, then studied in 1915–1916 at J. Bagajev's architecture courses in Petersburg, and in 1916–1918 architecture at the Petrograd Women's Polytechnic Institute. Worked in 1918–1919 as an assistant architect at the Tallinn city government. In 1919 exhibited for the first time at the art exhibition of the Pallas art society in Tartu and improved her skills in painting with Nikolai Triik. Worked in 1920–1921 as a drawing teacher at the Tartu Teachers' Seminary. Stayed repeatedly in 1922–1923 at sanatoriums in Germany. Exhibited from 1925 at exhibitions in Estonia, as well as in Helsinki, Riga, Berlin, Amsterdam, etc. Was a member of the Central Union of Estonian Fine Artists from 1925, a member of the Estonian Artists' Group in 1931–1935, a member of the Applied Artists' Union in 1936, and a member of the ESSR Artists' Union from 1946.
33231dd856dbbe3ff8fdf9fe7e5682371d859b01: Studied until 1933 at the Hugo Treffner Gymnasium in Tartu (drawing teacher Eduard Ole), graduated in 1934 from the Tallinn Boys' Secondary School (Realgymnasium), studied in 1934–38 at the State School of Applied Art in decorative painting. Worked from 1936 at the Tallinn Workers' Theatre. Designed puppet productions at the Drama Theatre from 1937, worked at the same theatre (with an interruption) until 1950 (as chief artist in 1948–50); in 1946–48 was also the set designer for the Youth Theatre. Worked in 1950–61 at the Industrial Combine of the Estonian SSR Theatre Union, later worked as an applied graphic artist (1968–86 at the experimental combine Bit). Designed books, for example Perrault's "Punamütsike" ("Little Red Riding Hood") (1942), Kreutzwald's "Puulane ja tohtlane" (1945); as a fiction designer made cover designs for the Estonian SSR Theatre Union's publication "Eesti NSV Teatrid" (1957–60). Estonian Encyclopedia.
97a81bcfb7980bf38c5ae6c4492d7242b3fc1f59: Miina Vilo (b. 1995) is an Estonian artist working mainly in Tallinn and Tartu. She has obtained a bachelor's degree in painting from the Pallas University of Applied Sciences (2025) and is a member of the art group MULTINEKTAR (founded 2024). Vilo's work has been characterized as an emotional and multifaceted synthesis of pop art, surrealism and symbolist elements. In 2023/24 she was awarded the D'Albret Collection: The Reiss von Filski Trust prize. The jury highlighted her ability to tell stories through symbols that invite the viewer on a journey of dreams and reflections, noting that the artist's individuality is noticeably present in every work. Vilo has actively participated in exhibitions and art auctions. More information and a complete CV can be found on the artist's website: www.miinavilo.com/cv.
96820cdd654736a2dd18f6489a7f9b9e3f1cc82d: Esko Lepp was born as the son of a blacksmith. Studied in 1935–1940 in Tallinn at the State School of Applied Art, graphics and applied graphics (instructor G. Reindorff). Was in the service of the Estonian National Museum (ERM). Improved his skills in 1940–1941 in Tartu at the Konrad Mägi-named State Higher Art School. In 1941 joined a destruction battalion. During World War II worked in Russia at a kolkhoz and a factory, in 1942 joined the Red Army, in 1943 was called up to the collective of Estonian artists in Yaroslavl, was also a front-line draughtsman. In 1943–1948 studied graphics in Moscow at the Surikov Art Institute, which he completed as a student of P. Pavlinov specializing in wood engraving. In 1948–1951 Lepp was a lecturer at the Tallinn State Art Institute (EKA), thereafter a freelance artist. Has created works on war and industrial themes, series of wood engravings, illustrations, watercolours, ex-libris.
2225a912dd656753fa6dfc357dc7f2c3bda1bc67:
Born in Smolensk, Russia; in 1914 the family moved to Estonia. Lived in Laeva. Studied in 1938–40 at the Pallas Art School in Tartu, continued studies until his arrest in the spring of 1945 (instructors included Aleksander Vardi et al.). In 1944 attempted to flee to the West together with Valve Janov and Kaja Kärner. Was until 1954 in a prison camp in the Arkhangelsk region of Russia. From 1958 lived in Tallinn, where he also died. Painter, watercolourist. In 1937–39 was a set designer at the Tartu Workers' Theatre. In the 1960s, like Lembit Saarts, he came close to abstract painting with nature motifs.

Bibl.: Eesti kunsti ajalugu 2, 1970, p. 89; Sirje Helme, Jaak Kangilaski, Lühike Eesti kunsti ajalugu. Tallinn: 1999, pp. 128, 144, 196 (ill. 98). See also: Enn Lillemets "Enne valguse vaheaega", exhibition at the Tartu City Museum 2010.
67431262c03fc468a7523f4b176ecbfb8e8a5d7c: Vano Allsalu's (1967) work, with its forcefully expressive style and distinctive colour world, spans a range of themes from natural elements to states of mind and mythological constructions. It touches on the intimately personal, but also offers interpretations of what is happening in the cultural and social sphere. Allsalu graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in painting (1991) and has worked as a lecturer at the University of Tartu, the Estonian Academy of Arts and Sally Stuudios; in 2013–2025 he was president and vice-president of the Estonian Artists' Association. He has actively participated in exhibitions, received numerous accolades, and his works belong to many museum and private collections. He is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association and the Tartu Artists' Association, and an honorary member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
e0130f62c8417a908ccfa060df090304b97d3287:
Ilmar Kimm was born in Petrograd. Studied in 1927–1935 at an Estonian school in Leningrad, and in 1936–1939 at the art secondary school of the All-Russian Academy of Arts. In 1939–1941 he studied at the All-Russian Academy of Arts. In the autumn of 1941 he was mobilized into the Red Army. He was severely wounded in battle near Velikiye Luki and was demobilized. He resumed his art studies in 1944, graduating in 1948 from the Ilya Repin Art Institute in Leningrad.

He worked in 1948–1951 at the Tartu State Art Institute as a lecturer in painting. In 1952–1988 was a lecturer at ERKI: from 1954 was a docent, from 1965 a professor. In 1963–1983 he was head of the Painting Department, in 1983–1988 he was a consultant professor. From 1951 he was a member of the Artists' Union.
bfffac0e0b9694ab06fc1242409cb1080e2cda74: Kateryna Tyshchenko is a Ukrainian stage designer, costume artist and installation artist who works at the intersection of theatre, spatial practices and contemporary visual art. Her work explores themes of cultural identity, memory, displacement, and the relationship between body and space. She combines traditional stage design methods with experimental installation approaches and digital tools. She is actively engaged in introducing Ukrainian culture in Estonia through artistic and curatorial initiatives. 2022–2026 Estonian Academy of Arts (EKA), Tallinn. Specialty: scenography. 2021–2023, 2025–present Kyiv State Academy of Decorative and Applied Arts and Design (Kyiv National University of Art and Architecture). Specialty: scenography and film scenography.
0811c09bd076a33e9b8af8c9fa12f97e96788448: Whose art teacher was Alexander Schlater. In 1870 and 1875 he stayed for treatment in Germany and Austria. Studied at the philological faculty of the University of Tartu in 1879–1884 (cand. phil.), stayed the same year at a sanatorium in Switzerland, also in France. In 1889 began studies in painting and watercolour. Teachers: Hermann Eschke in Berlin, Charles Way in Lausanne. In 1891–1893 Winkler was a home tutor at Kehtna manor. In 1893 took the teacher's examination at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. In 1898 travelled in Norway, in 1901–1904 in Dalmatia (Croatia) and Italy, in 1903 stayed in Rome. In 1904 a solo exhibition in Tallinn at the Kanuti Guild hall. In 1905 stayed in Dresden. Lived from 1911 in Tallinn, where he led watercolour courses. Died in Dresden on 23.08.1911, was buried near Tallinn at Mõigu cemetery (grave has not been preserved)
7587703d535beaa682f8af21b2ca078e0d879f4c: Tõnis Laanemaa (born 1937) studied painting at the Tartu Art School and graphics at the Estonian State Institute. Initial leader and later member of the innovative Estonian art group of the 1960s, ANK'64. Tõnis began exhibiting with paintings, but gained recognition primarily for his free graphics and posters, though over time he has also exhibited nudes, portraits and abstract compositions. From 1970 onwards Laanemaa has participated in numerous exhibitions in the Baltic states, Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Germany, Russia, the Netherlands. Tõnis Laanemaa belongs to a generation of artists for whom proper drawing from nature is a matter of course. He has also gained recognition as a figure draughtsman and is valued as a drawing teacher.
eaa56c4280f853029b755b048c245e8528d02af2: Singer (baritone); ETL 1945; 1930 Pärnu Boys' Gymnasium; 1938 Tallinn Conservatory (A. Arder's class); was in 1938–39 a soloist of the Vienna Volksoper, in 1942–1943 of the Kassel State Opera, and in 1940–41 and 1944–1988 a soloist of "Estonia"; worked from 1940, with interruptions, as a lecturer at the Tallinn Conservatory; from 1947 professor; performed outside Estonia; was also known as a chamber and oratorio singer; also appeared in film and several films were made about him; first place in Vienna at the international singers' competition in 1938; ESSR Honoured Artist 1945; ESSR People's Artist 1952; USSR People's Artist 1954; Soviet Estonian Prize 1949, 1959, 1967; since 1993 a fund named after him has operated at the Estonia Society to support voice students, and singing competitions are held.
1027c58d2d14458b9bd4cf06852a6701272e0bed: Oskar RAUNAM (1914, Paide – 1992, Tallinn) was an Estonian painter and pedagogue who created realistic landscape, flower and portrait paintings as well as figural compositions; in addition, he published several textbooks, such as "Akvarellimaal" ("Watercolour Painting") (1952) and "Joonistamise ja maalimise õpik" ("Drawing and Painting Textbook") (1961, 1963). Raunam obtained his art education in the decorative painting specialty at the State School of Applied Art, in the drawing and drafting teacher specialty at the Tallinn Pedagogicum, and in painting under the guidance of Johannes Greenberg at the State Higher Art School. Worked at ERKI as a lecturer in drawing and painting, as vice-rector for studies and research, and as head of the General Painting Department. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
ac1291e5b468db90c1fa5ef702db71055872b65e: Aleksander Koemets was born in Moscow into a factory worker's family; at the beginning of the First World War his father returned with his son to their native land, Estonia, where A. Koemets obtained his primary education in Võru and Pärnu. After finishing evening gymnasium in Tartu in 1931, he studied from 1936 at the State School of Applied Art, graduating in 1941 from the J. Koort State School of Applied Art. He furthered his studies in France and Belgium. He was mobilized into the Red Army, was a frontline soldier in the Second World War, and was wounded. He continued his art studies and graduated in 1948 from the Art Institute (EKA) as a book graphic artist. He was an art editor of the publishing house Ilukirjandus ja Kunst, and from 1957-1970 chief artist of the publishing house Kunst.
00a0f8f0003814176d15e68c34cb70536e164abb:
He was born in St. Petersburg as the son of a Swedish father and a Russian mother. In 1916–1917 he studied at the Karl May Gymnasium in St. Petersburg. He came to Estonia in 1921 and finished the Narva Russian Gymnasium. He studied drawing in Tallinn under K. Zeidler and E. Verber. In 1926-1928 he studied graphic art at the State School of Applied Art, and in 1928-1930 painting at Pallas in Tartu (in the studios of N. Triik and A. Vabbe). He furthered his studies in Paris and worked in Estonia as a painter.

He repeatedly visited the Pechory Monastery and, at the age of 19, converted to Orthodoxy. After the Second World War he lived in Paris, entered monastic life, and devoted himself to icon painting. He died at the Holy Spirit skete near Mesnil-Saint-Denis in France.
39b2a561a4074e7aeea546683a54f6e54ec50130: Born in 1974 in Tallinn, Katrin studied the free arts speciality at the Estonian Academy of Arts 2005 – 2012. Latest major exhibitions: "MIS VÄRVI ON ARMASTUS", Kunstiruum Gallery, Tallinn, Estonia (2021), MERRILY, MERRILY, MERRILY, Sakala Centre, Viljandi; Kõnnu Viinaköögi Gallery, Estonia (2021), IN THE LIGHT, Fruttis Gallery, Brazil, Abadiania (2021), 20th Spring Exhibition of Estonian Artists Association ''Kunstnikud maalivad kunstnikke'', Tallinn Art Hall, Estonia (2020), GAIA, Sargvere Manor, Estonia 2020, TROPICAL PASSION, Caminho Encantado Gallery, Brazil, Abadiania and in Kõnnu Viinaköögi Gallery, Estonia.
78c093f7307e42dd6e2b1a70ea60c1686b05b929: At ERKI, in theatre decoration painting, Uno Uibo was a student of Prof. Voldemar Haas and Natalie Mei. His diploma work in 1960 was Anton Chekhov's "The Cherry Orchard". While working at the Pärnu Lydia Koidula Drama Theatre (Endla), he designed such productions as: M. Lassila's "Tark neitsi", Lope de Vega's "Tantsuõpetaja", Th. Wilder's "Meie linnake", K. Saja's "Puutuvid" and others. From 1985, working freelance, U. Uibo practiced watercolour and pastel painting (landscapes, cityscapes, flowers), took part in review exhibitions of theatre artists, and held solo exhibitions in Pärnu, Tallinn and Vaasa. In recent years the artist was a valued teacher at the Pärnu Children's Art School.
8ed6d1d864c2dbf1f00e3a7fd5d6c4d053b3b059: Eva Jänes (1942) graduated from the Tartu Art School in 1962 with a specialty in art teaching, and from the Estonian Art Institute in 1970 with a diploma in painting, specializing in monumental painting. In the first decades of her creative period the artist mostly focused on monumental painting, executing numerous sgraffiti, frescoes, secco works, stained glass windows, and mosaics both in Tallinn and in many other places, mainly in Virumaa. In recent decades the author has devoted herself to easel painting. Jänes has organized dozens of solo exhibitions, participated in national art exhibitions and group exhibitions, and has also arranged numerous exhibitions as a curator.
f462f70710f9247fb160b28ffd0056e015969c49: He studied at the Dresden Academy of Art. He came to Estonia in 1809 at the invitation of the writer August von Kotzebue to be a drawing teacher for his children. Later he worked as a drawing teacher in Hageri at the church school founded by pastor F. Ignatius, and from 1815 at the Tallinn Cathedral School. He retired in 1850 and lived at Kaiu Manor, which belonged to his daughter. He mostly painted altarpieces (in the churches of Tallinn and Kuressaare, in Ambla church and elsewhere), as well as portraits; drawings depicting the ruins of Oleviste after the fire of 1820 also originate from him, after which lithographic sheets were also made. He founded the first lithography workshop in Tallinn. He also fulfilled commissions for portraits of Russian emperors and state portraits.
13bc6651a0ed629702ca4d6a232ea0dd205e7226: Voldemar PEIL (1907, Narva – 1999) was an Estonian theatre artist, who among other things also practiced realistic easel painting (flower and landscape pictures as well as portraits). As a stage designer he designed about three hundred productions. His style is mainly of an everyday character. Alongside painted decorations, Peil also made effective use of projection and lighting. He obtained his art education in the painting speciality at the Pallas Art School under Jaan Vahtra, Voldemar Mellik, Villem Ormisson and Ado Vabbe, and graduated from the art school with the qualification of drawing teacher. In the field of scenography he furthered his education at theatres in Moscow and Leningrad. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
6edea00356756ae1c4f9fbfee5fdbbd1584b76ea: Tõnu Maarand (1940) created, in the late 1960s and in the 1970s, both figure compositions with generalized form and characteristic portraits of Estonian cultural figures. As materials he used bronze as well as wood and hammered copper. In his later work, portraiture takes up an ever greater share of the sculptor's output. In the 1980s–1990s Maarand designed memorials and monuments, as well as gravestone monuments and decorative wall panels. He has also been creatively active in the first decade of the 21st century. He graduated in 1965 from the ESSR State Art Institute as a sculptor and has long been a teacher of sculpture.
34983c84307477064b572501086cb79c0dca85c5: Tiina Tammetalu (1961) prefers to define herself as an artist of fluid identity, transcending media and not to be pigeonholed, who realizes herself simultaneously in several different creative fields: painting, graphic design, illustration, and also curates, among other things, exhibitions of living Estonian painting classics. Tammetalu graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in the painting speciality (1989) and furthered her education in the Estonian Academy of Arts' master's programme in interdisciplinary arts (2003-2006). She has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and elsewhere, and her works belong to several collections. She is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
85a24388f669d0a4e951381f938526e0bcfb38c2: He was born in Tallinn as the son of a merchant, studied in Tartu under A. M. Hagen and in 1834-1839 at the Dresden Academy of Art, and worked in Riga, Tallinn and St. Petersburg. In 1838 he unsuccessfully applied for the position of head of the drawing school at the University of Tartu. In 1845 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Art. From 1850-1871 he was drawing teacher at the Tallinn Cathedral School, and in 1853-54 kept a photo studio in Tallinn. In 1871 he moved to Dresden. In the 1850s he made a series of watercolours depicting coastal Swedes, which were lithographed and published in 1854-1856 in C. F. W. Russwurm's scholarly book (Eibofolke...). He also painted landscapes, genre paintings and cityscapes.
45277a2c6b690e514d791c40d347d5c40a1b406e: In the 1960s Männi abandoned the naturalistically detail-rich style, experimenting with novel materials and striving for a degree of plastic freedom different from before. He was one of the first creators of iron constructions and welded iron sculptures. Interested in contemporary means of expression in sculpture, he created Estonia's first mobile in 1967. With figures rhythmically constructed and conventionally rendered, his work resonates with the so-called hard-edge style that dominated painting in the latter half of the 1960s. Works created in the 1970s from plastic, babbitt metal and tin test the expressive possibilities of new materials.
d0ad0b081fc5540de53b0c2e56c55e5e422246d1: Kippasto has been engaged in art for 25 years and is the winner of the 2016 linocut competition. In addition to Estonia, she has sold her graphic art to Japan, America, Mexico, Ireland and elsewhere. Recognition LAULUPIDU (2014, linocut), TYPA linocut competition 2016 winning work. Participation in exhibitions 2003 Tartu vaade. E-kunstisalong 2016 Linocut competition and exhibition. TYPA, winning work Laulupidu 2018 Linocut competition and exhibition. TYPA 2018 Tartu Art Annual Exhibition 2018. Tartu Art House 2021 Linocut competition and exhibition. TYPA 2023 THKS 25th anniversary review exhibition. St. John's Church 2023 New Art Museum recycling exhibition ANNA UUS ELU.
c7e39f4a5797be19c7a633479b18dd6b480f5685: A Tartu town councillor and painter. He finished gymnasium in Tartu in 1876, and studied oil and watercolour painting in his home town under Woldemar Friedrich Krüger and Julie Wilhelmine Hagen-Schwarz. He continued his art studies in Vienna under William Unger and in Berlin under Gustav Richter. In the years 1880–1897 he ran a brewery in Tartu. He became a citizen of Tartu in 1881 and was a town councillor until 1897. In 1888–1889 he was a Tartu town councillor (raehärra). From 1898–1920 he worked as a bank official in Pskov, Łódź, Šiauliai and Riga. He painted landscapes in oil and watercolour technique. He exhibited in Tartu, Riga, St. Petersburg and Moscow. - Wikipedia.
eb177ce7d9319a4c67c965d1786af9cd8e355902: RANDEL, Felix (1901, Valga – 1977, Tallinn). Estonian painter and caricaturist, who practiced free graphic art influenced by expressionism, mannerist figure painting in a cubist style with intense colours, and later also painting in a realistic manner. Among his caricature work, the most outstanding are aptly characterized caricatures of cultural figures. Randel received his art education at the Penza and Pallas art schools; he worked as chief artist of the J. Tombi Culture Palace, as caricaturist for the magazine Pikker, and as head of the design workshop of the Tarbekunsti Keskus (Applied Art Centre). /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
c2e9c953c54ead06d098f2ace42f3df5b5ecd293: In 1955 he completed a full-figure statue of the then prima ballerina Helmi Puur. In the following decades, too, Erika Haggi dedicated herself mainly to portraying Estonian cultural figures. From her oeuvre one recalls the Nordic-granite works August Jansen, Heino Eller, Tiit Kuusik, and the granite bust of Georg Ots unveiled in the foyer of Estonia in his jubilee year 1977. She has also portrayed well-known athletes. Alongside portraiture, the sculptor was also interested in the decorative genre. Among her decorative works, one might first mention the dark granite torso "The Sailor's Bride", which adorns the green area in front of the Tallinn Art Hall.
bfc779cb78b79a2413723dd72e4b1e400a06f447: He was born into a joiner's family, received his general education at Nõmme Town 1st Primary School and at Tallinn Town Boys' Gymnasium. He studied art in 1931-1937 at the State School of Applied Art (decorative painting), and in 1938-1941 at the State Higher Art School (painting). In 1941 he was mobilised into the Red Army labour battalion, and in 1944 belonged to the collective of Estonian artists in Yaroslavl. After World War II he studied at the Moscow Academy of Arts. From 1944 he was a teacher at ERKI (TKÜ, EKA), and in 1993 became emeritus professor. While creating his works, E. Okas travelled to the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg in 1958, Italy in 1961, France in 1962, and Japan in 1963.
63312bb15204a8669077ca8c167b3182bd92346a: In 1902, at the initiative of teacher Wieckmann and with the Consistory's permission, the winged altarpiece (B. Notke, 1483), as a Catholic-era object unsuitable for a Lutheran church, was exchanged for a new altar wall. In 1929 the congregation's council had agreed to donate the winged altarpiece to the Museum Society, but in connection with the church's renovation works in 1933, efforts began to reclaim it. The Museum Society did not agree, despite expert assessments that considered the storage place in the Cathedral unsuitable for the altarpiece. Only on 18 December 1942 was the winged altarpiece reconsecrated in its own place. (source: National Register of Cultural Monuments)
893103a4c64dbd626469e18946a74c545b9a0ccb: He studied art in 1923-1924 at the Charlottenburg School of Applied Art in Berlin and at the free academies of F. Colarossi, P. Ranson and Montparnasse in Paris. His teachers were Charles Guerin, Roger Bissiere, Moise Kisling, Andre Lhote, Vassili Šuhhajev. He lived in France, Spain and elsewhere until 1932, and in Greece in 1933-1934. During World War II, in 1941, he was evacuated to the rear of the USSR, where he was the head of the Union of Estonian Artists founded in Yaroslavl. In 1945-1949 he was director of the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art. In 1951 he fell under Soviet repression. In 1983 the Adamson-Eric Museum was founded in Tallinn.
730cf802debd7bd7cf1d6c657cb07de8366db97a: A. M. Hagen was born in Vijciems in Livonia (present-day Latvia) as the son of an estate leaseholder. He studied at the Cēsis district school and in Karl August Senff's studio in Tartu (also serving as his assistant), and travelled in 1820-1823 in Germany and Switzerland. In 1826 he was an art teacher at the provincial gymnasium and in 1826-1832 at the girls' gymnasium, and in 1838-1851 headed the drawing school of Tartu University. Commissioned by the Russian tsar, he made a series of views of the Finnish islands (influenced by C.D. Friedrich), became a member of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts in 1837, and received the title of free artist. He retired in 1851, but from 1855 engaged in photography in Tartu.
8d8cea76160421546517d49d215f8938604578aa: H. E. Hartmann studied art in Tartu under A.M. Hagen, at the Düsseldorf Academy of Arts and in Munich. In 1841-44 he worked in Latvia as a schoolteacher in Bērzaine, and from 1845 in Tartu as a drawing teacher and town treasury bookkeeper. In 1845 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, and from 1860 was conservator of the collections of the Learned Estonian Society. He painted portraits and landscapes; particularly important is his Estica-themed graphic art. Hartmann's woodcuts of Estonians appeared in the publications: Talurahva Postimees, Tartu Postimees, Das Inland (in German), Pasaule (in Latvian), and others.
e113a400ec85146fd29abe20c6d6c99e44e02b2f: EINMANN, Eduard (1913, Kullamaa – 1982, Tallinn). Einmann's oeuvre can be divided into periods. In the 1950s he created naturalistic portrait drawings of workers, peasants, scientists and art people; in the works of the 1960s a stylising line is noticeable; in the 1970s the artist returned to realistic portrait and landscape painting. Einmann studied art at the State School of Applied Art and the State Higher Art School, where he graduated in decoration painting. During World War II he belonged to the collective of Estonian artists in Yaroslavl. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
e6dd24d641810099190b0a8f9101804b355a02a8: 1956	According to Paul Ambur's periodisation, the second period of ex-libris creation began; from 1957 he took part in all major and most thematic Soviet Estonian ex-libris exhibitions. As an ex-libris artist he also became known outside the Soviet Union; his ex-libris were acquired into private collections in the USSR, the Eastern Bloc, Western Europe, America and Australia (among others he made an ex-libris for Gianni Mantero, president of the International Federation of Ex-libris Societies) and were exhibited at international ex-libris exhibitions.
644bc09d83efa942b5a99635916e9b7145148836: Eldar Jakubov (b. 1987 in Tallinn) is a young artist who in 2015 graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a master's degree in installation and sculpture. The artist on his work: "I remove unimportant objects and concentrate my gaze on the human body, its character, mood and, above all, on relations between people. I am interested in society and the processes that keep it working, and the illusions that give us the feeling that we understand this system. Every social problem and illusion, as well as physical ones, can be discussed piece by piece."
94eefb0c425e705bc98f55d1ea0b046acf2bf56c: 2014 – Artist's Day. Vehicle painting. Narva Museum Art Gallery 2019 – Winner of Street Art Battle. Jõhvi Street Art Day. Jaama 6, Jõhvi 2019 – Narva Urban Lab, Narva Art Residency 2019 – Funky Monkey Street Art Festival, Ro-Ro Artclub, Narva 2020 – Exhibition ZE+F, Astri Centre, Narva 2020 – Street art festival Rural Urban Art, Kohtla-Järve 2021 – Street art festival, Rummu Quarry 2021 – Street art festival, Tallinn, Lasnamäe Youth Centre 2022 – Art exhibition "Talve Art Зима", Narva-Jõesuu White Hall.
79e7e6509ef2b59c3215d7d09dc248ce4918393c: Mildeberg worked from 1925 as a photographer and applied artist. In 1941 he was evacuated to the rear of the Soviet Union, to Bashkiria, where he worked as a farm labourer in the Birsk district. In 1942-1945 he was a front-line artist and photographer in the Estonian Rifle Corps of the Red Army. In 1945 he became a member of the Artists' Union. After returning to Tallinn, Mildeberg worked in 1945 as a photo correspondent for Rahva Hääl; in 1945-1946 he was technical editor of the magazine Pikker, and later a freelance artist. He preferred graphic techniques, made caricatures and cartoons, and illustrated books.
4d4a86426dd4d2f7c404ee0c4010a258b861fb8b: In 1912 he enrolled in the drawing courses of the Tallinn Estonian Art Society, which in 1914 were named the Tallinn School of Applied Art; he also studied at Nikolai Triik's studio school until 1917, when he was mobilised into the army. In 1916 he became a member of the Estonian Art Society, and in 1917 a member of the art group Vikerla. In 1918-1921 he worked as a drawing teacher at Paldiski Gymnasium. In 1920 Haavamägi moved to live in Haapsalu, where he worked as a teacher of drawing and art history at the Läänemaa Joint Gymnasium, and thereafter as a freelance artist.
8d6ecee8465b619d99f8207c051ddc543174f1f7: Andrei Jegorov lived in St. Petersburg from 1887 to 1921. Having lost his hearing in childhood, he studied in 1887-1896 at the St. Petersburg school for the deaf-mute. In 1898 he enrolled in the drawing school of the St. Petersburg Society for the Encouragement of the Arts. In 1901-1909 he studied as an auditor at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts under Ilja Repin. He further trained in Munich in Dmitri Kardovski's studio. He then began working as a freelance artist. In 1919-1920 he was an artist in the tsarist army's 1st Cavalry Army of Semyon Budyonny. Having opted for Estonian citizenship, he worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn. During World War II he was evacuated to the rear of the USSR.
320e29ec876a60b55d15b44e41be51c0fc1a7489: Jaan Paavle was an Estonian writer and artist. Paavle published six poetry collections, the first of which, "Vabaarmastus", appeared in 1972. At the age of 35 he enrolled at the Tallinn Art Institute to study ceramics. In the 1990s Paavle became interested in performance art. He taught performance to children at the Tallinn Art School and worked as a guard at the Museum of Applied Art and Design. Jaan Paavle created ceramics, painted, wrote poems, plays, film and theatre criticism, made a few films himself, and appeared in mass scenes in several films.
8213a5d0c04070005eb159d3d8c8b53d16fbf36b: Väino Õun (born 1984) is a freelance artist and graphic designer. He graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts (EKA) in graphic design, from which his interest in typography, lettering and calligraphy also arose. His artistic direction has been influenced by his contact with street art in 1996, from which arose a decade-long relationship and influence on his further work. He began working independently with calligraphy in 2015, guided by a sincere interest in learning the principles of classical letterforms. From this grew a unique and.
510797112ae30d7364371ad73c4da28f2d43ab6b: Linda ROSIN (1904, Lesnoi, St. Petersburg – 1981, Tallinn) was an Estonian sculptor who, alongside sculpture, also practised oil painting. In sculpture she worked mainly in portraiture and figural composition, her portraits having a certain mannerist quality. Rosin received her art education at the State School of Applied Art in the women's handicraft speciality (also obtaining a drawing teacher's qualification), in applied sculpture at the Tallinn School of Applied Art, and in sculpture at the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, where after graduating she began working as a teacher.
d5bd8c84b0c09e6c9906e1cdfb8c8b65772a561e: He was born as the son of the Rakvere county doctor, and was the stepson of Count Rehbinder, the owner of the Udriku manor. He studied at the Tallinn cathedral school and, from 1812 to 1814, medicine at the University of Tartu. In 1814 he set out on a study trip to Berlin, then in 1815-1816 to Vienna, and lived in 1817-1820 in Italy, Germany, Switzerland, England and France. In 1821-1823 he lived in various places in Estonia and Latvia, and in 1823-1830 was an art teacher at the Smolny Institute in St. Petersburg. In 1827 he travelled in Finland. In 1839 he became a candidate for academician at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. From 1842 he lived permanently in St. Petersburg.
6549695eb3ebc01b1531a491e6225301420657f6: Born in Dresden as the son of a craftsman, he studied at the Dresden Academy of Art. The writer August von Kotzebue invited him to Estonia as a home tutor for his children; Walther worked at the Vardi manor and at the Hageri parsonage in the service of Provost Ignatius, who was a relative of Kotzebue. In 1812 Walther settled in Tallinn and in 1815 became the art teacher at the Tallinn Cathedral School. In Tallinn he was the first to work as a lithographer, painted portraits, and made altar retable paintings for churches. In 1835 Walther received the title of free artist from the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts.
8f3d3b91350dfd0fd38808e751a01faea5efdc6c: A prominent Estonian sculptor, monumentalist, painter and ceramicist. Jaan Koort studied at Hugo Treffner's Gymnasium in Tartu and at the drawing courses of the German craftsmen's society, and in 1902-05 at Stieglitz's Art School in Peterburi. He lived in Paris in 1905-15, studying sculpture and painting. He worked in Moscow in 1915-16 and 1920. In 1919 he headed the South Estonian Art Protection Committee. In 1921-22 he was the head of the sculpture workshop of the Tallinn School of Applied Art. In 1927 he stayed in Australia. In 1934-35 he worked in Russia as an artist at the Gzhel ceramics factory.
dde9e554ebf0baae04875657b35c5669e8e2bdae: Elina Vitola (b. 1986) is a young Latvian artist who introduces herself as follows: “I have been happily learning to paint for almost my whole life, and in 2018 I will finish my master's studies at the Art Academy of Latvia. The exhibitions I have had the greatest joy of participating in are, for example, “Children of the New East” at the Tallinn Art Hall and “The Viewing and Reading Room” at Gallery Kogo in Tartu. Recently I have made several abstract paintings, but in the near future I plan to paint pasta.”.
9a65e9139c4f8f2909cd0bf69d9f531c043b7026: Hannah Harkes (1989) is a Scottish artist and printmaker who has lived and worked in Tallinn since 2012. She graduated (BA) from Aberdeen Art Academy in Scotland, in the Fine Arts department with a major in printmaking (2011), and obtained a Master's degree in Death, Religion and Culture at the University of Winchester in England (2019). She has held solo exhibitions in Estonia, Finland, Sweden and Great Britain, and has participated in group exhibitions from Xi'an to New York. In 2020 she had a solo exhibition "As long as we make it".
9117201eed929e80b4b8af7415ac78c96d72965c: He was elected chairman of the Estonian Writers' Union in 1939. In 1940–1941 he worked in the editorial office of the newspaper Kommunist and was editor-in-chief of the publishing house Ilukirjandus ja Kunst; he was also chairman of the organizing committee of the Estonian Soviet Writers' Union. During the Second World War he organized Estonian literary life in the rear of the USSR. In 1944–1946 and 1950–1954 he was chairman of the Estonian Soviet Writers' Union, and in 1950–1958 chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Council of the Estonian SSR and deputy chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Council of the USSR.
7fd931d95a2dfaa75bc3225e7b65140766bf6f8f: Aime Jürjo (1928) has cultivated lyrical, material-influence-oriented free-standing sculpture and portraiture. Her figurative work is characterized by restrained northern mood sensibility, precise modelling, and an emphasis on beautiful, generalized silhouette effect. She has preferred dolomite, marble and wood, but has also used ceramics in her decorative work. She graduated in 1953 from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in the field of sculpture and has been an art educator with long-standing experience.
eac27b3244f8d8e9c6022e4765dbeca1abd6e8df: Worked as a graphic designer, newspaper illustrator and caricaturist, also as a painter. Was an advertising artist in Tallinn in 1924–1932, caricaturist for "Soviet Estonia" in 1941. During World War II he stayed in the Soviet rear in Yaroslavl and participated in the founding of the Estonian Soviet Artists' Union, was its chairman in 1962–1967. Worked in 1943–1946 in the editorial office of the newspaper "Rahva Hääl" and in 1945–1946 in the editorial office of the magazine "Pikker". In 1946–1950 he was a lecturer at the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, 1950–1962.
d3de6790044cb0a48ad0600b264e11b1a725fa78: Painter, graphic artist, ex-libris artist and poster artist Lev Vassiljev was born in Tula, Russia, into an engineer's family. After studying at the Moscow Art School, he moved to Tallinn in 1950, where he studied sculpture at ERKI (EKA), his teachers being Enn Roos, Aleksander Kaasik and Martin Saks. He also worked as a graphic artist (etching and aquatint), and made collages and assemblages. Among his works are pieces with a political tone, while the artist was also attached to mythology and literary themes.
de96dee9c991acfb5d570bdc59702ef8cb61e4cb: Viive Kuks began her art studies in 1966 at the Tallinn Light Industry Technical School, specialising in the artistic design of fabrics, which she completed in 1970. In the same year Kuks began studies at the Tallinn Art University (EKA) in the field of graphic art. Her principal teacher was Evald Okas. In 1976 she received a diploma in printmaking and moved to Võru, working as a freelance artist. Viive Kuks has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1984, and has taken part in exhibitions since 1977.
46099dda1bb0af32a67921fb5383010fe546ddf5: Priit Piirmets was born on 15.03.1948 in Hageri Parish. He came to Rakvere in 1956. He studied at Rakvere 1st 8-year School. He graduated from the Rakvere Correspondence Secondary School. At Rakvere 1st 8-year School, drawing was taught by teacher Gustavson. During his secondary school years he attended the art circle at the House of Culture, led by Ella Rajand. From 1973 he was himself the leader of an art circle. He was a member of the Artists' Union Youth Group. He considers Luulik Kokamägi to be his teacher and role model. In 1974 he moved to live in Tallinn.
a9669ef244028af6457926e32a1ee7d56b5af6b7: Architect, alumnus of the University of Tartu (Faculty of Technology 1935-1936), University of Helsinki architecture 1937-1940, Munich Technical University architecture 1942-1944, Ontario College of Art (Toronto) ceramics 1982-1992, architect in the building department of the Bavarian Ministry of Finance 1945-1948, Sweden 1948, to Canada 1949, lecturer in architecture at the University of Toronto, also private architect 1949-1982, visiting professor at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts 1964, professor emeritus 1982.
5ea6ccf732950555c0c3b7427f7b4afb92795193: Loik is an Estonian artist who cultivated figure composition, nude, interior and view painting, as well as still life; portrait painting also occupies an important place in his oeuvre. He began with a narrative manner of treatment, but later became more generalising and forceful, adding intense colours to his work. Loik received his art education at N. Roth's private studio and at the Pallas art school as a student of Ado Vabbe. From 1950 to 1976 he worked as a teacher at ERKI.
02cdda9c09acb6b8e5f95a364846447553add6d3: Endel Kõks studied philosophy and psychology at the University of Tartu. He began his art studies in 1934 at the Pallas Art School, which he graduated from in 1940 as a student of Ado Vabbe. In 1944 he fled to Germany, where he was one of the organisers of the first exhibition of art by war refugees in 1945. He was the first chairman of the Central Union of Estonian Artists formed in the Geislingen refugee camp. In 1950 Kõks moved to Sweden and settled in Örebro.
df0c2002ca8394e64a5374491e81e840e529f2fc: In 1924 he joined the Eesti Kunstnikkude Rühm (Estonian Artists' Group) and became its spiritual leader; in 1928 he edited the group's programmatic almanac Uue Kunsti Raamat, in 1926–1927 the Estonian Art yearbook, and in 1928–1929 the youth magazine Taie. He exhibited at EKKKY and RaKÜ exhibitions. He published art criticism in newspapers and in the journals Olion, Looming and Kunst ja Kirjandus. He worked as a teacher in Tallinn schools until 1945 (J. Westholm Gymnasium and others), after which he was a freelance artist.
43c55f2b3b5d51a47a5c1d2665b322a68b371da2: 1930–1940 he worked as a primary school teacher in Aluvere and Tartu. In 1936 he furthered his studies in Finland, in 1938 in Sweden, in 1940 in Italy. 1940–1941 he was director of the Riiklik Kunstimuuseum. In 1941 he was arrested by the NKVD and deported to Siberia, to Krasnoyarsk Krai. He was in a prison camp from 1941–1951, and in exile settlement from 1951–1956. 1956–1965 he was a researcher at the State Institute of Design and Scientific Research "Eesti Ehitusmälestised", 1965–1982 chief specialist, 1982–1990 consultant.
1fe37163ef54f79df971d746459eacf46a358307: Voldemar HAAS (1898, Tori – 1982, Tallinn) was an Estonian theatre artist and teacher, who enriched Estonian stage design with many technical innovations (cyclorama, projection and cloud apparatuses). In the 1920s he was a prolific painter of landscapes, and in the 1970s of townscapes. Haas received his art education under Ado Vabbe and Konrad Mägi at the Pallas Art School and studied drawing pedagogy at the University of Tartu. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
a09f0ad138cf7450b96b42e09d8691e59a29127d: Born in Koeru, Järva County; lived in Narva 1907-1915, in Omsk, Russia, 1915-1921. Returned to Estonia in 1921, studied at Pallas in Tartu 1923-1935. Graduated as a graphic artist. Married to Kaarel Liimand 1937-1941. Study trip to Paris in 1937. In 1940, member of the organising committee of the artists' union, a "June communist". Taught at the K. Mägi Art School in Tartu 1940-1941. Was in the rear of the Soviet Union 1941-1944, in Yaroslavl in 1942. Freelance artist in Tallinn from 1946.
420e77e579c52fea97a1dd995fe0a5c6a1269ff7: Interior view of Pärnu St. Nicholas' Church towards the west along the nave. A wall with low arcade arches separating the central nave from the southern side aisle opens up, with pilasters and windows above. At the end of the nave, the organ gallery with the organ, and the church's western entrance below it. On the right, the pulpit with a canopy. In the church, rows of pews with closed doors. Light falls from the windows of the southern aisle on the left; the church is generally dim. The sides of the triumphal arch frame the view on both sides.
c6440e779dda28f0e0dfad042c53dee1a78f63a4: From 1934 Herman Talvik began exhibiting at Finnish and Estonian art exhibitions; during World War II he worked as a teacher (mainly at Tallinna Reaalkool), in 1944 he fled to Sweden, where he was a freelance artist. Solo exhibitions of this outstanding Estonian émigré artist in Estonia took place in 1971 and 1981 at the Kadriorg Palace of the Art Museum of Estonia, in 1991 at the Tartu Art Museum, in 2006-2007 at the Adamson-Eric Museum of the Art Museum of Estonia, and in 2016 at the Hiiumaa Museum.
d6df59bc57cdc80541cb86ca0a1b375b068aeab7: Applied art. He has created large-scale bindings and objects with forceful composition and colour treatment in his own invented hand-sewing and paper-relief technique, using papier-mâché (bindings "Armunud naise päevik" 1987, "Kaotatud paradiis" 1991, "Kurb kirjutaja" 1999, object "Neeger" 1995), illustrated books (E. Niidu's "Onu ööbiku ööpäev" 1998). He has published the poetry collection "Tõsimäng" and articles on applied art.
009d920836f04a62b018b077ae5bb16a53290a29: Born in Tallinn in 1945. He received his art education at the Estonian State Art Institute, graduating in painting in 1969. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1979. Has been exhibiting since 1970. Lecturer at the Estonian Academy of Arts since 1992. Member of the Board of the Estonian Union of Painters since 1997. Member of the Estonian Watercolourists' Association 2002. Chairman of the Estonian Union of Painters in 2006.
af7861c4b2ce6d5924a561835791a35f51c2c12d: Silver Vahtre (b. 1953 in Tartu) is a graphic artist, designer and theatre artist. Vahtre graduated in 1977 in the design speciality from the Estonian State Art Institute and has since worked in various positions, including as the city artist of Tartu (1991-94). Vahtre has participated in about 30 solo and group exhibitions in Estonia and Finland. Silver Vahtre is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association, the Union of Stage Designers, the Union of Design Graphic Artists and the Tartu Artists' Union.
d619d43ef91b208b6450fa1208dec0548ec56a97: Sculptor. He has created monumental works, portraits and figural compositions on mythological themes. He has achieved expressiveness and plastic richness of expression by combining various classical materials (plaster, bronze, stone, wood) with one another or by using them separately or together with ready-made materials. Characteristic of him is the interweaving of the ironic and the grotesque with the serious. Since the 1990s he has created installations and conceptual projects.
fb622d10c370a5cc8787f582d92ae311b460f1c4: Physician, studied at Albert Reimann's art school in Berlin in 1922, graduate of the University of Tartu (medicine 1923-1929), took courses (sculpture) at the art school "Pallas", private doctor in Tallinn in the 1930s, evacuated to Tatarstan in 1941, physician in the Red Army from 1943, physician at the therapy department of Tallinn's Second United Hospital from 1945, head, deputy chief physician for outpatient care, physician of the "Estonia" theatre, lecturer at the art institute in Tallinn.
98e62af516e7033522eb5834b939978fdef82f9f: Graduated from the Viljandi County Boys' Gymnasium in 1937 and from the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Tartu in 1946. 1946–1951 assistant at the Department of General Surgery of the University of Tartu, 1951–1952 assistant at the Department of Hospital Surgery, 1952–1960 head of the surgery department of Jõhvi Hospital, 1960–1962 surgeon at the Viljandi District Central Hospital, 1962–1968 head of the surgery department, 1968–1978 deputy chief physician for treatment, 1978–1994 surgeon at the hospital and polyclinic.
cd4a4b0f521b28593c4399eb20973d9107fabe57: Graduated from Valga Joint Gymnasium in 1935 and from the J. Koort State School of Applied Art in 1941. Worked in Tallinn during World War II as a design artist in V. Tomassov's and, from 1965-78, in Ars's decoration studio. Member of the EKL from 1939, of the KL from 1946. Designed exhibitions and major events (including the 12th General Song Festival in 1947 and, in the 1950s, Tallinn song days and processions). Practised portrait and decorative painting and posters.
bdcf6af181b38a1e55398ea1b17b819ba392dfc8: August Pulst was involved in the founding and management of the Art Museum of Estonia, the Estonian Theatre and Music Museum, the Tori Museum, and the Estonian Open Air Museum. In 1915, A. Pulst, Ants Laikmaa, Kristjan Raud, Mihkel Aitsam and Peeter Parikas founded the Tallinn branch of the Estonian National Museum, which was transformed in 1919 into the Tallinn Estonian Museum, from which the present-day Foundation Art Museum of Estonia has grown.
16ed5c491cdc7a6968fa8ebf15145770a875ef39: Born 05.02.1851, Tartu; died 03.03.1912. Education: received basic knowledge of painting in Tartu from K. von Kügelgen and of lithography in C. A. Shulz's workshop. Continued studies 1872–77 at the Düsseldorf Academy of Art, including in 1874 with E. von Gebhardt and from 1875 with E. Dücker. Made study trips to Westphalia, the upper reaches of the Rhine and the North Sea islands. Studied for a short time in Paris.
d7f34ae516dbfbe82143a44a3aaeff749d818332: Marju Bormeister (b. 1945 in Tallinn) graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute as a painter in 1985. As a descendant of artists, she has lived half her life at the Tallinn Art Hall, coming early into the turpentine-scented world of paints. Bormeister especially likes to paint nature and the various surface structures found in it. As a technique, Bormeister especially enjoys monotype.
1f22432f1a0c637f3d0dd11624e75639aa08c3d8: Born in Tallinn, studied ceramics at the Tallinn Institute of Applied Art in 1947-49 and graphic art at ERKI in 1949-53.
